default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vi: My younger brother is very healthy.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of the sentence, meaning that it is about the younger brother.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object described as strong and healthy.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: 強い is an adjective ending in い and functions as the predicate; です is added at the end to make the sentence polite.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q1.kobun.why: The pattern NはNがAい describes a feature of a body part or an aspect related to the topic. からだが is the part being described, so use が instead of を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 元気です, it means being healthy, energetic, or cheerful in general, without focusing on the body's strength.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を before an adjective, but body features usually go with が.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that さとうさん is the person being commented on.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the part being described as beautiful.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: きれいです is an adjective predicate ending in な, describing 字.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q10.kobun.why: さとうさんは makes the person being discussed the topic, while 字が is the subject of the feature きれい. This expression is more natural than using を with きれい.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 上手です, it means “being good at writing,” so it evaluates the skill rather than only the beauty of the handwriting.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q10.kobun.tip: きれい is an adjective ending in な, so use きれいです and do not add い at the end.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q11.kobun.vi: Because there is a swimming pool nearby, it is very convenient.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the location where プール exists.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing that exists in the location pattern に Nがあります.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the reason to the result and makes the explanation of the cause softer.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: 便利です is the result stated after the reason あるので.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q11.kobun.why: ちかくにプールがある states that something exists as the reason. ので connects this reason to the conclusion 便利です; because 便利 is an adjective ending in な, before です it keeps the form 便利.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the meaning of the reason is almost the same, but the expression is more direct and subjective.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: 便利な is used only when modifying a noun, such as 便利な場所, and is not used independently before です.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q11.kobun.tip: Before ので, adjectives ending in な and nouns need な: 便利なので, 学生なので.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q12.kobun.vi: When I was young, I had a habit of writing a diary.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 子ども with とき to identify the time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: とき indicates the time when the habit occurred and comes at the beginning of the sentence as a time adverbial.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the thing being written.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: 書く in the dictionary form comes before しゅうかん to modify the habit.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the habit that exists in the pattern しゅうかんがありました.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: ありました is the polite past form of あります and functions as the main predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q12.kobun.why: 子どものとき places the time setting at the beginning of the sentence. The clause 日記を書く comes before しゅうかん to modify “habit,” and then しゅうかんがありました expresses the existence of the habit.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this pattern, it means “have written a diary before,” referring only to experience, not to a habit.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q12.kobun.tip: When a verb comes before a noun to modify it, use the plain form such as 書く, not 書きます.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q13.kobun.vi: In the evening, I went to the supermarket and bought vegetables and meat to bring home.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q13.kobun.sk: Time に ＋ N に ＋ Vて ＋ NとNを ＋ Vてくる
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: This part only indicates the time when the action took place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the destination of the verb 行く.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the action of going with the following action of buying.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle と connects やさい with the noun that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the whole phrase “vegetables and meat” as the object of 買う.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: The form 買ってきました expresses buying something and then bringing it home.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q13.kobun.why: The part indicating the time comes at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the destination of 行く. The form て connects the two actions, while 買ってくる shows that the purchase was made and the items were brought home.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If used here, it means going in order to buy something, without emphasizing that it was bought and brought home.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget that に in スーパーに indicates the destination, not the object of the buying action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective comes before a noun to modify パソコン.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the thing that the speaker wants to have.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: ほしい is an い adjective that expresses a desire for an object.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q14.kobun.why: The adjective 軽い comes directly before パソコン to describe the computer. With ほしい, the desired object usually goes with が.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the person who wants something is usually someone else, and the tone is more observational.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern makes the sentence softer and shows that it is the speaker's thought or desire.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を before ほしい because of the usual pattern for the verb “want,” but the basic pattern uses が.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q14.kobun.cn: Aい ＋ N が ＋ ほしいです
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q15.kobun.vi: Please show me how to make this dish.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative この modifies the noun 料理.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects 料理 with つくりかた, creating the meaning “how to make the dish.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks つくりかた as the content for which instructions are requested.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: The form おしえてください is used to politely ask the listener to do something.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q15.kobun.why: この料理 identifies the dish being discussed, while の turns 料理 into a modifier for つくりかた. The phrase つくりかたを is the object of the request おしえてください.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced here, the sentence changes from a request for instructions to a question about whether the listener knows how to make it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may rigidly translate の as “of”; here, it connects nouns to form the phrase “how to make the dish.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q15.tokens.3.m: how to make; how to cook
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q2.kobun.sk: N には ＋ N が ＋ Number of people ＋ います
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: に only points to the person who has something or the range of existence, while は makes that person the topic.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person who exists in a possessive relationship with わたし.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 一人 is the number of people, while います is the existence verb used for people.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q2.kobun.why: The structure NにはNがいます expresses that a person exists or belongs to N. The quantity 一人 comes before います to show how many people there are.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If わたしの兄 is used, it only creates the noun phrase “my older brother”; by itself, it does not express the meaning “I have an older brother”.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q2.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically translate に as “at” or “in”; in this pattern, に can point to the person who possesses something.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q3.kobun.vi: Last night, I was playing a game alone.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects a time noun with 夜, creating the phrase “last night”.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: は states the time being discussed and marks the time topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: で shows the state or manner in which an action is performed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the game as the object of the action していました.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: していました is the past progressive form. It describes an action that was in progress at a time in the past.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q3.kobun.why: きのうの夜は puts the time at the beginning of the sentence, then 一人で states the manner. ゲームを is the object, while していました shows that the playing was continuing last night.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with しました, it only says that I played and does not emphasize that the action was in progress.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q3.kobun.tip: で in 一人で does not indicate only a location. It indicates the state or manner “alone”.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vi: On Sunday, I went to the beach with a friend.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks Sunday as the time being stated as the topic.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: と indicates a person who participates in or accompanies someone during an action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the destination of the verb 行きました.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きました is the polite past form of 行く and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q4.kobun.why: The time is placed at the beginning of the sentence and marked with は. 友だちと shows who went along, while うみに indicates the destination, so it goes with に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If うみで is used, the beach is the place where an action happens, not the destination of going.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q4.kobun.tip: With 行く, a destination usually goes with に or へ, not で.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vi: My friend appeared on a famous television program.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who performs the action of appearing on the program.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 有名 is a な adjective, so it needs な when placed before a noun to modify the program.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place or medium where the friend appears.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 出ました is the polite past form of 出る and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q5.kobun.why: 有名な comes before テレビばんぐみ to modify the noun. With 出る, に indicates the place or program where the subject appears.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 有名の, it is incorrect because the adjective な needs な when it directly modifies a noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q5.kobun.tip: Do not omit な after the adjective な when it comes directly before a noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vi: My older brother got married last year.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q6.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time ＋ Vました
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the older brother is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: 去年 is a time word. It can stand directly before a verb without a particle.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: けっこんしました is the predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q6.kobun.why: あには identifies the person being discussed, 去年 adds the time, and the past verb comes at the end of the sentence. Time words such as 去年 usually do not need に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is added, the sentence can still appear in some contexts, but natural speech usually omits に with 去年.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q6.kobun.tip: Not every time word needs に; 去年 usually comes directly before the verb.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vi: I will give my son a gift that he likes.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects むすこ with the noun after it to modify the object that is liked.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: すきな modifies the noun 物, creating the phrase “favorite item”.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the item being given as a gift.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q7.kobun.why: The phrase むすこのすきな comes before 物 to limit which item is being given. 物を is the direct object of プレゼントします.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ほしい, the meaning is “the item my son wants,” emphasizing his desire rather than his preference.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place a modifying phrase after the noun, but Japanese places the whole phrase むすこのすきな before 物.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that あに is the person being discussed in the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: In the pattern 好きだ, が marks the object of liking.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: すきです is an adjective predicate ending in な. It expresses a preference.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q8.kobun.why: The person who has the preference is stated with は, while the preferred object goes with が in the pattern Nは Nが好きです. Therefore, 黒が is not an object that uses を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 黒いです is used, it means “black” and describes the color of an object. It does not express liking black.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after 好き, but the basic pattern is Nは Nが好きです.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 子ども with 教育 to create the phrase “children’s education”.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: について indicates the topic or object being discussed, which here is 教育.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 話しました is a verb in the polite past form and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q9.kobun.why: 子どもの modifies 教育, while 教育について states the topic of the action 話しました. The comma after について separates the topic part from the main clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with に関して, the meaning is still “about,” but the expression is more formal and more common in writing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If についての is used, the phrase must come before another noun, such as 教育についての話.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t1-q9.kobun.tip: Do not use について directly as a verb; connect the noun with について to state the topic.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q1.kobun.vi: Please move this luggage to the next room.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify luggage near the speaker or listener.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object being moved.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: となりの modifies へや, forming the phrase “the next room.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に indicates the destination of the luggage.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてください is used to politely ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q1.kobun.why: The luggage is the object affected, so it takes を, while the next room is the destination, so it takes に. The form Vてください is placed at the end to make a request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vなさい, the speech sounds more like a strong command.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vてもらえませんか is used, the request sounds softer and more humble.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で for “move to the room,” but the destination of movement takes に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q10.kobun.vi: When you take time off work, please contact the company.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks しごと as the object of taking time off in the phrase しごとを休む.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: 休むとき indicates a time or situation; は makes that situation the topic.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the recipient of the contact.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: ください combines with the て verb form to make a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q10.kobun.why: 休むときは places the condition or time at the beginning of the sentence. Then, 会社に indicates the place receiving the contact, while れんらくしてください expresses the required action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If ときは is replaced with 場合は, the sentence sounds more formal and hypothetical, like “in the case of taking time off.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If に is replaced with へ, the focus shifts toward contacting the company, but in this sentence に is more natural for the recipient of the contact.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for しごとを休む; here, を is what marks the action or object of 休む.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q10.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 ＋ とき(は); Nに ＋ れんらくする; Vて ＋ ください
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q11.kobun.vi: Excuse me, may I sit here?
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: This is an opening phrase used to get someone's attention or make a question more polite.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where a person or object is placed in a sitting position.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: すわって is the て form. It combines with もかまいません to ask whether an action is allowed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: てもかまいませんか is a permission-seeking pattern meaning “is it okay to do …?”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q11.kobun.why: The place ここに comes before the action すわる. The ても form combines with かまいませんか to turn the action into a request for permission.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vてもいいですか is used, the meaning is almost the same, but the expression is more common and direct.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vてはいけませんか is used, the question has the meaning “is it not allowed to do …?”, emphasizing prohibition.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget the て form before も; do not say すわるもかまいませんか.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q11.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ もかまいませんか
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q12.kobun.vi: A: Do you want to go shopping together on Saturday? B: I have something to do on Saturday, so it may be difficult…
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The symbol A「 opens A's direct speech.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: どようび states the time of the invitation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: いっしょに modifies the action of going shopping.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the purpose of going in the pattern Nに行く.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: 行きませんか is a polite way to invite someone, meaning “shall we go … together?”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: The line break and B「 open B's direct reply.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.6.n: は makes Saturday the topic and creates a contrast with other times.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.7.n: が marks ようじ as the thing that exists in the pattern ようじがある.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.8.n: ので connects the reason to the refusal or delay of the invitation that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.9.n: ちょっと…… leaves the answer unfinished to refuse indirectly without saying so directly.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q12.kobun.why: A states the time, purpose, and invitation using 行きませんか. B uses は to make Saturday the specific topic, gives the reason with ようじがあるので, and ends unfinished to refuse politely.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason sounds more direct and subjective.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If 行きましょうか is used, the sentence focuses more on suggesting that they go together or confirming a plan than on making a soft invitation with a negative form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate ちょっと as “a little,” but at the end of a sentence it is often a softened refusal.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q12.kobun.cn: Vます形 ＋ ませんか; V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q13.kobun.vi: The soccer match starts at 1 p.m.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting time of the match.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects サッカー with the following noun and shows what kind of match it is.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks しあい as the subject that undergoes the state of starting.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: はじまります is the main predicate and describes an event that is starting or will start, depending on the context.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q13.kobun.why: The time phrase comes first to state the starting point. サッカーの modifies しあい, while しあいが はじまります form the subject and predicate structure.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with に, the sentence only states when the match starts and does not emphasize the period counted from that point.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If 始めます is used with を, the subject actively starts the match; はじまります describes the match starting by itself.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse はじまります and はじめます: the first means that something starts by itself, while the second requires someone to perform the action and usually goes with を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q14.kobun.vi: I do not know the rules of this game very well.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q14.kobun.sk: N の ＋ N を ＋ adverb ＋ Vません
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: このゲームの modifies ルール and shows a possessive or belonging relationship.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object that is known or not known.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: よく modifies しりません and shows the degree of knowing clearly.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q14.kobun.why: The phrase このゲームの comes before ルール to identify which game's rules they are. ルールを is the object of しりません, while よく adds the degree of knowledge.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used here, the sentence emphasizes “not knowing much” and usually appears with a negative form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place を after the subject instead of placing を immediately after the verb's object.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q15.kobun.vi: Let's compete to see who can do it best.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q15.kobun.sk: 疑問 from が ＋ いちばん ＋ Vく ＋ Vるか ＋ Vましょう
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person being identified in an indirect question clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: いちばん modifies うまく and expresses the highest degree.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: うまく is the adverbial form of うまい and modifies できる.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: か closes an indirect question clause and makes its content the subject of the competition.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: しましょう is the inviting form of します, used to suggest doing something together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q15.kobun.why: The clause だれがいちばんうまくできるか states what the competition is about, and then きょうそうしましょう is the main invitation. うまく comes before できる because it describes how the action is carried out.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If the final part is replaced with 分かりません, the sentence means “I do not know who…,” so it is no longer an invitation to compete.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand か here as a direct question, but it is placed inside the sentence to form an indirect question clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q16.kobun.vi: If we win the next match, let's celebrate together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the setting or event in which the action of winning takes place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: たら connects a hypothetical condition with the proposed action in the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the people who take part in carrying out the action together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: しましょう expresses an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q16.kobun.why: The conditional clause こんどのしあいでかったら is placed first to state the condition for the suggestion. みんなで shows that the celebration is done together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If なら is used, the sentence has a nuance based on information or an assumption stated earlier.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If と is used, the sentence can mean that whenever this condition occurs, the result naturally follows, so it is less suitable for an invitation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget で in みんなで, making the meaning “together” unclear.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q17.kobun.vi: Because of the major earthquake, the bookcase fell over, and I was injured.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the cause that made the bookcase fall over.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of the falling action in the previous clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the bookcase falling over with the result that happened afterward.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the noun けが in the fixed expression けがをする.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: てしまいました shows that an event has been completed, often with a feeling of regret or an unwanted result.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q17.kobun.why: The cause phrase comes first, followed by the subject ほんだなが and the verb たおれて, which lead to the result. けがをしてしまいました describes an unwanted result that has occurred.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is replaced here, the sentence only describes a state or an ongoing event, without emphasizing that the regrettable event has ended.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate で as “at,” but in this sentence で indicates the cause: the earthquake.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q17.kobun.cn: Vて + しまう／しまいます／しまいました
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q18.kobun.vi: I planted many flowers in the garden.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the flowers are planted.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: たくさん modifies 花 and shows that the quantity is large.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the flowers as the object being planted.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: ました is the polite past form and shows that the action has been completed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q18.kobun.why: The place phrase に comes before the object 花を and the main verb. たくさん comes before 花 to describe the quantity.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If が咲く is used, the sentence says that flowers bloomed by themselves in the garden, not that someone planted them.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse にわに with “into the garden,” but here に indicates the place where the planting is done.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q19.kobun.vi: Because this pond is deep, please do not play around here.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this pond the topic being described.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason with the request in the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where playing is not allowed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: ないでください creates a polite request meaning “please do not do it.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q19.kobun.why: The sentence begins with the topic and the reason, then states the place to avoid and gives a negative request. ので makes the prohibition sound softer and gives it a clear reason.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason sounds more direct and conversational.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If ください is omitted, the sentence still means “do not play,” but it becomes shorter and less polite.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use ないでください as if it only negated the verb, but the whole pattern is a polite request meaning “please do not do it.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q2.kobun.vi: If you put the bag at the entrance, it will get in the way.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the bag is put.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object affected by おく.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects a natural condition, meaning that if you put it there, the following result will occur.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the state or result that something becomes.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: なります is the predicate and describes the change into a state that causes trouble.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q2.kobun.why: The place and the object come before the verb おく to state the action of putting down the bag. と connects this action with the natural result, じゃまになります.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is replaced with たら, the sentence has a more hypothetical or specific-time condition.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: Using じゃまでなります is wrong because the resulting state with なる must be connected with に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で before なる because they are used to translating it as becoming in a place, but the correct pattern is Nに なる.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q20.kobun.vi: It has gradually become a little cold, so let's turn on the heater.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects a reason clause with the action that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object that is turned on.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: ましょう expresses an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q20.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first, followed by the proposed action. を marks the heater as the object being turned on.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still gives a reason, but the expression sounds more direct and subjective.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistakenly use に instead of を when talking about turning a device on or off.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q21.kobun.vi: If there is a word I do not understand, I will look it up in the dictionary.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: わからない comes before a noun and modifies the word that is not known.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the word as something that exists in the hypothetical situation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: たら creates a hypothetical condition and sets the starting point for looking it up.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the tool or means used for looking something up.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: This is the main predicate and states the action that will be done when the condition occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q21.kobun.why: The condition is placed at the beginning with たら, followed by the means and the related action. The clause わからないことば modifies the noun ことば.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: Using と emphasizes a natural or certain result that happens whenever there is a word that is not understood.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: Using なら gives the nuance of taking that information as the topic for giving advice.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that the modified noun must come after the clause, as in わからないことば.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q21.tokens.0.m: do not understand, do not know
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q21.kobun.cn: Vた・Aかった・Nだった・Aなだった + ら
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q3.kobun.vi: Because it is broken, please do not touch this door.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: ので connects the reason to the reminder in the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the object touched by さわる.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ないでください is used to ask the listener not to perform an action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q3.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first with ので, followed by the object that the listener is asked not to touch. さわる goes with the particle に to indicate the object touched.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If ください is omitted, the sentence becomes only a direct prohibition or request, so it sounds less gentle.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes the rule that touching is not allowed. It sounds more formal and more strongly prohibitive.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q3.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily say さわらないください, but で must be included in the Vないでください pattern.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q3.kobun.cn: Vない形 + でください; Vている + ので
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q4.kobun.vi: I received a souvenir from Mr. Tanaka.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person giving something or the source from which something is received in the pattern もらう.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun りょこう with おみやげ to describe the souvenir.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the item that the speaker received.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: もらいました is the predicate and describes the speaker receiving a gift.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q4.kobun.why: The giver goes with に, the item received goes with を, and の connects りょこう with おみやげ to identify the type of gift. The verb もらう takes the recipient as the implied subject of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with あげました, the meaning changes to the speaker having given a gift to someone else.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If くれました is used, another person is the subject and gives something to the speaker or the speaker’s side.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q4.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily confuse に and を, but with もらう, the giver uses に and the item received uses を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q5.kobun.vi: Because the train was delayed by snow, I ended up being late.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the reason why the train was delayed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject experiencing the state おくれる.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the event of the train being delayed with the result of the speaker being late.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: てしまいました describes a completed event and often carries a sense of regret.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q5.kobun.cn: N で indicates the reason; Vて + しまう
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q5.kobun.why: ゆきで states the reason, and 電車が is the subject of the delayed state. The form て connects the reason directly to the result of the speaker being late.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used, the cause-and-effect relationship is stated as a clearer clause instead of using a cause noun with で.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If しまいました is omitted, the sentence only says that the speaker was late, without a sense of regret or an unintended result.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q5.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily understand で here as a place, but ゆきで uses で to indicate a cause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q6.kobun.vi: While I was singing, I was told that I was being noisy.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the verb うたう.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects the verb うたう with いる to form a state that is in progress.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: たら connects the situation of singing with the event that happens afterward.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: と marks the content of the quoted comment.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: されました is a polite passive form showing that the speaker was affected by another person.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q6.kobun.cn: Vている + たら; quoted sentence + と + V受身
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q6.kobun.why: うたっていたら creates the background of an action in progress, and then the passive sentence describes another person’s reaction. と connects the exact quoted content of the warning with ちゅういされました.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If たら is replaced with と, the sentence emphasizes a result that usually happens immediately while singing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If ので is used, singing becomes the cause being explained, without the situational sense of an event arising as in たら.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q6.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily translate ている as only “be doing,” but in うたっていたら it also creates the background for the following event.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q7.kobun.vi: Have you found the key that was lost yesterday yet?
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: きのう indicates when the action of losing the key occurred.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause なくした comes before かぎ to describe which key.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the lost key the topic being asked about.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: もう indicates that the expected event has happened by the present time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: か at the end turns the sentence into a polite question about the result.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q7.kobun.why: The clause きのうなくした comes before かぎ to identify which key. は states the topic, while もう combines with the final question to ask whether finding it has been completed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If なくなった is used, it means that the key disappeared or is no longer there, without emphasizing who lost it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If みつけましたか is used, the question asks whether the listener found it; みつかりましたか focuses on whether the key has been found.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q7.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily confuse みつける and みつかる: one means finding an object, while the other means that the object is found.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q8.kobun.vi: I slipped on the stairs and hit my head.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where an action or event occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: すべて usually means “entirely”; in this sentence, this spelling does not form a natural connecting pattern with the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the body part affected by the verb うつ.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: うちました is the polite past form of うつ and describes an action that happened.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q8.kobun.why: A place phrase comes before the verb to state where the event occurs. あたまを is the object affected, while うちました comes at the end to finish the sentence in the polite past tense.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If すべって is used, it means “slipped and then...,” which connects naturally to hitting one’s head.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If ころんで is used, the meaning changes to “fell and then...,” and it does not necessarily mean that the person slipped.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q8.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily confuse で, which indicates where an action occurs, with に, which indicates where something exists or where it is headed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q9.kobun.vi: This restaurant is delicious, so you should definitely come here.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes このレストラン the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason clause to the suggestion in the following clause; おいしいです is the adjective い in its polite form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: ぜひ modifies the invitation and emphasizes the speaker’s wish for the listener to do it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 行って is the て form of 行く and combines with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: ください expresses a favor or request; ね makes the tone softer and more friendly.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q9.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first with から, followed by the suggestion. ぜひ comes before 行ってください to emphasize how strongly the speaker wants the listener to go.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with ので, the reason sounds softer and more objective, and less direct.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If 行ってください is replaced with 行きましょう, the sentence becomes an invitation to go together instead of a request for the listener to go.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q9.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily place から after the whole sentence; in Japanese, から attaches immediately after the clause stating the reason.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t10-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな/Nな・Nの + から; Vて + ください
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q1.kobun.vi: The kanji in the newspaper are difficult, so I can hardly read them.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun 新聞 with the noun かんじ to show a modifying relationship.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the kanji in the newspaper the topic of the comment.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The form くて of the adjective ending in い connects this feature with the result that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: ほとんど modifies the degree of being unable to read.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: 読めません is the negative potential form and expresses the inability to read.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q1.kobun.why: The phrase の identifies the type of kanji, は makes that phrase the topic, and くて connects the reason with the result. ほとんど comes before the predicate to limit the degree.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used instead of くて, the two clauses are connected in contrast or in parallel, depending on the context, so the cause-and-effect relationship here sounds less natural.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: あまり + negation also means “not much,” but it is weaker than ほとんど and does not necessarily mean that the speaker can hardly read at all.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate くて mechanically as "and", but in this sentence it connects a cause with a result.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q10.kobun.vi: Check once more for mistakes before submitting it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: まちがって is the form て, joined with いない to express “not be wrong”.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: か turns the preceding clause into the thing to be checked.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: てから shows that the checking must be completed before submitting.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: The form て connects the verb 出す with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: ください comes after the form て to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q10.kobun.why: The clause with か states what must be confirmed. Then, てから puts checking first and submitting second. ください turns the final action into a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing てから with たあとで still expresses “after”, but てから clearly stresses that the later action can happen only after the earlier action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand てから as two simultaneous actions; this pattern requires the first action to finish before the second begins.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q10.kobun.cn: Vて + から; Vて + ください
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q11.kobun.vi: Because I carry heavy luggage every day, my arms have become stronger and thicker.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q11.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Aい ＋ N を ＋ Vている ＋ N が ＋ Aいく ＋ なる
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: 毎日 indicates the time or frequency of an action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: おもい modifies the noun にもつ that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the thing being carried.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: はこんで is the て form, connecting the carrying action with the continuing state that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: いて creates the structure はこんでいて, expressing a continuing state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the body part that undergoes a change.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.6.n: ふとく is the conjunctive form of the adjective い, connecting with なりました.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.7.n: なりました expresses a change that has occurred.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q11.kobun.why: The phrase おもい にもつを states what heavy thing is carried, and then はこんでいて expresses a continuing action. The pattern Aいくなる is used to say that one quality changes into a new state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with てから, the sentence emphasizes that the arms changed after carrying, without emphasizing a continuing state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may forget to change the adjective い into the form く before なる.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q12.kobun.vi: My daughter is at least 5 centimeters taller than me.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q12.kobun.sk: N より ＋ N のほうが ＋ Quantity ＋ N が ＋ Aいです
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: より marks the object used as the comparison standard.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects むすめ with ほう, creating the side chosen in the comparison.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: ほうが marks the side with the higher level in the comparison.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: いじょう indicates a difference of at least 5 centimeters.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the quality judged to be high.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: 高い is the adjective predicate describing height.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q12.kobun.why: より gives the comparison standard, while のほうが marks the more prominent side. せが高い is natural because height is expressed with the noun せ and the adjective 高い.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If ほど〜ない is used, the sentence becomes a negative comparison, meaning that one side is not equal to the other.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q12.kobun.tip: Do not use に instead of より when stating the comparison standard.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q13.kobun.vi: I went to visit a friend who was in the hospital.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The clause comes before the noun 友だち and modifies the friend.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the friend with おみまい, indicating the act of visiting that person.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: に in おみまいに行く indicates the purpose of going.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きました is the main verb, expressing that someone went.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q13.kobun.why: The clause にゅういんしている comes before 友だち, so it means which friend. The phrase おみまいに行きました uses に to indicate the purpose of going.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: This expression uses を to directly mark the person being visited, while おみまいに emphasizes the purpose of the trip.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q13.kobun.tip: When a clause modifies a noun in Japanese, do not add a relative pronoun such as “that” as in English.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q14.kobun.vi: I said “get well soon” to a friend who had a cold.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q14.kobun.sk: N を ＋ Vた ＋ N に ＋ 「Quoted speech」と ＋ Vました
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the illness or condition that the person has.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: ひいた comes before 友だち and modifies the friend who has a cold.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: と marks the content of the quoted speech.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: 言いました is the main verb showing the act of speaking.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q14.kobun.why: ひいた comes before 友だち to identify which friend. In a quotation structure, the spoken content comes before と, followed by 言いました.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: This is the complete quotation pattern; if と is omitted, the spoken words cannot connect directly to 言いました.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may use を for the listener, but the listener in a “say to someone” structure uses に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は states who is being discussed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the area in which the ability うまい is applied.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: うまい functions as the predicate and evaluates singing ability.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: です makes the statement more polite.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q15.kobun.why: は makes the person being evaluated the topic, while が marks the ability area as うた. うまい directly functions as the predicate to say that someone is good at an activity.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: 上手です has a more polite and neutral tone than うまい, while うまい is usually more casual.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q15.kobun.tip: Do not understand が here as the only subject of the whole sentence; it marks the object of the ability or evaluation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q15.tokens.1.m: Mr., Ms., or a polite title
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q16.kobun.vi: I was very embarrassed because the teacher scolded me in front of everyone.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects みんな with 前 to create the phrase “in front of everyone”.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates where the scolding happened.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the person who performs the scolding action in a passive sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: しかられて is the て form of the passive, connecting being scolded with the feeling that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: とても modifies the adjective はずかしかった.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: はずかしかった is the past form of the adjective い and describes an emotion that occurred in the past.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q16.kobun.ch.6.n: です ends the sentence in a polite way.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q16.kobun.why: 前で sets the context, 先生にしかられて states the cause or an earlier event. Then はずかしかったです is the speaker's emotional result.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use ので, the cause-and-effect relationship is clearer, while て connects events more naturally and briefly.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q16.kobun.tip: In a passive sentence, the person who performs the action usually goes with に, not を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: This word modifies the noun としょかん.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は marks the library as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: でも follows an interrogative word to express an inclusive meaning: anyone can.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: できます expresses the ability to perform an action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q17.kobun.why: The topic is introduced first with は, then だれでも marks the object to which it applies. The predicate できます shows that the library can be used.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace it with だれか, the meaning becomes someone, not just anyone.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget that でも after an interrogative word has an inclusive meaning, such as anyone or anywhere.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q18.kobun.vi: After waiting for 30 minutes, I finally managed to get on the bus.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q18.kobun.sk: Duration ＋ Vて ＋ やっと ＋ N に ＋ past potential verb
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: The duration phrase comes before the verb to show how long someone waited.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects the action of waiting with the event that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: やっと modifies the predicate and emphasizes the result achieved after waiting.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に marks the means of transport or the object toward which the action 乗る is directed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: のれました is the polite past potential form and means that the speaker was able to get on the bus.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q18.kobun.why: The duration and the waiting action come first, then the て form connects them to the result. やっと makes it clear that getting on the bus was achieved only after waiting for some time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use とうとう, it also means finally, but it emphasizes the result after a process rather than the difficulty of waiting.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use を with 乗る, but this verb usually goes with に to indicate the vehicle or means of transport someone gets on.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q19.kobun.vi: Tea goes very well with sweet cake.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective あまい directly modifies ケーキ.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: には marks the object being considered and adds a slight contrast.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks tea as the subject that creates the good match.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: あう describes two foods or things that match well.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q19.kobun.why: The cake is presented as the object of comparison with には, while tea is the subject being evaluated with が. あう comes at the end of the sentence to state the good relationship between the two foods.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use を合わせます, the meaning becomes active: to combine or mix tea with cake.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often translate あう as meet, but in sentences about food it means match or combine well.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q2.kobun.vi: In the future, I want to do work that is useful to people.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q2.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Nの ＋ V辞書形 ＋ Nが ＋ Vます remove ます＋たいです
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: しょうらい states a future time or direction.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 人 with the phrase やくにたつ to identify the people who benefit.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb phrase comes before しごと to modify the word for work.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks work as the desired object in the pattern したい.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: たい expresses the speaker's desire, and です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q2.kobun.why: The clause やくにたつ comes before the noun to describe the type of work. In the pattern 仕事がしたい, が marks what the speaker wants to do.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use を with 仕事, the sentence sounds unnatural in the pattern したい when you want to say that you want to do a job.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing it with 人のためになる is close in meaning to being useful to people, but it emphasizes the benefit given to them.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use を after 仕事, but with したい in this sentence, you need が to mark what is desired.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q20.kobun.vi: There is a party tomorrow, but I have something to do, so I cannot go.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q20.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N が あります が ＋ N は ＋ N が あります から ＋ negative potential verb
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The time word comes before the predicate to identify when the party takes place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: が connects two clauses that contrast having a party with being unable to go.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は makes the speaker the topic of the next clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q20.kobun.ch.3.vi: because I have something to do
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: から comes after a clause to state the reason for being unable to go.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: 行けません is the polite negative potential form and means cannot go.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q20.kobun.why: が creates a contrast between the information about the party and the speaker's situation. The clause with から comes directly before 行けません to explain the reason the speaker cannot go.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace から with ので, the reason stays the same, but the expression becomes softer and more objective.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If you replace が with けれども, the meaning of but remains, but the connection becomes longer and clearer.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often freely use the plain form before から, but remember that the entire clause before から must be complete in meaning.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q21.kobun.vi: Before playing the game, we had already decided on the rules.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the game as the object of the action する.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb clause する comes before まえに to indicate a time before an action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the game rules as the object of the action in the predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: The final phrase is the predicate and describes the action of deciding the rules in the given form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q21.kobun.why: The clause するまえに sets playing the game as the time reference, and the action of deciding the rules comes after it. Both verbs relate to the same activity, so the before-and-after order is clearly shown by まえに.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace まえに with あとで, the meaning changes to deciding the rules after playing the game.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: てから also shows the order of events, but emphasizes that the second action starts after the first action is completed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often put the verb before まえに in the past tense, but normally you must use the dictionary form, such as する.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q21.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの ＋ まえに
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q3.kobun.vi: It takes one hour to get from home to the graduation ceremony venue.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q3.kobun.sk: Nから ＋ Nの ＋ Nまで ＋ Duration ＋ かかります
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: から marks the starting point of the route.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the graduation ceremony with the venue where it takes place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: まで marks the endpoint of the route.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: １時間 states the amount of time needed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: かかります acts as the predicate and describes the time needed to travel the route.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q3.kobun.why: The pair から～まで creates the entire range from the starting point to the destination. The duration comes before かかります to say how long that route takes.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use に instead of まで, it only marks the destination and does not clearly show the entire range from home to there.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: で in a time expression can indicate a deadline for completion, so it is less suitable than expressing the required time with かかります.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often reverse から and まで; remember that から is the starting point and まで is the endpoint.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q4.kobun.vi: Excuse me, please tell the teacher that I will be a little late.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q4.kobun.sk: Opening phrase ＋ Degree ＋ Plain sentence ＋ と ＋ Recipient に ＋ Vてください
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: が connects the opening apology with the request or favor that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the content that must be passed on.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the recipient of the information.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: てください creates a polite request, asking the listener to pass on information.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q4.kobun.why: The content to be reported comes before と, the recipient of the information goes with に, and then comes the verb つたえる. てください turns the act of passing on information into a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If と言ってください is used, it means asking someone to say the exact sentence, while つたえてください emphasizes passing on the content.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern makes the request softer and more tentative, similar to asking whether the listener could pass on the message.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q4.kobun.tip: English learners may easily place に after the reported content; in this structure, と comes after the content, while に comes after the recipient.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ と ＋ 伝える/言う
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q5.kobun.vi: There is a test tomorrow, so I am studying today.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q5.kobun.sk: Time N ＋ N が あります ＋ それで ＋ N は ＋ Vます
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: This part only shows when the event takes place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: テストが marks something that exists or happens.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: それで connects the cause before it with the result after it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes today the topic in contrast with tomorrow.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q5.kobun.why: The time is placed at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the event that gives the reason. それで connects that reason with the action of studying, while は limits the topic to today.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing それで with だから still means “therefore,” but だから usually gives a more direct and conversational conclusion.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q5.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use それで as an independent word, but here it must connect a cause with a result.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q6.kobun.vi: I wrote a report about the Asian economy and submitted it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: について indicates the topic covered by the report.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the report as the object of the writing action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the action of writing with the later action of submitting.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q6.kobun.why: The phrase について states the topic of the report, while を marks the thing that was written. The two verbs are connected by て to show that the writing happened first and the submission happened later.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: に関して also means “related to,” but it is more formal and more common in written language than について.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q6.kobun.tip: Do not translate について as “about” and ignore the particle を; clearly identify the report as the object of 書く.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q7.kobun.vi: I felt uncomfortable because an unfamiliar person said something rude to me.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: しらない modifies 人, forming “an unfamiliar person.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person who performed the speech act in the passive sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な modifies こと, so な stays before the noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: ことを indicates the content of what was said.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: 言われて is the passive form て, connecting the event of being spoken to with the feeling that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the mood as being in the described state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.6.n: わるい changes the sentence to the polite past tense to describe the feeling at that time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q7.kobun.cn: Vる → Vられる; Vられるて ＋ following clause
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q7.kobun.why: The clause しらない 人 modifies the speaker, while に states the person who caused the action in the passive sentence. The content that was said is しつれいな こと, and then the form て connects it with the result: an uncomfortable mood.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If the active sentence is used, it focuses on the person who said the rude thing, rather than emphasizing the listener’s affected feelings.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q7.kobun.tip: English learners may easily confuse に in the passive sentence with を; the person who performs the action usually goes with に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q8.kobun.vi: This machine is new, and the technology is being used.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this machine the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: 新しい is the descriptive predicate of the topic before it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks technology as the object being used in the passive clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: つかわれています expresses the state in which the technology is being used.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q8.kobun.why: The sentence has one part describing the machine and another part stating that the technology is being used. は marks the topic at the beginning, while が goes with the affected subject in the passive sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If を使っています is used, the person or thing using the technology is stated clearly, instead of focusing on the technology being used.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q8.kobun.tip: Do not automatically translate が as the person performing the action; in a passive sentence, the noun with が can be the thing affected by the action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q8.kobun.cn: Vる → Vわれる; Vわれています
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q9.kobun.vi: When the schedule is decided, I will notify you by email or phone.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The past form + たら creates a condition or time for carrying out the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: か is placed after email to present a choice.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: または connects choices and has a slightly formal tone.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the means used to give the notice.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q9.kobun.why: たら sets the time condition for the act of notifying. The means are connected as two choices, and で marks the means used to perform the action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: それとも also means “or,” but it is usually used in questions that ask someone to choose one of several options.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q9.kobun.tip: English learners may easily omit で after 電話; when saying “notify by phone,” the means must go with で.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t11-q9.kobun.cn: Vた ＋ ら; N・Aな ＋ だったら; Aい ＋ かったら
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は presents the younger brother as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object that is liked in the pattern すきです.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: すきです is the adjective predicate な, expressing preference.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q1.kobun.why: The person who likes something is made the topic with は, while the liked thing goes with が in the pattern すきです. The predicate すきです comes at the end of the sentence to complete the statement.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If を使うのがすきです is used, it means liking to use vehicles, emphasizing the action rather than simply liking the vehicles themselves.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q1.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use を with すき, but the basic pattern is N が すきです.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q10.kobun.vi: I asked my senior about the school.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: に refers to the person being asked or the person providing information.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 学校 with こと to modify it, forming the meaning “a matter or topic about school.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: こと turns the content being asked about into a noun, while を marks the content of the asking action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: うかがいました is the humble form of 聞きました when asking someone of higher status.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q10.kobun.why: The person being asked goes with に, while the content of the question goes with ことを. 学校の modifies こと, and うかがいました comes at the end as the main predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 聞きました, the basic meaning is still “asked,” but the humble and polite nuance is weaker.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: 学校について聞きました also means asking about school, but it uses について to state the topic clearly instead of nominalizing it with こと.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for the content and を for the person being asked; in this pattern, the two roles must be distinguished in the opposite way.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q10.kobun.cn: N に + N の ことを + うかがう
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あなた with the noun that follows to show possession.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は states ゆめ as the topic being asked about.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 何ですか creates a question about the content or identity of ゆめ.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q2.kobun.why: The phrase あなたの modifies ゆめ, and then は makes ゆめ the topic. 何ですか is used to ask about the identity or content of that topic.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If used, the sentence asks what type of dream it is or what features it has.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を instead of は when stating the topic of a question.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q3.kobun.vi: On days off, I usually go somewhere.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the time or situation as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: たいてい modifies the action 出かけます and shows how often it usually happens.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: へ shows the destination of the action 出かけます.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 出かけます is the main predicate. It uses the ます form to describe a habit or a usual action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q3.kobun.why: 休みの日は sets the time context, たいてい shows the frequency, and どこかへ indicates the unspecified direction of going out. The predicate 出かけます comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with たいてい, the meaning is still “usually” or “generally,” but it places less emphasis on regular frequency.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake へ for a specific place, but here へ emphasizes the direction of movement.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q4.kobun.vi: Mr. Kimura is a beautiful person.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は states きむらさん as the topic being described.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: うつくしい is an adjective ending in い. It comes before 人 to modify 人.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 人です serves as the predicate and combines with the preceding adjective to describe the person being discussed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q4.kobun.why: The topic きむらさんは is described by the phrase うつくしい人. The adjective うつくしい comes before the noun 人, and then です ends the affirmative sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with きれいな人, the meaning is still “a beautiful person,” but it uses an adjective ending in な.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily add な after うつくしい, but an adjective ending in い does not use な before a noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q5.kobun.vi: After reading the letter, I was very surprised.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks てがみ as the object being read.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 読んで is the て form of 読む. It connects the action of reading with what happens afterward.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: びっくりしました is the main predicate and describes a state of surprise that happened in the past.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q5.kobun.why: てがみを is the object of 読む. The て form connects the action of reading with the following result or reaction, so びっくりしました comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 読んで is replaced with 読んでから, the sentence emphasizes more clearly that the surprise happened after the reading was finished.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate the て form as only “and,” but in this sentence it also shows the order of events.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q6.kobun.vi: The old man next door passed away.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects となり with いえ to modify the noun that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects いえ with おじいさん to identify which house the old man belongs to.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks おじいさん as the subject of the state なくなりました.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: なくなりました is the main predicate and is a polite, less direct way to say that someone has died.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q6.kobun.why: The two phrases の identify the house and the old man, respectively. が makes おじいさん the subject, while なくなりました describes the death at the end of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 死にました, the basic meaning is still “died,” but the expression is more direct and less tactful.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use は for おじいさん, but が is suitable when presenting a newly occurring event.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks おれい as the content or object of the speaking action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 言いました is the main predicate and uses the polite past form to describe a completed action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q7.kobun.why: おれいを is a noun for the content that was said and goes with を. 言いました comes at the end of the sentence to complete the meaning “said thank you.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence gives the exact words spoken as “thank you,” instead of generally saying that the person said thank you.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use と with おれい, but と is used to quote the exact words or content of speech; here, おれい is the object of を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q8.kobun.vi: My father gave me a novel.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject who performs the giving action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the item that was given.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: くれる describes another person doing or giving something for the speaker or someone on the speaker’s side.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q8.kobun.why: 父が is the person who performs the action, while しょうせつを is the item given. くれました is used because the benefit of the giving action is directed toward the speaker or someone on the speaker’s side.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with もらいました, the sentence changes to the recipient’s point of view: I received a novel from my father.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: あげる emphasizes someone giving something to another person and is not used to describe someone giving something toward the speaker.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse くれる and もらう because both relate to giving and receiving, but they use different points of view.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q8.kobun.cn: Vて + くれる/くれます/くれました
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: でも expands the range and means “anyone” or “everyone.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies こと, forming the meaning “the act of using.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: こと nominalizes the action, while が marks it as something that can be done.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: できます expresses the ability to perform an action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q1.kobun.why: りようする is changed to the dictionary form before こと to turn the action into a noun. The structure ことができます places the ability to do it in the final predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If りようできます or 利用できます is used, the meaning of ability is similar, but Vられる attaches directly to the verb.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If だれでも is replaced with だれかが, the meaning changes from “everyone” to “someone.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q1.kobun.tip: Do not change りようする into りようします before こと; this pattern requires the dictionary form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q1.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + ことができる/できます
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q10.kobun.vi: A large city has convenient transportation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective modifies まち, forming the phrase “large city.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: は states まち as the topic being described.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object with the characteristic べんり.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: This is the main predicate, using the adjective な in its polite form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q10.kobun.why: 大きい comes before まち to modify the noun. After stating the topic with は, the sentence uses が to mark the object with the characteristic べんり.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used after こうつう, the sentence contrasts the transportation with other objects.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use は for both まち and こうつう, but こうつうがべんり is the natural structure for saying that the transportation is convenient.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q2.kobun.vi: That store is open for business every day.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q2.kobun.sk: N は + Time + Nしています
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that store as the topic being described.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: This phrase indicates the time or frequency of an activity.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: しています describes business activity that is being maintained or taking place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q2.kobun.why: The store is made the topic with は, while 每日 adds the frequency of the action. えいぎょうしています is placed at the end of the sentence to describe the store's regularly operating state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with あいています, the sentence emphasizes that the store is open, not its business activity.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: 営業します refers to the action or schedule of opening every day, while 営業しています emphasizes the continuing state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand しています as meaning that something is happening right when it is said; with business activity, it can also describe a continuing state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q2.kobun.cn: Nを + する/します/しています
