default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q3.kobun.vi: This computer is made in Japan.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は states this computer as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: せい comes after a country name to indicate that a product was made in that country.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q3.kobun.why: このパソコンは is the topic, while にほんせいです is the statement about the product's origin. The pattern 国名+製 expresses in a concise way that the product was made in that country.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 日本で作った, the sentence emphasizes the action of making it in Japan rather than the label that it is a Japanese product.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: 日本のパソコン can mean a Japanese computer or a computer related to Japan. It has a broad meaning and does not confirm where it was made.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q3.kobun.tip: Do not translate せい as the adjective い; it is a suffix showing a product's origin and comes after a country name.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q4.kobun.vi: The restaurant was very crowded at that time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states that the restaurant is the topic being described.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The state verb is in the form ～ていました, describing a condition that existed in the past.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q4.kobun.why: The topic レストランは comes first, followed by the predicate describing the restaurant's condition. The form ～ていました emphasizes a state that occurred or existed at a particular time in the past.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this form is used instead, the meaning changes to say that the restaurant is crowded now.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ～ていました as an action in progress, but in this sentence it describes a crowded state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: に turns いっしょ into an adverb that modifies an action performed together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks しょくじ as the object of the verb する.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: しましょう is the polite volitional form of します, used to invite or suggest doing something together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q5.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます + ましょう
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q5.kobun.why: いっしょに modifies the action, しょくじを is the object, and しましょう comes at the end to create an invitation. The particle を connects the noun to the verb する.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ～ませんか, the invitation sounds gentler because it asks for the listener's opinion.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use を after いっしょに because に has already changed this phrase into an adverb showing how the action is done together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q6.kobun.vi: This restaurant is quiet and has few customers.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this restaurant the topic for comment.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: ～ています describes the restaurant's current state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q6.kobun.why: The phrase marking the object このレストランは comes at the beginning of the sentence, while すいています serves as the predicate describing the current state. は limits the comment to this restaurant.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used in this sentence, the meaning is similar, but it directly says that there are few customers.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q6.kobun.tip: すいています does not mean that the restaurant is open; in a restaurant context, it usually means that there are few customers.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q7.kobun.vi: I cut the vegetables into small pieces.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the vegetables as the object being cut.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The form く of the adjective こまかい turns it into an adverb that modifies how the cutting is done.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: きりました is the polite past form and the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q7.kobun.why: やさいを is the object affected, こまかく shows how the cutting was done, and きりました ends the sentence in the past tense. The adverb comes before the verb to describe how the action takes place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 小さく is used, it emphasizes a small size, while こまかく emphasizes cutting something into many small pieces.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q7.kobun.tip: When changing an adjective ending in い into an adverb, change い to く. Do not use the form い directly before a verb.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q8.kobun.vi: I hear that this city is safe.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that this city is the topic of the information being conveyed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.1.vi: I hear that it is safe
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: だ connects the adjective ending in な with そうです, creating the expression meaning that this city is said to be safe.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q8.kobun.why: このまちは is the topic, while あんぜんだそうです is the predicate carrying information heard from someone else. The adjective ending in な must have だ before そうです when it conveys reported information.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If あんぜんそうです is used, the meaning changes to “seems safe,” based on the speaker's judgment.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q8.kobun.tip: Do not omit だ before そうです with an adjective ending in な or a noun when そうです means “I hear that.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + そうです
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q9.kobun.vi: I threw away the old notebook.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: 古い comes before a noun to modify ノト.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks ノト as the object being thrown away.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: すてました is a verb in the polite past form and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q9.kobun.why: 古い comes directly before the noun to form the noun phrase 古いノト. This phrase takes を and becomes the object of すてました, while the final verb shows that the action was completed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is changed to this structure, 古い becomes the predicate and only says that the notebook is old; it no longer modifies the noun within the throwing-away action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t13-q9.kobun.tip: An adjective before a noun does not need a particle between the two parts, so say 古いノトを, not 古いのノトを.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q1.kobun.vi: I have already prepared the things to take on the trip.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the purpose or situation connected with the action of taking something.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb phrase modifies もの; 行く keeps its dictionary form before a noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: もの is the main noun in the modified phrase, while は states that this phrase is the topic.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: もう indicates that something was completed before the time of speaking.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb is in the polite past form and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q1.kobun.why: もって行く comes before もの to identify what kind of things they are. The phrase ものは is the topic, followed by もう and よういしました to express that the preparation has been completed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: This spelling also means things to take along, but it uses いく in kana instead of 行く.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If the past form is used, the meaning changes to things that were taken along, not things that are planned to be taken along.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put 行く in the past form because they think the action has already happened, but before もの, the dictionary form is needed to modify the noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q10.kobun.vi: I disagree with Mr. Tanaka's opinion.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects the owner to the noun いけん.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the object that the disagreement is directed toward.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: はんたいします is the main predicate and shows the action of disagreeing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q10.kobun.why: たなかさんの modifies いけん, forming the phrase “Mr. Tanaka's opinion.” With はんたいする, the object of disagreement is connected by に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it replaces the original expression, the meaning changes from disagreeing with the opinion to agreeing with it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after はんたいします, but this verb usually takes an object with に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q2.kobun.vi: Please do not make noise on the train.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 電車 with 中, forming the phrase “inside the train.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows the place where the action happens.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: ないで connects the negative form of a verb with ください to make a request not to do something.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: ください makes the request more polite.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q2.kobun.why: The place phrase 電車の中で comes before the verb to show where the action happens. The form ないでください comes at the end of the sentence and expresses a polite request not to do the action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it replaces the original expression, the sentence becomes a rule or a stronger prohibition, rather than only a polite reminder.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If ください is omitted, the request becomes more casual and direct.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily say さわらないでください when they want to say “do not make noise,” but さわる means to touch, while さわぐ means to make noise.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person who performs the action of apologizing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the person who receives the apology with the verb あやまる.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is in the polite past form and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q3.kobun.why: わたしは states the topic, while 友だちに identifies the person toward whom the apology is directed. あやまりました comes at the end of the sentence and shows that the action has been completed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: This writing keeps the same structure and meaning; it only replaces the verb's kana with kanji.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes saying “sorry,” rather than directly describing the act of apologizing as あやまる does.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after the person who receives the apology, but あやまる goes with に to mark the object.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q4.kobun.vi: While traveling, my bag was stolen.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: のとき shows the time or situation in which an event occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the thing that was stolen in the passive sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The polite past passive form describes an unpleasant event that happened to the speaker.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q4.kobun.cn: Group 1 verbs: change the row う to the row あ ＋ れる; Group 2: remove る ＋ られる; する→される; 来る→こられる.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q4.kobun.why: りょこうのとき states the situation first, and then かばんを is the thing affected by the act of stealing. The passive form emphasizes the harm suffered by the speaker.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the sentence focuses only on the bag being stolen and does not emphasize the affected person.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: 取られる can mean that something was taken or lost, while ぬすまれる emphasizes the act of stealing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use が for かばん because it is the thing that was lost, but in a passive sentence describing harm, the thing taken can still go with を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q5.kobun.vi: I did not make it to the appointment on time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects やくそく with 時間, forming the phrase “the appointment time.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: に shows the time that must be reached.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.2.vi: did not make it in time
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 間に合う means to make it on time; the polite past negative form shows that the person did not make it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q5.kobun.why: やくそくの時間 creates a specific time reference, and に marks the time that must be met. 間に合いませんでした describes the result of not meeting that time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced by 遅れました, the direct meaning is “arrived late,” while 間に合いませんでした emphasizes missing the deadline.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If までに is used, the meaning is not making it before or by the deadline.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate and use に as “at,” but in 間に合う, に marks the time that must be met.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q5.tokens.4.m: did not make it in time
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q6.kobun.vi: I invited Mr. Yoshida to our party.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the person who is invited.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects the owner with the noun パーティー.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に shows the event or place to which the invited person goes.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb さそう is changed to the polite past form to describe a completed action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q6.kobun.why: The invited person comes before を, while the event they are invited to comes before に. The verb さそう is the main predicate at the end of the sentence and changes to さそいました to show that the event happened.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it replaces the original expression, the meaning becomes participating in the party rather than inviting Mr. Yoshida.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse を and に, but the invited person takes を, while the event they are invited to takes に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q7.kobun.vi: This school is very active in sports.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes この学校 the topic being described.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the field described as active.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: さかんです is the adjective predicate な and describes the lively state of sports activities.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q7.kobun.why: は states the larger topic, the school, while が identifies the field being evaluated. さかんです ends the sentence and states the characteristic of that field.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced in this sentence, the meaning would focus on there being many people or things related to sports, rather than on sports activities being active.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate が as “is,” but here が marks the field being described, not a definition.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q8.kobun.vi: Before running, you must always warm up.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: 前に comes after a verb in the dictionary form to show when one action happens before another.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: This adverb modifies the action します and emphasizes that it is always done.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the activity being performed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: します is the main predicate and describes doing the warm-up exercises.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q8.kobun.why: The clause はしる前に comes first to set the time reference. Then かならず modifies the action じゅんびうんどうをします, while を marks the warm-up exercises as the object being performed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced in this sentence, the meaning becomes “after running” instead of “before running.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use the form た before 前に, but with 前に, the verb normally uses the dictionary form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q9.kobun.vi: It has started to get dark.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the natural phenomenon that is changing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects くれる with きました to form a sequence that describes an ongoing change.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: きました in the structure てくる shows that a change has gradually appeared and progressed toward the present.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q9.kobun.why: 日が is the phenomenon that serves as the subject of the change, while くれてきました describes the sky gradually becoming dark. て connects the verb showing the change with くる to direct the change toward the present.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced in this sentence, the nuance would be that the change continues to progress from the present into the future.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t14-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand てきました as only meaning “came,” but in this sentence it shows a process of gradual change reaching the present.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q1.kobun.vi: I am studying Japanese very hard.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The form に of the adjective な ねっしん modifies the action of studying.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object being studied.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: ています describes an action that is continuing at the time of speaking.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q1.kobun.why: ねっしんに comes first in the sentence to describe how the studying is done. 日本語を is the object of べんきょうする, while ています shows that the studying is still continuing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If it replaces the expression in this sentence, the meaning is still studying with great effort, but it emphasizes effort more than an enthusiastic, focused attitude.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget に after the adjective な when using it as an adverb, but they must say ねっしんに.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q10.kobun.vi: I prepared luggage for the trip.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects りょこう with にもつ and shows what kind of luggage is being mentioned.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the luggage as the object being prepared.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: しました is the polite past form of する and describes a completed action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q10.kobun.why: りょこうの modifies にもつ to identify which luggage. The luggage is the object marked by を, and then よういしました describes the completed preparation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: じゅんびしました also means prepare, but it is more common and direct in tone than よういしました.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often omit の between りょこう and にもつ, making the relationship “the trip’s luggage” unclear.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q2.kobun.vi: I have experience working part-time at a restaurant.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q2.kobun.sk: N place で + N の + N が + あります
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where an activity or state occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun アルバイト to the following noun and modifies “experience.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks what exists in the pattern あります.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is a predicate that indicates existence or possession.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q2.kobun.why: The place is introduced first with で. Then the noun 経験 is made the subject with が. あります expresses that the speaker has an experience.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this expression is used instead, the sentence emphasizes having done an action before rather than currently having experience.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use に instead of で when talking about the place where the work happened.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q3.kobun.vi: This Japanese novel has been translated into English.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q3.kobun.sk: この + N の + N は + N に + past passive verb
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify an object near the speaker.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 日本語 with the noun しょうせつ and creates a modifying relationship.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the novel the topic of the passive sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the target language into which the content is changed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: されました is the polite past form of the passive voice and shows that the topic was translated by someone else.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q3.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます + れる/られる; passive V, ました form
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q3.kobun.why: The phrase この日本語のしょうせつ identifies the book, while は marks it as the topic. えいごに gives the target language and combines with the passive form to express that the book was translated.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If the active voice is used, the sentence focuses on the translator or the person who performed the action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse に, which indicates the target language, with で, which indicates a tool or means.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q4.kobun.vi: Among the people here, I only know Tanaka.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q4.kobun.sk: N は + この + N の中で + N以外は + negative verb
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks the person who knows or does not know.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: この modifies the range mentioned afterward.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the range used to limit the objects being compared or chosen.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 以外は states what is excluded or limited within the range under consideration.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: しりません is a negative predicate meaning not to know the person or thing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q4.kobun.why: わたしは is the topic, and then で limits the range. 以外は creates the meaning “except …,” and together with しりません it expresses that the speaker knows only Tanaka.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If だけ知っています is used, the meaning “I only know Tanaka” is stated more directly and has less of an excluding tone.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand 以外は as “also outside …,” but in a negative structure it usually means “except …, not.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q5.kobun.vi: Mr. Mori went on a business trip instead of Mr. Kimura.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q5.kobun.sk: N のかわりに + N が + N に + past verb
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: のかわりに indicates the person or thing being replaced in the action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person who actually went on the business trip.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the purpose or activity that follows the verb 行く.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きました is the polite past predicate form of 行く.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q5.kobun.why: のかわりに states who was replaced, while が marks the person who performs the action instead. The activity or purpose of going is placed before 行きました with に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with のために, the meaning is “for Kimura’s benefit,” which does not necessarily imply that Mori went instead of Kimura.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often mistake the person going instead as the topic with は, while が makes clear who directly performs the action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q5.kobun.cn: Nの + かわりに; Vる/Nの + かわりに
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q6.kobun.vi: Mr. Kimura has recovered from his illness.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q6.kobun.sk: N は + N が + past verb
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person whose health condition has changed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the direct object whose condition changes or which is cured.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: なおりました is a past predicate that describes an illness being cured or recovered from.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q6.kobun.why: は identifies the person being discussed, while が marks the illness connected with the recovered state. なおりました describes the result that has been achieved.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes that the person’s health has improved without directly saying that the illness has been cured.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use を with 病気, but a state or changing object usually goes with が.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q6.tokens.1.m: Mr., Ms., older man, older woman
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q7.kobun.vi: My older sister was discharged from the hospital last week.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q7.kobun.sk: N time、 + N が + nominalized past verb
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence to identify when the action occurred.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person who performed the action of leaving the hospital.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: たいいんしました is a polite past predicate that describes leaving the hospital after treatment.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q7.kobun.why: The time is placed at the beginning of the sentence and separated by a comma. The subject あねが comes before the predicate to state who performed the action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning is “came home from the hospital,” describing the act of returning rather than emphasizing the discharge procedure.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate たいいんしました as “leave the hospital,” but they need to understand that this is a fixed expression meaning “be discharged from the hospital.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q8.kobun.vi: The next lecture starts at 2 o’clock.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は marks the lecture being discussed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: から marks the starting point, while です ends the polite statement.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q8.kobun.why: The phrase つぎの modifies こうぎ, forming “the next lecture.” は marks the topic, while ２時からです shows the starting time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ２時までです, it means that it ends at 2 o’clock.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake から for “from,” but in this sentence it marks the starting point of the lecture.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q9.kobun.vi: I am sorry for being late.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: て connects an action or reason to the apology in the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: すみません is a sentence-final expression used for a polite apology.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q9.kobun.why: The verb ちこくする changes to the て form to connect a reason or situation to an apology. The apology comes afterward to show the speaker’s attitude toward being late.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: ので clearly states the causal relationship “because I was late” and sounds more formal and explanatory.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: てしまって adds a feeling of having accidentally caused it or regretting being late.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t15-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use the dictionary form before すみません; here, the て form is needed to connect the two parts of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q1.kobun.why: This is an independent vocabulary entry, not a sentence with a grammar structure; the word is read as しょうらい.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q3.kobun.why: しっかり is an adverb. It modifies the following verb and describes doing something firmly, seriously, or thoroughly.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: ちゃんと also means doing something properly or thoroughly, but しっかり emphasizes stability and effort.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate しっかり only as “certainly” and forget that this word usually modifies an action with the meaning “seriously” or “carefully.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: This part carries the main meaning of the adjective, while い is the ending.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: い identifies this as an い-adjective in the dictionary form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q4.kobun.why: This is a standalone vocabulary word, so it does not use a particle or sentence-linking pattern. い is the fixed ending of an adjective ending in い.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q4.kobun.tip: Do not confuse きびしい with きびしく, because きびしく is the adverbial form used to modify another verb or adjective.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the first sound of the word 最近 and does not function as a particle.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: This is the final sound that completes the reading of the noun 最近.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q6.kobun.why: 最近 is a noun referring to a time period. It usually appears at the beginning of a sentence or before a verb to indicate a period close to the present.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: このごろ also means recently and is more conversational.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: 今ごろ usually refers to the time around now and is not exactly synonymous with 最近.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q6.kobun.tip: Do not use 最近 to refer to an exact time such as yesterday or 3 o’clock.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.0.vi: stem of the verb meaning receive
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: This part carries the humble meaning of receiving, while く is the dictionary-form ending.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: く completes the dictionary form of the verb いただく.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q8.kobun.why: いただく is the humble form of もらう. The giver is marked by から, and the received item is marked by を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: もらう also means receive, but it is neutral and does not clearly show humility.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: くださる describes a superior giving something to the speaker, while いただく describes the recipient’s side.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q8.kobun.tip: Do not use いただく to elevate yourself; it is a way to lower yourself when receiving from another person.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the first sound of the adverb とうとう, not a particle.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: This is the repeated sound that completes the adverb とうとう.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q9.kobun.why: とうとう is an adverb placed before the predicate. It emphasizes a result that happens after a period of waiting or continuation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: ついに also means finally, but it can be used in writing and has a more formal tone.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: やっと emphasizes the hardship or relief felt when finally achieving a result.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t16-q9.kobun.tip: とうとう usually goes with a result that has already happened, so it often combines with a verb in the た form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The part はずかし carries the adjective meaning embarrassed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: い is the ending of an adjective ending in い. It allows the word to be used as a predicate or to modify a noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q1.kobun.why: はずかしい is an adjective ending in い, so it can be used directly as a predicate without adding だ. When the tense changes, the ending い changes according to the tense and negative form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 恥ずかしそうだ, the sentence means “looks embarrassed,” which is an inference from outward appearance.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily add だ after an adjective ending in い; in a present affirmative sentence, はずかしい is already complete.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q10.kobun.why: This is a transitive verb in the dictionary form. It describes going to pick up or receiving a person, time, or event.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 送る, it means seeing someone off or taking someone away, opposite to the direction of welcoming someone toward the speaker.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q10.kobun.tip: 迎える describes welcoming someone toward the speaker, so it must be distinguished from 送る, which means seeing someone off.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: くら is the first part of the verb 比べる and carries the meaning of comparing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: べる completes the dictionary form of the verb 比べる.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q3.kobun.why: 比べる is a transitive verb, so the object being compared is marked by を. The two objects being compared are usually connected by と.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 比べて is used, the verb changes to the て form to connect it to the next action or clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に for the object of comparison, but 比べる usually uses を for the content being compared.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q4.kobun.vi: almost time, it is about time
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: そろ is the adverbial part indicating that a point in time is approaching.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The repetition creates the sense of “almost time” or “it is about time” and modifies the following action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q4.kobun.why: そろそろ is an adverb placed before a verb to signal that an action will soon happen as time naturally passes. This word usually does not need a particle.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with もうすぐ, it means “very soon,” emphasizing that the time is even closer.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand そろそろ as “slowly,” but in this pattern it only refers to an approaching time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q6.kobun.why: This is a noun presented as an independent vocabulary word, without a particle or grammar pattern.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q6.kobun.tip: Do not confuse 準備 with 支度; 準備 usually emphasizes preparation in general.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q7.kobun.why: This is an intransitive verb in the dictionary form. It describes becoming dirty without stating an object with を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 汚す, it means making something else dirty.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with 汚れる, but this verb usually goes with が to state what becomes dirty.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q8.kobun.why: This is a transitive verb in the dictionary form. It usually needs an object before を, such as a room or an object.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 片付く, it means become tidy or be tidied up, without emphasizing who performs the action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q8.kobun.tip: Distinguish 片付ける, meaning to tidy something up, from 片付く, meaning to become tidy or be tidied up.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q9.kobun.why: This is a transitive verb in the dictionary form. It is used when someone cares for and helps a person or plant grow.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 育つ, it means to grow or develop by itself, without a direct object.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t17-q9.kobun.tip: 育てる needs an object with を, while 育つ usually uses が to describe an object developing by itself.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q1.kobun.why: This is an adjective ending in い in its dictionary form. It can directly modify a noun or be used as a predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 特別だ, it means special and does not necessarily suggest rarity.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q1.kobun.tip: When modifying a noun, keep the form 珍しい and do not add な.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: Combine with すぐ to form an adverb indicating a time that will soon arrive.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: It follows もう to complete the adverbial phrase もうすぐ, meaning before long.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q2.kobun.why: もうすぐ is an adverbial phrase referring to a time near the present. The two parts, もう and すぐ, combine as a fixed expression to modify an action or event that will soon happen.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with すぐに, it leans toward doing something immediately and does not emphasize an event that will soon happen.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q2.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically split もうすぐ into the meaning of もう, “already,” and すぐ, “immediately.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the first part of the vocabulary word げんいん, and it has no independent grammatical role.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: Combined with げん, it forms the noun げんいん.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q3.kobun.why: げんいん is a noun. In a sentence, it can be the subject or object, depending on the particle that follows it. The word itself stands alone, so its specific grammatical role cannot yet be identified.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use りゆう, it means a reason, usually the reason for an action or decision.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q3.kobun.tip: Do not confuse げんいん with a general reason; this word usually emphasizes the cause that leads to a result.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the first part of the vocabulary word こしょう, and it has no separate grammatical role.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: Combined with こ, it forms the noun こしょう.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q4.kobun.why: こしょう is a noun referring to a machine or device being faulty. In a sentence, it needs a particle such as が or の to show its grammatical relationship.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use こわれる, it becomes a verb describing an object that is broken or damaged.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q4.kobun.tip: Distinguish こしょう, the noun for a malfunction, from こわれる, the verb meaning to be broken.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q7.tokens.0.m: to stop, to end, to clear up
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q8.kobun.vi: It started to rain during the baseball game.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects やきゅう to the noun しあい, creating the phrase “baseball game.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects しあい to とちゅう, creating the phrase “during the game.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the time or situation in which an event occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks rain as the subject of the falling phenomenon.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: ふって is the て form of ふる. It connects with きました to create a pattern that describes a change moving toward the present.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: きました is the main predicate. It shows that the rain started falling and that this situation has continued up to the present.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q8.kobun.why: The phrase やきゅうのしあいのとちゅうで identifies when the event occurred. The pattern Vてくる shows that the rain started and has continued up to the time of speaking.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence only says that it is raining, without emphasizing the beginning.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning changes to an event continuing and developing toward the future.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q8.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically translate てきました as “has come”; in this sentence, it adds the meaning “has started to appear.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t18-q8.tokens.0.m: in the middle, on the way
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the first part of the vocabulary word ていねい, not a separate grammatical element.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: This is the remaining part of the word ていねい. The complete word is the adjective な, meaning polite or careful.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q1.kobun.why: ていねい is the adjective な, so when it modifies a noun, it must be connected with な. When it is used as a predicate, it can be connected with です or だ.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: 親切な emphasizes being kind and helpful, while 丁寧な emphasizes a polite or careful way of doing or saying something.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: 詳しい means detailed and does not have the polite sense of 丁寧.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget な before a noun. For example, you must say 丁寧な言葉.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q10.kobun.why: This is an independent vocabulary word, not a sentence with a complete grammatical structure.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q10.kobun.tip: Do not confuse 関係 with 関心[かんしん], which means interest or concern.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the first part of the repeated adverb どんどん, not an independent sentence element.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: Repeating it creates the adverb どんどん, which modifies an action or change that happens strongly and continuously.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q2.kobun.why: どんどん is an adverb. It usually comes before a verb or adjective to express rapid, continuous, or increasingly clear progress. It does not need a separate connecting particle.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: だんだん describes a gradual change, which is milder and more neutral than どんどん.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: ますます emphasizes an increasing degree and is often used in writing or formal speech.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate どんどん as only “quickly,” but this word also emphasizes continuation and steady development.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the first part of the vocabulary word てきとう, not a separate grammatical element.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: This is the remaining part of the word てきとう. The complete word usually means suitable or appropriate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q3.kobun.why: てきとう is the adjective な, so use てきとうな before a noun. Depending on the context, this word can also have a negative sense of doing something carelessly or arbitrarily.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: 適切な means suitable and accurate according to a standard, without a careless sense.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: いい加減な emphasizes carelessness and arbitrariness, and is usually more negative than 適当な.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand 適当 as only meaning suitable, but in many sentences it can mean careless or arbitrary.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q4.kobun.why: This is a vocabulary word written entirely in hiragana, not a sentence with a grammatical structure. The word is divided into two parts to identify its full reading.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q4.kobun.tip: Do not assume that が is a particle in がく, because がく is only part of the sound of the word.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q5.tokens.0.m: to send, to see someone off
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q9.kobun.vi: The summer vacation is about to end.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q9.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Nが ＋ Vて ＋ しまいます
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: もうすぐ modifies the predicate and shows that the event is about to happen.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the summer vacation as the event that is about to end.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: おわって is the て form of おわる, connecting the main verb with しまいます.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: しまいます describes an event that will be completed, often with a feeling of regret or something happening against one's wishes.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q9.kobun.why: もうすぐ is placed before the predicate to signal that the time is near. Vてしまう follows おわる, emphasizing that the vacation will end completely and that the speaker feels regret.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the meaning emphasizes continuation or a change from the present toward the future.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence only predicts that the vacation will end, without a feeling of regret.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may overlook the emotional sense of しまう and understand it simply as “finish doing.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t19-q9.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ しまう／しまいます
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative その modifies the noun りんご.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the apple as the object of the cutting action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: 切って is the て form of 切る. It connects with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: ください follows a verb in the て form to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q1.kobun.why: そのりんごを is a noun phrase used as the object, placed before the verb in the basic Japanese word order. The て form combines with ください to turn the clause into a favor or request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, it means cutting together or suggesting cutting, not directly asking the listener to cut.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence asks for permission to cut rather than asking someone else to cut.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may place ください before the verb, but in Japanese ください follows the verb in the て form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q10.kobun.vi: A strange sound is coming from the next room.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects となり with へや to modify the room.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the place from which the sound comes.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the thing that produces or is perceived in the phenomenon.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: します creates a predicate showing that a sound is being produced.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q10.kobun.why: The source phrase へやから comes before the phenomenon 音がします. The adjective へんな comes directly before the noun 音 to describe the sound.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence emphasizes that the sound is heard, rather than that it is being produced.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を with 音がします, but the pattern for simply perceiving a sound uses 音がします.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q10.tokens.7.m: to produce a sound, to be
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q11.kobun.vi: My father is injured and is in the hospital.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that my father is the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks けが as the object of します in the expression けがをする.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the preceding action or state with the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the location where a person exists.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: います is used for the existence of a person and combines with the location に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q11.kobun.why: けがをして、 connects the injured state with current information about the person's location. Because the subject is a person, use います, while the location goes with に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence emphasizes receiving treatment at the hospital rather than simply being there.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q11.kobun.tip: Do not use で with います when saying where a person exists; a location of existence usually uses に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q12.kobun.vi: Would you like to go and watch the soccer match?
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects サッカー with 試合 to indicate a match in the sport of soccer.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the match as the object of the action of watching.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: Vます is omitted and ます combines with に to indicate the purpose of going.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きませんか is a negative question used to invite or suggest something.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q12.kobun.why: The object 試合を comes before the purpose phrase 見に行く. The negative question form at the end of the sentence creates an inviting tone.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the invitation sounds more like an active suggestion to go together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q12.kobun.tip: Do not keep ます in 見ます when connecting it with に to show purpose; use 見に行く instead.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q12.kobun.cn: Vます-stem ＋ に ＋ 行く・来る・帰る
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q13.kobun.vi: I will ask Maria directly whether she will go with us.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: に changes いっしょ into an adverb that modifies 行く.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: か turns the clause 行く into unknown information that is taken to someone for questioning.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the person being asked.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 直接 modifies 聞いてみます and shows how the question is asked.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: てみる expresses trying to perform the action 聞く.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q13.kobun.why: 行くか is the content of the question, while マりアさんに indicates the person receiving the question. 聞いてみます shows the intention to try asking in order to find out the answer.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 行くかどうか, the meaning of the content becomes clearly “whether or not to go” and sounds more neutral.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q13.kobun.tip: When asking indirectly, Vietnamese speakers may easily add と after か; in this pattern, 行くか can connect directly with 聞く.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to indicate an object near the speaker.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that チーム is the topic being commented on.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: 弱い is an adjective ending in い used as the predicate, while です adds a polite tone.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q14.kobun.why: この modifies チーム, and then は makes the team the topic. The adjective ending い appears in the predicate and can connect directly with です.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence changes to a negative meaning: this team is not weak.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q14.kobun.tip: Do not change 弱い into 弱く before です; the adjective ending い stays in this form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q15.kobun.vi: The match was canceled because of the rain.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the cause that led to the match being canceled.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing that changes into a new state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the state or result that the thing changes into.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: なりました describes a change that has occurred.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q15.kobun.why: 雨で states the cause, while 中止になりました describes the match changing into a canceled state. The subject of the change goes with が.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence means that someone actively canceled the match, rather than simply saying that the match changed into a canceled state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q15.kobun.tip: Distinguish 雨で, which indicates the cause, from 雨が降って, in which 雨が is the subject of the action of raining.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vi: This carrot is thin, isn't it?
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative この modifies the noun にんじん.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the carrot the topic of the comment.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 細い is the adjective predicate い; ですね softens the comment and suggests agreement.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q2.kobun.why: このにんじんは states the object being commented on, while 細い is the predicate describing its shape. ですね adds a gentle comment, as if asking the listener to confirm it too.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the sentence focuses directly on the subject that has the thin feature instead of stating a topic for comment.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 細そうですね, the meaning changes to “it seems thin,” showing a guess based on appearance.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate 細い as small, but this word mainly describes something thin or slender in width.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vi: I will make a cake and take it with me.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the thing being made.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects the action of making the cake with the next action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: This part connects the action of carrying something with 行きます.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 行きます is the main predicate and describes going to another place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q3.kobun.why: The actions are arranged in order: make the cake, carry it, and then go. The て form is used to connect consecutive actions.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence emphasizes that the first action must be completed before the next action is performed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget that the て form here is used only to connect actions and does not mean past tense.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q3.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ Vて ＋ 行きます
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vi: Because there are few shops nearby, it is rather inconvenient.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates a place, meaning in the nearby area.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of the state 少ない.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 少ない changes into 少なくて to connect the cause with the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 不便 is an な adjective, used with です to form a polite predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q4.kobun.why: The place phrase comes first, followed by the subject 店が and the state 少ない. 少なくて connects the state “few shops” with the result “inconvenient.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 少なくて is replaced with 少ないので, the reason is stated more clearly and politely.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use 少ないで, but the correct connecting form of the adjective い is 少なくて.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vi: This apartment is spacious, isn't it?
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states that this apartment is the topic being commented on.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending い forms the predicate and describes the apartment's feature.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ですね is used to confirm something or seek the listener's agreement.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q5.kobun.why: The topic このアパートは comes first, followed by the adjective 広い as the main comment. ですね is placed at the end to turn the comment into a gentle confirmation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If です is used, the sentence simply gives information politely and does not ask for agreement as ですね does.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If 広くない is used, the meaning changes to “this apartment is not spacious, is it?”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily add な after the adjective ending in い; they should say 広いです or 広いですね, not 広いなです.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vi: The train we take is an express train.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject performing the action のる in the modifying clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb comes before the noun 電車 to modify that noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes 電車 the topic of the main sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: 急行 is the noun predicate, combining with です to state the type of train.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q6.kobun.why: The clause わたしたちがのる comes directly before 電車 to identify which train it is. After 電車 is introduced as the topic, 急行です states the type of train.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is changed to を, 電車 becomes the object of a later verb, rather than the topic being described.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: わたしたちの電車 only means “our train,” without emphasizing the action of our taking the train.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put のる after 電車, but a modifying clause in Japanese always comes before the noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q7.kobun.vi: Because I will travel, I will go to the airport.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: から connects the reason clause to the action of going to the airport.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the destination of the action 行きます.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きます is the main predicate and describes going in the present or future.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q7.kobun.why: The reason clause comes before から, and the destination comes before 行きます. The particle に is suitable because 空港 is the place being approached.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: ので also expresses a reason, but its tone is softer and more objective than から.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: へ also indicates going toward the airport, but emphasizes direction more than に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で with 行きます, but a destination must use に or へ.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q8.kobun.vi: Beautiful scenery can be seen from here.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point or the range of observation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: されいな comes before 景色 to modify the noun 景色.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object seen in the potential sentence 見られます.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 見られます describes the ability to see scenery from this location.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q8.kobun.why: ここから states the viewing location, while されいな景色 is the noun being seen. 景色が acts as the grammatical subject of 見られます, meaning that the scenery can be seen.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: 景色を見ます only describes the active action of looking at the scenery, without emphasizing the ability to see it from here.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: 景色が見えます says that the scenery naturally comes into view, without emphasizing ability or viewing conditions.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse 見られます with 見えます; 見られます focuses on “being able to see,” while 見えます means “to be naturally visible.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q8.tokens.2.m: beautiful (probably a spelling error for きれいな)
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q8.kobun.cn: V可能形・V受身形 + ます
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q9.kobun.vi: I received a map at the Japanese inn.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the action of receiving the map occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: もらいました is the main predicate and describes receiving something in the past.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q9.kobun.why: The place where the action occurs comes before で, the thing received comes before を, and then comes the verb もらいました. This order clearly shows the place and object of the receiving action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: から emphasizes that the inn is the provider or source of the map, not merely the place where the action occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: に with 行きました indicates a destination, not receiving a map there.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t2-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に to indicate the place of receiving, but the correct particle for the place where an action occurs is で.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q1.kobun.vi: I am interested in Japanese films.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the person being discussed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 日本 with the noun えいが to modify that noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the object toward which the interest is directed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject of the state あります.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: あります expresses the existence or possession of a state or thing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q1.kobun.why: The phrase 日本のえいが is placed before に to identify the object of interest. The pattern Nに興味がある uses に for the object and が for 興味, and then ends with あります.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, the meaning is still being interested, but the tone is more formal and focuses more on concern or interest.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after えいが, but 興味がある goes with に to indicate the object.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の shows possession and modifies しゅみ.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は introduces the hobby as the topic being explained.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the direct object of the verb 読む.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies こと and forms a noun referring to an action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: こと turns the action 読む into a noun, while です concludes the explanation of the topic.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q2.kobun.why: わたしのしゅみは introduces the topic, while 読むことです explains that topic. を marks the novel as the object of 読む before the action is turned into a noun with こと.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this structure is used, the sentence still states the hobby, but it may sound more like a definition or a formal explanation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the focus shifts to the feeling of liking that action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q2.kobun.tip: Do not repeat the sound む when connecting 読む with こと; it must be 読むこと.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q2.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの + ことだ
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q3.kobun.vi: I am working part-time at a store near my home.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the person performing the activity.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects ちかく with 店 to modify the place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the part-time work occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the activity being performed in the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: しています describes an activity that is continuing or currently happening.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q3.kobun.why: ちかくの店 forms a noun phrase meaning the nearby store, while で marks the place of the activity. アルバイトをしています uses を for the activity and ています to express a continuing or maintained work state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence emphasizes working at the store, not specifically doing part-time work.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for the place of an action, but the place where an activity occurs must use で.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の modifies 国 and indicates the speaker's country.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: は introduces the country as the subject being discussed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: と indicates the partner taking part in the trading activity.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks an activity carried out with Japan.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: しています shows that the trade activity is continuing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q4.kobun.why: わたしの国は is the topic, 日本と indicates the other participant, and ぼうえきをしています describes the ongoing trade activity. The particle と is suitable for a cooperative or interactive relationship between two sides.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the basic meaning does not change, but 行っている is more formal and more typical of written language.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q4.kobun.tip: Do not use に after 日本 when saying that the two sides trade with each other; use と for a partnership relationship.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the younger brother as the person whose preference is being discussed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the liked object in the pattern 好きです.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: すきです expresses a state of liking and ends the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q5.kobun.why: In the pattern Nが好きです, the noun used with が is the liked object, while the person who has the feeling is marked by は. Therefore, のりものが is not the subject in the usual English translation, but the object of the preference.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence becomes more formal and uses を because this is a verb, not the adjective 好き.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily say のりものをすきです, but 好きです always uses が for the liked object.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects noun あなた with noun ゆめ and shows possession.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes ゆめ the topic being asked about.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 何ですか creates a polite question about the content of the dream.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q6.kobun.why: The possessive phrase あなたの comes before the noun ゆめ to identify the dream being discussed. は states the topic, while 何ですか asks for the identity or content of that topic.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence asks about the feeling or condition of the dream, not what it is.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate の as "of" but forget to put the phrase あなたの directly before the possessed noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q7.kobun.why: This is a vocabulary word that stands alone and does not contain a particle relationship or grammar pattern to analyze. The two parts are separated only for presentation; when joined, they still form one complete word.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t20-q7.kobun.tip: Do not separate 将来 into two separate words when using it; it is one noun, pronounced しょうらい.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q1.kobun.vi: Mr. Kim is listening carefully to the teacher's words.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は shows that Mr. Kim is the person performing the action of listening.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 先生 with 話 and shows that the story or words belong to the teacher.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks 話 as the object being listened to.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The form に of the adjective な まじめな changes it into an adverb that modifies 聞いています.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: 聞いています uses the ている form to express an ongoing action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q1.kobun.why: The subject comes first, followed by the object being listened to, identified by の and を. The adverb まじめに comes directly before the verb to describe how the action is performed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, it only describes an action that was completed in the past and does not stress the state of listening now.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, it means that a sound is being heard naturally, not actively listened to.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use まじめな before the verb; before a verb, it must change to まじめに.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q2.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I went to a beauty salon to get my hair cut.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q2.kobun.sk: 時点 + N を + Vますdropます に + N へ + Vました
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: きのう indicates when the action happened and does not need the particle に in this expression.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks かみ as the object of the cutting action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The continuative form of きる combines with に to express the purpose of going somewhere to do something.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: へ indicates the direction of movement to a place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: 行きました is the polite past form of 行く and serves as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q2.kobun.cn: Vますdropます + に + 行く/来る/帰る
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q2.kobun.why: The time expression comes first, followed by the object of the cutting action. The phrase きりに states the purpose, while the destination comes before the movement verb and is used with へ.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, it still states the purpose, but it is more formal and has a wider range of use than きりに.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If で is used, it emphasizes the place where the hair-cutting happens, not the direction of going there.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に after きのう; with time words such as きのう, きょう, and あした, に is usually not needed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q3.kobun.vi: Mr. Nakagawa is a quiet person.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies Mr. Nakagawa as the topic being described.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: おとなしい comes before 人 to modify the noun 人.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 人です creates a noun predicate, in which おとなしい modifies 人.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q3.kobun.why: The adjective おとなしい comes before 人 because it describes the type of person being discussed. The whole phrase おとなしい人 forms a noun predicate with です.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the phrase becomes a connecting clause and needs another clause or feature after it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the sentence directly says that Mr. Nakagawa is quiet and no longer has the structure "is a quiet person".
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q3.kobun.tip: The い-ending adjective comes directly before a noun, with no な added between おとなしい and 人.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q4.kobun.vi: There is an interesting TV program being broadcast tonight.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: こんや indicates when the program is broadcast.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: おもしろい comes before テレビばんぐみ to modify the program.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects テレビばんぐみ with ほうそう and identifies the content being broadcast.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the existence of an event in the pattern あります.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: あります expresses the existence of the broadcast, while よ is used to inform the listener.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q4.kobun.why: The time expression comes first, followed by the phrases modifying ほうそう. In the existence pattern, the existing event is used with が, and the verb あります comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the subject actively broadcasts the program instead of announcing that there is a broadcast.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, it emphasizes that the program is broadcast in the passive voice or in a more polite way.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place おもしろい after the noun following Vietnamese word order; in Japanese, an adjective must come before the noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q5.kobun.vi: On days off, I usually go somewhere.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は indicates the time or topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The adverb modifies the action of going out.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: どこか means somewhere, while へ indicates the direction of movement.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 出かける in the polite form ます serves as the main predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q5.kobun.why: 休みの日は sets the time context, then たいてい modifies the action. へ is used with a place or destination, while 出かけます expresses the main action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced by どこにも, it usually must be used with a negative form and means not going anywhere at all.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced by どこへでも, the meaning changes to going anywhere.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に instead of へ without noticing that へ emphasizes the direction of movement.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes Kimura the topic being described.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending in い comes before a noun to modify 人.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 人です functions as a noun predicate and identifies what kind of person Kimura is.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q6.kobun.why: After the topic きむらさんは, the adjective うつくしい comes before 人 to describe that person. です ends the noun sentence politely.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with きれいな, the meaning is still beautiful or clean, but this is a な-adjective, so な must come before 人.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: This structure makes 人 the subject being described and changes the focus of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q6.kobun.tip: Do not add な after うつくしい because this is an い-adjective.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: しっかり is part of a fixed adverb; this part has no independent meaning when separated.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: り combines with しっか to form the adverb しっかり.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q7.kobun.why: しっかり is an adverb that modifies a verb. It often describes an action done seriously or firmly. This word usually keeps the same form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ちゃんと, the nuance is closer to doing something properly or completely.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with きちんと, it emphasizes being neat, orderly, or according to the rules.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t21-q7.kobun.tip: Do not translate しっかり with one fixed meaning; look at the following verb and choose the suitable meaning.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q1.kobun.vi: I am sad because I cannot meet my friend.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q1.kobun.sk: N に + negative potential V + なくて、 + Aいです
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the object of the action of meeting.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: 会える changes to the negative potential form 会えない, and then changes to なくて to connect the reason.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective さびしいです is the main predicate and expresses an emotion.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q1.kobun.why: 友だちに is the object of 会う. The clause 会えなくて comes first to give the reason, and then さびしいです states the emotion caused by that reason.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 会えないので, the cause-and-effect relationship is stated more clearly and formally.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 会えないのに, the meaning becomes “although I cannot meet my friend, ...,” showing a contrast.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q1.kobun.tip: Do not use 会わなくて when you mean that you cannot meet someone; 会えなくて expresses being unable to meet.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q2.kobun.vi: Thanks to you, I have gradually become used to my new job.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: おかげさまで is a polite expression that gives a positive reason and is often used to express gratitude.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the object or environment that the speaker gradually becomes used to.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: なれる means to become used to something, while てきました shows that the change has progressed up to the present.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q2.kobun.why: おかげさまで gives a positive reason, and 新しいしごとに is the object of なれる. なれてきました describes the process of gradually becoming used to something from the past until now.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with なれていきます, it emphasizes that the process will continue to develop in the future.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with なれました, it only says that the person has become used to it, without emphasizing the gradual process.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q2.kobun.tip: The verb なれる goes with に, not with を as in the way this idea is expressed in Vietnamese.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q3.kobun.vi: The family next door is having a loud argument.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject carrying out the action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows the method or manner in which an action is performed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: けんかしています is the noun けんか combined with する in the ています form to describe an action in progress.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q3.kobun.why: となりのかぞくが is the subject, and 大きなこえで states the manner of arguing. ています shows that the action is happening at the time of speaking.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with けんかしました, it only says that they argued, without the meaning that it is still happening.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 話しています, it means that someone is speaking loudly, not necessarily arguing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q3.kobun.tip: で shows the manner here, not a place; do not translate 大きなこえで as “in a loud voice.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q3.kobun.cn: N + する → Nしています
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q4.kobun.vi: I have a habit of waking up at 6 o’clock every morning.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person whose habit is being discussed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the time when the action おきる is performed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies the noun しゅうかん.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the subject that exists in the pattern あります.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: あります expresses the existence or possession of an object or matter.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q4.kobun.why: The clause おきる comes before しゅうかん to modify “habit.” に marks the time, while が marks what exists in the sentence using あります.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used here, the sentence means “sometimes do something,” not having a fixed habit.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q4.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use を with a time expression, but the time when an action is performed usually goes with に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q5.kobun.vi: After reading the letter, I was very surprised.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object being read.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 読んで is the て form, connecting the action of reading with the result or reaction that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: This phrase is the main predicate and describes the reaction after reading the letter.
