default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q5.kobun.why: The object てがみを comes before the verb 読んで. The て form connects the earlier action with the later reaction, so the sentence shows the sequence of reading the letter and then being surprised.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used here, the meaning is still “after reading,” but it emphasizes the period after the action more clearly.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q5.kobun.tip: Do not translate the て form mechanically as “and”; in this sentence, it also shows the order of events.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q6.kobun.vi: The old man from the house next door has passed away.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects a location word with the noun いえ.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects いえ with the noun おじいさん, creating the phrase “the old man from the house next door.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the person who has the state described by the predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: This is the main predicate; なくなる in the polite past form expresses passing away.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q6.kobun.why: The two phrases の connect となり with いえ and いえ with おじいさん, respectively, creating a chain of modifiers. おじいさんが is the subject, while なくなりました is the change in that subject’s state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used here, the basic meaning is still “died,” but the expression is more direct and less gentle.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t22-q6.kobun.tip: Do not translate each の mechanically as “of”; combine them into the phrase “the old man from the house next door.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q1.kobun.vi: We discussed it together and then gave flowers to the teacher.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the people who perform the action together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: して is the て form of そうだんする, connecting the action of discussing with the action of giving.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the person who receives the gift.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the item being given.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: This is the main predicate and describes the action of giving a gift.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q1.kobun.why: みんなで shows the group acting together. The て form connects the earlier action of discussing with the action of giving; に is the recipient, and を is the gift.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is replaced with と, the meaning leans toward “with everyone” as the people doing the action together, without clearly emphasizing the manner of acting together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q1.kobun.tip: English learners may easily reverse に and を, but the recipient goes with に, while the item being given goes with を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q2.kobun.vi: What will you give to celebrate your friend's wedding?
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 友だち with けっこん, showing the friend's wedding.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects けっこん with おいわい, creating the phrase “wedding celebration gift”.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows the purpose or occasion for giving a gift.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the gift being given, and 何 is the question word for that gift.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: This is the main predicate in the polite question form, asking about the action of giving.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q2.kobun.why: The two phrases の are placed one after another to narrow the meaning from “friend” to “wedding” and then to “celebration.” に shows the occasion or purpose, while 何を is the object asked about in the action of あげますか.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If おいわいに is replaced with 結婚式に, the question refers more specifically to the wedding occasion and does not stress the purpose of celebrating.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q2.kobun.tip: You must distinguish に, which shows the occasion or purpose, from を, which shows the item being given.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q3.kobun.vi: Who will you invite to the wedding?
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に shows the event that the invited person will attend.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the person being invited.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb しょうたいします combines with か to form a polite question.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q3.kobun.why: けっこんしきに states the event, だれを is the person being invited, and しょうたいしますか forms the question predicate. The particle を is used because だれ is the direct object of しょうたいします.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If を is replaced with が, the sentence asks who performs the inviting, not whom to invite.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse に and を: に is connected with the event one is invited to, while を is connected with the person being invited.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q4.kobun.vi: The children were very happy when they received their favorite sweets.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes 子ども the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the food received; すきな modifies おかし.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て of もらう connects the action of receiving with the happy state in the next clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The form ていました expresses a state that was continuing in the past.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q4.kobun.why: 子どもは states the subject being described, and すきなおかしを is the thing received. The form て connects the action of receiving with the happy state, creating a sequence of first the action and then the state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is used, the sentence stresses that whenever the children receive sweets, becoming happy happens as a natural result.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If ので is used, the sentence stresses that receiving sweets is the reason the children became happy.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate て as a fixed linking word, but here て naturally connects two events that happen one after another.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the content that is said.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 言いました is the polite past form of 言う.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q5.kobun.why: おれいを is the content of the speaking action, while 言いました is the main predicate at the end of the sentence. The particle を shows that thanks are what was said.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is used with a quotation, the sentence gives the exact words “thank you” instead of referring generally to thanks.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may omit を before 言う, but a noun showing the content of speech usually goes with を when the exact words are not quoted.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q6.kobun.vi: My father gave me a novel.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the person who performs the giving action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the thing being given.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: くれました shows that another person does something for the speaker or gives something to the speaker.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q6.kobun.why: 父が is the giver, しょうせつを is the thing given, and くれました shows that the thing is given toward the speaker. This order places the giver before the thing received and ends with the giving verb.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If もらいました is used, the speaker becomes the receiver and 父に marks the giver.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If あげました is used, the sentence only says that the father gave something to another person, without showing that the gift was given to the speaker.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse あげる and くれる; くれる is used when another person gives something to the speaker or toward the speaker.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t23-q6.kobun.cn: N が + N を + くれる
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q1.kobun.vi: I want to score 80 points or higher on the next test.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: つぎの modifies テスト, identifying it as the upcoming test.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で shows the situation or activity in which the score is produced.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: This quantity phrase is the score goal of とりたい.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The form たい of とる expresses the speaker's desire.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q1.kobun.cn: Vます-removeます + たいです
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q1.kobun.why: つぎの modifies テスト, テストで shows the test-taking context, ８０てんいじょう is the goal, and とりたいです ends with the desire to achieve the score. The particle で is suitable because the score is produced in a test.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If と思います is added, the desire is expressed more softly and cautiously.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If とらなければなりません is used instead, the meaning changes from desire to the duty to achieve the score.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use に instead of で, but で here only shows the context in which the test takes place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q2.kobun.vi: Because school is far away, I try to get up early and leave home every morning.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the adjective とおい.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason clause with the main clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: This is a time phrase showing when the action usually happens.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: なるべく modifies はやく and shows the degree of effort.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective はやい changes to the -く form to modify the verb 出ます.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the place one leaves in the use of 出る.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: 出ます is the main predicate and describes the action of leaving home.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q2.kobun.why: The reason clause comes before ので, while the main action comes after the comma. なるべく modifies はやく, and を marks the place where leaving begins with 出る.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から keeps almost the same reason meaning but makes the tone more direct and subjective.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use に with うち, but a place one leaves with 出る usually goes with を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q2.kobun.cn: Aい・V普通形・Nな + ので
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q3.kobun.vi: If 59 is added to 41, it becomes 100.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the number used as the base for adding another number.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the number being added.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects a condition with a natural or necessary result.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: に shows the result reached in the structure Nになる.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: なります is the predicate and describes the result of the calculation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q3.kobun.why: The starting number goes with に, the number added goes with を, and と connects the calculation with its necessary result. The result 100 goes with に before なる to show a change into a value.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Using たら emphasizes a hypothetical condition more, while と suits a result that always occurs when the calculation is performed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q3.kobun.tip: Do not confuse に and を: the base number goes with に, while the number added goes with を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q4.kobun.vi: I listened to a lecture by a famous teacher.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: ゆうめいな directly modifies the noun 先生.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 先生 with the noun こうぎ and shows possession or a related connection.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the lecture as the object being heard.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 聞きました is the predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q4.kobun.why: The adjective な comes before the noun and takes な to modify 先生. The phrase 先生のこうぎ forms a complete object before を, followed by the verb 聞きました.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: This structure emphasizes a lecture given or presented by the teacher, rather than simply a lecture related to the teacher.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q4.kobun.tip: With an adjective ending in な, keep な before the noun, but do not use な directly before の.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q4.kobun.cn: Aな + な + N; N + の + N
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q5.kobun.vi: I will practice as hard as I can.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase acts as an adverb and modifies the action of practicing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: れんしゅうします is the main predicate in the polite form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q5.kobun.why: An adverb of manner comes before a verb to show how an action is performed. れんしゅうします ends the sentence and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: The form with に can also act as an adverb, but this form is more common in writing or when the adverbial function needs to be made clear.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q5.kobun.tip: Do not translate 一生懸命 as a separate noun; in this sentence, it directly modifies the verb.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q6.kobun.vi: I asked my senior about school.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the person who is asked in the use of 伺う.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 学校 with こと, forming a phrase about matters related to school.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: こと nominalizes the content being asked about, while を marks that content as the object of 伺いました.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: うかがいました is the honorific predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q6.kobun.why: The person asked goes with に, while the content being asked about is formed with 学校のこと and marked by を. 伺いました comes at the end of the sentence as the predicate and shows respectful speech.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: 学校について asks directly about the topic of school, while 学校のこと has a more natural and broader meaning about things related to school.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q6.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use を for the person being asked, but with 伺う, the listener or person being asked usually goes with に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q6.kobun.cn: N の + こと; N に + V
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the first part of the adverb とうとう, which modifies the event being mentioned.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: This part combines with とう before it to form the adverb とうとう.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q7.kobun.why: とうとう is an adverb showing that an event finally happened after a period of waiting or progress. Because the sentence contains only this vocabulary item, it has no accompanying predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: ついに also means finally, but it often emphasizes an achieved result or an event that happened after a long time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t24-q7.kobun.tip: Do not confuse とうとう with たまたま; とうとう refers to the final result, while たまたま means by chance.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q1.kobun.vi: I overslept, so I arrived late for class.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: て connects the action of oversleeping with the result of being late for class.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the object or event that the speaker is late for.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q1.kobun.why: The first clause states the cause or an earlier action, and the main clause then states the result. The particle に marks the event that the speaker is late for.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ので, the cause-and-effect relationship becomes clearer and more polite.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q1.kobun.tip: English learners may easily confuse に and へ; with 遅刻する, the event that someone is late for usually goes with に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q2.kobun.vi: I said “I am leaving” to my family and went out.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: と marks the content of what was said.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 言って uses the て form to connect the action of speaking with the action of going out.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q2.kobun.why: The listener is marked by に, while the spoken words are placed in quotation marks and connected with と. The て form links the two actions in the order of speaking first and then going out.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with と言いながら, the two actions are understood to happen at the same time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q2.kobun.tip: English learners may easily omit と after the quoted content, but と is a required particle before 言う.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q3.kobun.vi: On rainy days, I could not play soccer, so it was a shame.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the rainy day the topic and setting of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the activity that cannot be done.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: できなくて is the negative linking form and states the reason for the feeling of regret.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q3.kobun.why: は sets the general setting, while が marks playing soccer as an activity that cannot be done. なくて connects the reason with the regretful comment at the end of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If できなくては is used, the sentence has a conditional or critical nuance rather than simply stating a cause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q3.kobun.tip: English learners may confuse が with を in the pattern できる; for ability, が is usually used to mark what can or cannot be done.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q4.kobun.vi: If I do something bad, my father scolds me severely.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the action performed in the conditional clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: すると connects the condition with the result that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: In a passive sentence, に indicates the person who performs the action affecting the subject.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: きびしく is an adverbial form that modifies the action of scolding.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: しかられました is the polite past form of a passive verb.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q4.kobun.why: と shows the result that usually occurs when the condition is fulfilled. The main clause uses the passive form, so the affected person is understood as the subject, and the father is marked by に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with たら, the condition becomes more specifically hypothetical instead of showing a usual result.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q4.kobun.tip: English learners may understand に as the receiver in every case, but in a passive sentence, に usually indicates the person who causes the action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q5.kobun.vi: When I was young, I liked swimming.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: とき indicates the time when the state or event in the main clause was true.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object of liking in the pattern すきだ.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: すきでした is an な adjective in the polite past form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q5.kobun.why: The time phrase is placed at the beginning of the sentence to give the setting. With すきだ, the thing liked goes with が, while でした shows that the preference belonged to the past.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 子どものころ, the meaning is still childhood, but it does not focus on a specific time or period as とき does.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q5.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use を with すき, but the standard pattern is Nがすきです.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: でも broadens the range and means that anyone can perform the action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: こと nominalizes the verb, while が marks using as something that can be done.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q6.kobun.why: The verb is nominalized with こと to become the content of ability. The pattern ことができる expresses that someone can do something, while でも emphasizes that there is no limit on who can use it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If the potential form is used instead, the sentence is shorter but does not clearly emphasize the action as the structure ことができる does.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily conjugate the verb right before ことができる; before こと, the dictionary form must be used.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t25-q6.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + ことができる
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q1.kobun.vi: I received change from the staff member, but it was 20 yen short.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q1.kobun.sk: N に + N を + Vました が + Quantity + Vませんでした
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the person who gives the change.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the thing received.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: もらいました is the polite past form of もらう; が connects to the following clause with a contrasting meaning.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The quantity phrase is the subject of the state of being short.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: 足りませんでした is the polite past negative form of 足りる.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q1.kobun.why: The person who gives the money is marked by に, while the change is the object of もらう, so it takes を. が connects two contrasting clauses: I received the change, but the amount was still not enough.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: It can replace が to connect contrasting ideas, but its meaning is more complete and formal.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: It also expresses a polite past state of being insufficient, but its auxiliary-verb conjugation is different from 足りませんでした.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を after a person's name, but with もらう, the giver usually takes に and the thing received takes を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q1.kobun.cn: Vます + が、 + Vます・Vません・Vました・Vませんでした
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q2.kobun.vi: Please choose your favorite color from these.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun and modifies that noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: で defines the range used for comparison or selection.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: いちばん modifies an adjective and gives it a superlative meaning within the range.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: すきな uses the form な to modify the noun いろ directly.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the chosen color.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: えらんで is the て form, which connects with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: ください follows the て form of a verb to ask the listener to do something.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q2.kobun.why: この中で limits the range of choice, and then いちばんすきな modifies いろ. The verb えらぶ takes を because the color is the object being chosen, and then てください is used to make a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If の中から is used, the focus is on choosing something from inside a specific group.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence becomes a more polite and softer request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use すきいろ; the adjective な must keep な when it comes before a noun: すきな いろ.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q3.kobun.vi: That shirt looks nice, doesn't it? It suits you very well.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: その modifies the noun シャツ.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The noun is made the topic through a pause in intonation, even though the particle は is omitted.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: いい is the predicate evaluating the shirt; ね is used to seek agreement.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: とても modifies the state にあっています.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: ています expresses a state that is currently effective; よ emphasizes the information being told to the listener.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q3.kobun.why: The first sentence evaluates the shirt, while the second uses に to show the person whom the shirt suits. The adverb とても comes before the predicate to increase the degree, while ています emphasizes the current suitable state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, it means that it seems it will suit someone or seems to look suitable, without making a firm statement.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This expression only gives a general comment that it suits someone; it does not emphasize a continuing state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q3.kobun.tip: 似合う goes with に to show the person or thing that the clothing suits, and it does not use を as with verbs for wearing or looking.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q3.kobun.cn: Vて + いる + です・ます・よ
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q4.kobun.vi: I put on a hat and tried looking at myself in the mirror.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the thing worn on the head.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects putting on the hat with the following action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で shows the means or place where the looking action occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 見てみる expresses trying the action of looking; みました puts the action into the polite past.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q4.kobun.why: ぼうしをかぶる is the first action, connected to the following action with the て form. かがみで shows the means, which is the mirror, while 見てみました shows that the speaker tried looking.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vている is used, the sentence describes an action or state in progress, without emphasizing the meaning of trying.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vておく is used, it means doing something beforehand to prepare for what comes later.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q4.kobun.tip: Do not confuse で with に: で shows a means such as a mirror, while に usually shows a destination or an object.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q5.kobun.vi: That store is open every day.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: あの modifies the noun 店.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the store the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The time phrase comes before the predicate to show the time or frequency of the activity.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: えいぎょう is a noun that describes an activity, and it combines with しています to form the predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: しています expresses an activity that continues regularly or is still in progress.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q5.kobun.why: The store is made the topic by は, and then 每日 shows the frequency of its activity. えいぎょう combines with する, and the form しています expresses that the store continues operating.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes that the store is open every day, not its business activity.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If 営業します is used, the sentence only describes a habit or schedule and emphasizes continuation less.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q5.kobun.tip: Activity nouns usually combine with する; a noun is not connected directly to います.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q5.kobun.cn: N + する → Nをしています・Nしています
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q6.kobun.vi: This computer is made in Japan.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the computer the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: This part is the predicate and states the computer's attribute or origin.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q6.kobun.why: この modifies パソコン, and then は makes パソコン the topic. にほんせいです serves as the predicate and states the topic's characteristic.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence emphasizes that the computer was made in Japan.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t26-q6.kobun.tip: Do not understand は as a word with its own meaning such as “is”; here, は only marks the topic.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q1.kobun.vi: The bread sold at this store is very soft.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows the place where the selling action takes place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause うっている comes before パン to modify the bread.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は makes パン, the modified noun, the topic.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: とても modifies the degree of やわらかい.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: やわらかいです is an adjective predicate that describes the bread.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q1.kobun.why: この店でうっている is a relative clause placed before パン to identify which type of bread it is. After the topic パンは, とても modifies the adjective やわらかい at the end of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with この店のパン, the sentence is shorter and only refers to this shop's bread, without emphasizing the action of selling.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q1.kobun.tip: A modifying clause in Japanese always comes before the noun, unlike the usual word order in Vietnamese.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q2.kobun.vi: No matter how much I scold him, my son does not eat vegetables.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: いくら states how great the degree of the following action is.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb しかる changes to the て form and then connects with も to express concession.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は indicates that むすこ is the topic of the main clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks vegetables as the object of eating.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: 食べません is a negative predicate in the present tense.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q2.kobun.why: いくらしかっても is a concessive clause placed before the main clause. In the main clause, は states the topic, and を marks the food affected by 食べる.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes that even increasing the amount of scolding does not change the result.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with しかると, the sentence expresses a condition or a natural result, and no longer means “even if I scold him.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use ても with the dictionary form such as しかるても; the verb must first change to the て form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q3.kobun.vi: Because I am full, I cannot eat everything.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of the state of being full.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: なので connects the reason to the following clause; いっぱい identifies な before ので.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ぜんぶ modifies the action 食べる and refers to the entire amount.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: の turns 食べる into a noun meaning the act of eating, while は makes that act the topic.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: むりです serves as the predicate and states that eating everything is impossible.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q3.kobun.why: The clause おなかがいっぱいなので gives the cause before the result. 食べるのは nominalizes the act of eating and makes it the topic to be evaluated with むりです.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If なので is replaced with から, the reason sounds more direct and conversational, while なので sounds softer and more explanatory.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If むりです is replaced with 食べられません, the sentence emphasizes that eating is impossible because of ability or the actual situation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q3.kobun.tip: With nouns and な adjectives, use な before ので: いっぱいなので, not いっぱいので.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・なAな・Nな + ので
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は indicates the type of milk being commented on.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: へんな modifies あじ and describes the quality of the taste.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks taste as the sensation that appears in the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: します combines with あじが to express a sensation or taste that is perceived.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q4.kobun.why: このぎゆうにゅうは makes the type of milk the topic. へんな modifies あじ, while あじがします expresses the strange taste perceived from the milk.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 味がある, it means that it has a flavor in general, without emphasizing the sensation being noticed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with おいしい, the sentence only evaluates it as tasty and does not state the specific quality of the taste.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q4.kobun.tip: For sensations or tastes, Japanese usually uses Nがします instead of translating each word as “N does.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the restaurant is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb in the ていました form describes a state that existed in the past.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q5.kobun.why: The topic レストランは comes first, followed by a predicate that describes the restaurant's state. The particle は makes the restaurant the subject being commented on.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If written in kanji, the meaning does not change; only the way it is written記 is different.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 混みました, the sentence emphasizes becoming crowded, not the state of already being crowded.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate は as “is,” but here は only marks the topic “restaurant.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: に turns いっしょ into an adverb describing the manner of doing an action together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks しょくじ as the object of the action します.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: しましょう is a form used to suggest doing an action together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q6.kobun.why: いっしょに comes first to show the manner, while しょくじを is the object of します. The ましょう form at the end creates an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 食べましょう, the sentence directly says “let's eat,” while しょくじをしましょう emphasizes having a meal.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q6.kobun.tip: Do not translate しょくじをします mechanically as “do a meal”; this phrase means “have a meal.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The two repeated parts combine to form the adverb そろそろ, which describes an approaching time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q7.kobun.why: そろそろ is an adverb that usually comes before a verb to signal that an action is about to happen or that it is time to do it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: もうすぐ also means “soon,” but it usually emphasizes the very short period before something happens.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t27-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use そろそろ as a verb, but it is an adverb modifying the following action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q1.kobun.vi: Dinner is ready, so let's eat.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ばんごはん with したく and shows that the preparation belongs to dinner.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks したく as the subject in a completed state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: から connects the reason to the following clause; できました expresses that the preparation has been completed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 食べましょう is a suggestion to eat together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q1.kobun.why: ばんごはんのしたくが is the subject of できました. This clause comes before から to give the reason, and then 食べましょう gives a suitable suggestion.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with ので, the reason is expressed more softly and objectively.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q1.kobun.tip: Do not confuse が with を: したくが できる means “the preparation has been completed,” not “prepare to make something.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q1.tokens.5.m: let's eat, let's have a meal
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q1.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + から
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q2.kobun.vi: Let's reserve the restaurant that we will go to tomorrow.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q2.kobun.sk: Time + V普通形 + N の + N を + Vます + ましょう
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: あした indicates the time related to the action of going to the restaurant.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 行く comes before レストラン to modify it and identify the restaurant we will go to tomorrow.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects レストラン with よやく, forming the phrase “the restaurant reservation.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks よやく as the object of します.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: しましょう expresses a suggestion to make the reservation together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q2.kobun.why: あした行く is a clause modifying レストラン, so it comes directly before that noun. Then レストランのよやくを forms the object of しましょう.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence means “let's go to the restaurant tomorrow,” and no longer emphasizes making a reservation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q2.kobun.tip: A modifying clause in Japanese comes before the noun, so we do not say レストランを行くあした.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q3.kobun.vi: Because I will drink coffee, please boil some water for me.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks コーヒー as the object of the action of drinking.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason to the request in the following clause; 飲みます keeps the polite form before から.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks おゆ as the object to be boiled.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: てください connects form て with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q3.kobun.why: Clause 飲みますから gives the reason first, while おゆをわかしてください is the main request. Each verb has its own object, so コーヒーを and おゆを both use を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with ので, the reason sounds softer and less direct.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence becomes “May I boil the water?”, so it is no longer a request for someone else to do it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit ください after form て, but わかしてください is needed to complete the meaning “please boil it for me”.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q3.kobun.cn: Vます形・V普通形 ＋ から; Vて ＋ ください
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q4.kobun.vi: A: A hamburger and coffee, please. B: Yes, I understand.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: と connects two items included in the order.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: This noun continues the list of ordered items and is combined with the previous item using と.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: おねがいします is used at the end of a sentence to make a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: かしこまりました is a very polite response used when a staff member accepts a request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q4.kobun.why: Two nouns are connected by と to make a list of ordered items. おねがいします is placed at the end of the sentence to turn the list into a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with ください still makes a request, but the tone is more direct.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit と when listing two items, but in this sentence と is needed to connect the two nouns.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q4.kobun.cn: N＋と＋N。; おねがいします
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks this restaurant as the topic being described.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: すいています describes the state of a dining place having few customers.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q5.kobun.why: The sentence makes the place the topic first, then states its condition using すいています. Form ています here describes an ongoing state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 混んでいます, the meaning changes to “the restaurant is crowded.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q5.kobun.tip: すいています does not mean that the food is cheap; in a restaurant context, this word refers to the state of having few customers.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q6.kobun.vi: I cut the vegetables into small pieces.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the vegetables as the object affected by the cutting action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: こまかく is the adverbial form of adjective こまかい and modifies how the cutting was done.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: きりました is the polite past form of きる and states the main action of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q6.kobun.cn: Aい omit い ＋ く ＋ V; Vます omit ます ＋ ました
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q6.kobun.why: The vegetables come before を because they are the object being cut. Adjective こまかい changes to form こまかく to modify how the action is performed, and the past-tense verb comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: 小さく can also be used here, but it emphasizes small size rather than being finely chopped or detailed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q6.kobun.tip: When an adjective ending in い is changed into an adverb, い must change to く; こまかいきりました cannot be used directly.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q7.kobun.why: This is a standalone vocabulary item, not a sentence with a particle or grammar pattern. This word often appears in structures such as 旅行の準備をする.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t28-q7.kobun.tip: You need to remember the complete reading じゅんび, rather than guessing the reading of each character from its Chinese-based sound.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q1.kobun.vi: I am looking for an apartment with rent of 50,000 yen or less.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q1.kobun.sk: N が ＋ Amount 以下の ＋ N を ＋ Vて ＋ います
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the rent as a feature used to identify the apartment.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: いかの modifies アパート and shows that the rent does not exceed 50,000 yen.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the apartment as the object being searched for.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: さがして is the て form and connects the verb to います to express an ongoing action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: います completes the pattern Vている and shows that the search is continuing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q1.kobun.cn: Quantity・N ＋ 以下の ＋ N; Vて ＋ いる
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q1.kobun.why: The phrase ５万円いかのアパート is a clause that modifies the noun アパート. The apartment is marked with を because it is the object of さがしています, while form ている shows that the search is still continuing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 以上の, the meaning changes to an apartment with rent of 50,000 yen or more.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: までの also indicates an upper limit, but usually emphasizes a range up to a certain level.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place いか after the main noun, but in a noun-modifying phrase, いかの must come before アパート.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q2.kobun.vi: Because the window broke, I had someone repair it for me.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the window as the object that entered a broken state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: われてしまった describes a completed event with a regrettable feeling, while ので connects the cause and the result.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: なおして is the て form and connects the repair action to pattern もらう to express receiving help.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: もらいました shows that the speaker received help repairing the window.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q2.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first and is connected by ので, followed by the result. なおしてもらいました combines form て with もらう to show that the speaker benefited from the repair.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is more subjective and direct.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If なおしてもらいました is replaced with なおしました, the meaning becomes that the speaker repaired it personally.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q2.kobun.tip: Vてしまう does not only mean that something was completed; in this sentence, it also expresses regret that the window broke.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q2.tokens.5.m: had someone do it for me
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q2.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ しまう; V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので; Vて ＋ もらう
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q3.kobun.vi: Because today is my birthday, I will decorate the table with flowers.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は states that today is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: なので connects the cause and the result and means because.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle に indicates the place where an object is placed or decorated.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: Particle を marks the object being decorated.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The polite present-tense verb expresses an intended or future action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q3.kobun.why: The sentence gives the topic first, then states the reason using なので. The location goes with に, while the affected object goes with を before verb かざります.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If なので is replaced with から, the meaning of the reason is almost unchanged, but the wording is more direct and subjective.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を for a place, but a place where an object is placed or decorated usually goes with に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ ので
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q4.kobun.vi: I hung the calendar on the classroom wall.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects noun きょうしつ to the following noun to modify it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle に indicates the location where the object is hung.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle を marks the object being hung.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: かけました is the polite past form of かける and indicates a completed action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q4.kobun.why: Phrase きょうしつのかべ identifies the wall as belonging to the classroom. The hung object goes with を, while the hanging location goes with に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used instead of に, the sentence describes where the hanging action takes place rather than emphasizing the object's position.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse に and で; for an object placed, hung, or attached to a location, に usually indicates that destination or location.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q5.kobun.vi: I hear that this city is safe.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks this city as the topic being described.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: だ is the ending form of the adjective な あんぜん when it comes before そうだ to report information.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: そうです shows information that the speaker heard or received from another source.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q5.kobun.why: The quality あんぜんだ forms the reported content. そうです is placed at the end of the sentence to show that this is hearsay, not the speaker's direct assertion.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it expresses a prediction based on appearance, そうです means looks safe instead of is said to be safe.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: ようです expresses a judgment based on evidence or feeling, not simply reported information that was heard.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q5.kobun.tip: With the adjective な and nouns, だ must be kept before そうだ in the reported form of speech聞.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ ＋ そうだ
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q6.kobun.vi: I threw away the old notebook.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective い comes before a noun to modify ノト.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the thing being thrown away.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb すてました is in the polite past form and shows that the action was completed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q6.kobun.why: 古い comes before ノト to describe the notebook. The notebook is the direct object of the action, so it takes を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 捨てない, the sentence becomes negative and means not throwing away the notebook.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put an adjective after a noun, but Japanese puts an adjective before the noun it modifies.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: This is the ending that forms the verb かたづける.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q7.kobun.why: This is a dictionary-form verb presented independently, without clause parts or particles attached.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: 片付く is an intransitive verb, meaning to become clean or tidy, while かたづける means to clean or arrange something actively.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t29-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse the transitive verb かたづける with the intransitive verb 片付く.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vi: Because there are many cars here, the air is especially bad.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the place being discussed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject that is said to be numerous.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the cause to the result and has a softer explanatory tone than から.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: に turns 特 into an adverb modifying the adjective わるい.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the subject that has the bad quality.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: わるいです is the polite form of the adjective predicate い.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q1.kobun.why: ここは sets the place as the topic, and then 車が多いので states the cause. The main clause 空気がわるいです states the result, while 特に emphasizes the degree of badness.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the sentence still means that the air is bad because there are many cars, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で instead of ので, but ので must follow the plain form to connect the cause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: その comes before 青 to identify the color or object being mentioned.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects 青 with ボタン, forming the phrase “blue button”.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks ボタン as the object being pressed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: おして is the て form of おす, and it connects with ください to form a request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: ください makes the request polite.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q10.kobun.why: その and 青の identify the object and then the color of ボタン, respectively. ボタンを is the emphasized object, while おして ください is the polite request pattern.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 青いボタン is used, it still means “blue button,” but 青い directly modifies ボタン and does not use の.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily say 青のいボタン; they need to choose one of the two structures, 青のボタン or 青いボタン.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q11.kobun.vi: I went to the supermarket to buy food.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle へ indicates the direction of movement.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks 食料 as what is bought.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: 買う changes to the continuative form and combines with に to show purpose.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q11.kobun.why: スーパーへ indicates the destination, and 食料を is what needs to be bought. 買いに行きました shows that the purpose of going is to buy food.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 買って行きました is used, it means that the speaker bought it and then took it away, without emphasizing the purpose of going to buy it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place に after 食料, but に in 買いに行く must attach to the verb's continuative form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the place or position where the content is written.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks 解答 as the content being written.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: 書いてください uses the て form with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q12.kobun.why: ここに indicates the place receiving the action, while 解答を indicates the content to be written. The て form plus ください creates a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If ここに is replaced with ここで, it means writing here, emphasizing the place where the action takes place rather than where the content is written.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で because of the habit of translating it as “here,” but に is more suitable for the place where the written result is put.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the bus as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: もう modifies the action and shows that the departure has already happened.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: 出発する is changed into the polite past form 出発しました.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q13.kobun.why: バスは sets the topic first, and then もう adds that it has already happened. 出発しました is the main predicate and uses the polite past form to describe a completed action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used in this sentence, the meaning changes to the bus has not left yet.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget that 出発 is a noun combined with する, so they must say 出発しました instead of directly conjugating 出発.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents this room as the topic being described.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: 暗い is a い-ending adjective used as the predicate; です keeps the polite tone.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q14.kobun.why: このへやは brings the object being discussed to the front. 暗い directly serves as the predicate describing the quality, and です is added to make the sentence polite.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used in this sentence, the meaning changes to this room is not dark.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q14.kobun.tip: With a い-ending adjective, do not add な before です.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q15.kobun.vi: I do not have anything in particular that I want to eat.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: 特に is an adverb. It modifies the desire to eat and is often used in negative sentences to mean “anything in particular.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q15.kobun.ch.1.vi: as for what I want to eat
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause 食べたい modifies もの, while は marks the whole phrase as the topic.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: ありません is the polite negative form of あります. It is the predicate showing nonexistence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q15.kobun.cn: Vます-remove ます ＋ たい
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q15.kobun.why: 食べたい comes before もの to create a clause that modifies a noun, like “something I want to eat.” This noun phrase is marked as the topic by は, while ありません negates its existence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If it replaces this part of the sentence, the meaning emphasizes not wanting to eat anything at all, rather than simply not having anything special to eat.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q15.kobun.tip: English learners may easily understand 食べたいもの as an independent sentence; in fact, 食べたい directly modifies もの.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: もう modifies 一度, creating the meaning “one more time.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 一度 indicates the number of times the speaking action is performed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: ゆっくり modifies 言って and shows how the speaking is done.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 言って is the て form of 言う. It connects the verb to ください to make a request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: ください follows a verb in the て form to express a polite favor or request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q2.kobun.why: もう一度 specifies the number of requests, ゆっくり shows how to perform the action, and 言ってください creates a polite request. The て form connects directly to ください.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If 一度 is replaced with 一回, the meaning is almost unchanged, but the expression is more casual and conversational.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q2.kobun.tip: English learners may easily forget that the verb must change to the て form before ください.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vi: I will collect the tests now.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: これから indicates the starting point of an action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the test as the object being collected.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 集めます is the polite form of the verb predicate 集める.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q3.kobun.why: これから sets the time before the action, テストを is the affected object, and 集めます ends the sentence and states the action that will be performed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 集めます is replaced with 集まります, the meaning changes to the tests or people gathering by themselves, not collecting something.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q3.kobun.tip: English learners may confuse 集める, a transitive verb that needs を, with 集まる, an intransitive verb that usually goes with が.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vi: There is a Japanese test tomorrow.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q4.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N の ＋ N が ＋ あります
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: あした indicates the time when the test exists.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 日本語 with the noun 試験 and shows what type of test it is.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the existing thing as a Japanese test.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is an existence predicate for things or events.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q4.kobun.why: あした sets the time, 日本語の modifies 試験, and 試験が あります expresses the existence of an event.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If あります is replaced with います, the sentence sounds unnatural because います is used for people or animals, while a test is an event.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q4.kobun.tip: English learners may translate both あります and います as “there is,” so remember that あります is used for things and events.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vi: The teacher is still in the classroom.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the teacher is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: まだ modifies います and shows that the state is continuing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the place where the teacher is present.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: います is an existence predicate for people or animals.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q5.kobun.why: 先生は is the topic, 教室に indicates the place of existence, and まだいます shows that the teacher has not left that place. The particle に is used with an existence verb to indicate a location.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If まだ is replaced with もう, the sentence means that the teacher was or has been there, without emphasizing a continuing state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q5.kobun.tip: English learners may use で with います, but a place of existence must go with に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vi: Please do not enter the dangerous place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: きけんな comes before 場所 to modify the noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the destination of the action 入る.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 入らないで is a negative form connected to ください to ask the listener not to perform the action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: ください completes the polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q6.kobun.why: きけんな modifies 場所, 場所に indicates the destination, and 入らないでください asks the listener not to enter it. The verb 入る changes to the negative form ない before でください is added.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 入ってはいけません, the sentence becomes a stronger rule or prohibition instead of a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q6.kobun.tip: English learners may say 入らなくてください, but a request meaning “please do not” uses 入らないでください.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vi: I will go to meet my friend from high school.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The phrase の turns 高校時代 into a modifier for 友だち.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the object of the action 会う.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The continuative form of 会う combines with に to indicate purpose.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きます is the main predicate and describes going.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q7.kobun.why: The phrase 高校時代の modifies 友だち, and then に marks the person to be met. 会いに行きます describes going for the purpose of meeting a friend.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 会って行く, the meaning is going after meeting someone, rather than emphasizing going in order to meet someone.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q7.kobun.tip: English learners may use 会うを行く, but purpose must use the continuative form of the verb with に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vi: The store will close at 9 o’clock today.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q8.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N を ＋ Time に ＋ Vます
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states that today is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the closing action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the time when the action occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 閉めます is a transitive verb and takes お店を as its object.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q8.kobun.why: お店を is the object being closed, while 9時に indicates the closing time. The time expression comes before the predicate to clearly state when the action occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 閉まります is used, it means that the store closes by itself or is in a closed state, without emphasizing who performs the closing action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q8.kobun.tip: English learners may confuse 閉める and 閉まる; this sentence uses 閉める because there is an object marked by を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vi: Please take this medicine before the meal.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects しょくじ with 前, creating a phrase that indicates a time related to the meal.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the time before taking the medicine.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: この comes before a noun to identify something near the speaker or being pointed out.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks medicine as the object of 飲む.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: 飲む changes to the て form to connect with ください and make a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: ください comes after the て form to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q9.kobun.why: しょくじの前に sets a time before the main action. Medicine is the object of 飲む, and 飲んでください uses the て form to make a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 前に is replaced with 前で, it does not fit the time meaning “before eating”; で usually indicates a place or means.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit the particle の in しょくじの前に, but の is necessary to connect “meal” with “in front.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t3-q9.kobun.cn: Nの + Nに + Vて + ください
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q1.kobun.vi: Because it is dark here at night, it is scary.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states the place being described.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: よる indicates the time when the dark state is being discussed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: くらいですから uses the polite form of a reason clause and connects it to the following result with から.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: こわいです is the main predicate and states the result of it being dark.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q1.kobun.why: ここは is the topic, while よる identifies the time. Clause くらいですから gives the reason first, and then clause こわいです gives the result.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with ので, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is softer and more objective.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily reverse the order of the reason and result as in Vietnamese, but Japanese usually places the reason clause before から or ので.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q1.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな + だ・N + だ + から
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q2.kobun.vi: The train has just arrived at the station.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject performing the state or action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: さっき indicates the time when the action occurred.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the destination of the verb つきました.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: つきました is the polite past-form predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q2.kobun.why: The subject comes before が, the time comes before the verb, and に indicates the destination of arriving at the station. The predicate comes at the end of the sentence and uses the past form to describe an action that has already happened.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with へ, the sentence still indicates the direction toward the station but emphasizes the direction more.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に as a time word and forget that に also marks a destination.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q3.kobun.vi: This seat is empty. Would you like to sit here?
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the seat whose state is being described.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: あいています describes the state of being empty, while から connects the reason to the following suggestion.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: すわりませんか uses a negative question form to make a gentle invitation or suggestion.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q3.kobun.why: The state of the seat is given first, and then から explains the reason for the invitation. すわりませんか comes at the end of the sentence to turn the suggestion into a polite question.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with ので, the reason sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand ています as meaning “is doing,” but here あいています describes the state of being empty.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q4.kobun.vi: Tokyo is crowded. In addition, the trains are packed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes Tokyo the topic of the first clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing being described as numerous.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 多いです is the い-ending adjective predicate in polite form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: それに adds information that supports the same point as the previous clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the train as the thing described in the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: こんでいます describes the train as being crowded.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q4.kobun.why: Each sentence has its own topic or subject, and the predicate comes at the end. それに connects the second clause as additional information that further explains the crowded situation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If そして is used, the sentence focuses more on a sequence of events than on adding another reason or feature.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit は after とうきょう, making the topic of the first clause unclear.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: 大きい comes before a noun to modify まち.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the large city the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks transportation as the thing being described.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: べんりです is the な-adjective predicate in polite form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q5.kobun.why: The adjective 大きい comes before まち to form a noun phrase, and then は makes this phrase the topic. こうつうがべんりです describes the topic with the structure N が Aなです.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 大きな is used, the meaning is still “large city,” but this is a special modifying form that comes before a noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake べんり for a い-ending adjective because its meaning ends with an i sound, but it is used as a な adjective.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q6.kobun.vi: The next bus will depart at 3 o’clock.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q6.kobun.sk: N は + Time に + Nします
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the next bus the topic.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the time when the bus departs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: しゅっぱつします is a present polite-form verb predicate that can indicate a future schedule.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q6.kobun.why: The bus topic is stated first, the time comes before the verb and goes with に. The present polite form of a verb is often used for schedules or fixed times.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with ごろ, the meaning becomes “around 3 o’clock” rather than exactly 3 o’clock.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で with time, but the specific time of an action usually uses に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q7.kobun.ch.0.vi: the beginning of the word meaning welcome
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: むか is the beginning of a vocabulary word, not an independent 文節 with its own meaning.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: える completes the dictionary form of the verb むかえる.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q7.kobun.why: This is a single word in dictionary form, so it has no particle or accompanying clause. The word is split into two parts for presentation, but when combined it must be read continuously as むかえる.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If it changes to むかえます, the meaning does not change, but the expression becomes polite.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t30-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily misread むかえる as a verb with the る ending from another group; they need to learn this word's conjugation as well.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q1.kobun.vi: Please move this luggage to the next room.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object being moved.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates where the object is moved.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: Vてください is used to ask or request the listener to do something.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q1.kobun.why: The object goes with を, while the destination goes with に. The verb in the て form combines with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used here, the sentence means “please do not move it,” which is opposite to the current request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse に, which indicates the destination, with で, which indicates the place where an action occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q2.kobun.vi: If you put the bag at the entrance, it will get in the way.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates where the bag is placed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the item being placed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary form of a verb combines with と to state a result that usually occurs under that condition.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: じゃまに adds the state expressed by なる.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: なります indicates a change into a state; よ emphasizes a reminder.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q2.kobun.why: The place where an item is put goes with に, and the item goes with を. The clause おくと states the condition, while じゃまになります describes the natural result.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use おいたら, the sentence focuses on a specific condition and does not stress an inevitable result as と does.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use で after a place when saying where an item is put; this structure requires に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q3.kobun.vi: It is broken, so please do not touch this door.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: ので connects the reason to the request in the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the object toward which the touching action is directed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: Vないでください is used to make a polite request not to perform an action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q3.kobun.why: The broken condition is given first as the reason, followed by a request not to touch it. The verb さわる uses に to mark the object affected.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason becomes slightly more direct and subjective.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q3.kobun.tip: With the verb る, the negative form is Vない; do not attach でください directly to the dictionary form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q4.kobun.vi: I received a travel souvenir from Mr. Tanaka.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person who gives something or the source from which it is received.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects noun りょこう with noun おみやげ to modify it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: もらいました is the polite past form of もらう.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q4.kobun.why: The giver goes with に, and the item received goes with を. The phrase りょこうのおみやげ forms a compound noun meaning a travel souvenir.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use あげる, the subject is the person who gives the item, and the direction of the action changes.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q4.kobun.tip: When using もらう, the giver usually goes with に, not the receiver.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q4.kobun.cn: N に ＋ N を ＋ もらう
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q5.kobun.vi: I have finished preparing the things I will take on the trip.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the purpose or occasion for carrying something.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause もって行く comes before もの to modify もの; は makes this phrase the topic.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: もう modifies よういしました and shows that the preparation is complete.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: よういしました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q5.kobun.why: The clause もって行くもの is a noun phrase in which the verb comes before もの to modify it. は makes the phrase for the things to take the topic, and the predicate states that they have been prepared.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use りょこうのためのもの, the sentence emphasizes items for the purpose of travel, which do not necessarily have to be carried.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q5.kobun.tip: In a clause that modifies a noun, the verb comes directly before the noun and does not take の.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形 ＋ N; Vて ＋ 行く
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q6.kobun.vi: Please do not make noise on the train.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates where the action takes place; の中 means inside.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: Vないでください is used to make a polite request not to do something.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q6.kobun.why: The place where the action takes place goes with で. The negative form さわがない combines with でください to make a reminder not to make noise.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use さわいではいけません, the sentence has a stronger prohibitive and more rule-like tone.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q6.kobun.tip: Do not confuse ないでください with ないで, because only ないでください forms a complete polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: い completes the い-ending adjective form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q7.kobun.why: This is an い-ending adjective used independently to describe a feature. The word remains in its dictionary form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: This is the kanji spelling of めずらしい, with the same meaning.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t31-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistake the final い for a particle, but here it belongs to the adjective.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q1.kobun.vi: Because of the snow, the train was late, so I was late too.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the cause that makes the following event happen.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the direct subject of the delayed state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the preceding cause or event with the following result.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects being late with しまいました to form a pattern expressing regret.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: てしまいました expresses something that happened unintentionally or regrettably.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q1.kobun.why: The cause is placed first with で, followed by the affected subject marked with が. The two actions are connected by て, while てしまいました emphasizes the regrettable result that occurred.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If ゆきで is replaced with ゆきだから, the sentence has a clearer and more direct reason-giving tone.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use only ちこくしました, the sentence only reports that the event happened and loses the sense of regret.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に to indicate a cause, but the cause in this sentence uses で.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q1.kobun.cn: Nで; Vて; Vてしまう
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q2.kobun.vi: While I was singing, I was warned that I was noisy.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q2.kobun.sk: N を ＋ Vている ＋ とき／たら、＋ 「文」と ＋ passive V
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the verb うたう.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: て combines with いたら to describe an action in progress.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: ていたら creates a time point or condition when another action occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: と marks the content of quoted speech or a quoted comment.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: されました is the polite past passive form of ちゅういする.
