default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q2.kobun.why: The object of singing goes with を, while ていたら sets the context of singing. The content of the warning is introduced by と before the passive verb ちゅういされました.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use うたっているとき, the sentence only states the time when I was singing and does not emphasize the condition that led to the warning.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with と言われました, the focus is on being told that it was noisy, not on being warned.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit と before the quoted content, but と is required to connect the quoted sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q2.kobun.cn: Vている ＋ とき; Vたら; 「文」と ＋ V受身
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q3.kobun.vi: Has the key that was lost yesterday been found yet?
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q3.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Vた ＋ N は ＋ もう ＋ Vますか
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: きのう modifies the action なくした and indicates the time when the loss occurred.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The usual past form なくした comes before a noun to modify かぎ.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the lost key the topic of the question.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: もう modifies the predicate and asks whether finding it has already happened.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: みつかる is an intransitive verb; its polite form combines with か to make a question.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q3.kobun.why: The clause きのうなくした comes before かぎ to identify which key. The topic is marked by は, and then もう comes before the predicate to ask whether the finding has been completed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use 見つけましたか, the question asks whether someone found the key; 見つかりましたか focuses on whether the key has been found.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with みつかる, but みつかる is an intransitive verb, so it does not take the object を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q3.kobun.cn: Vた + N; Vます + か
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q4.kobun.vi: I slipped on the stairs and hit my head.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where an action or event occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects the action of slipping with the following action of hitting one's head.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the body part affected by うつ.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: うちました is the polite past form of うつ.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q4.kobun.why: で states the place where the event occurred, and て connects two consecutive actions. あたまを is the part directly affected by the verb うつ.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use すべったから, the sentence means that the speaker hit their head because they slipped, emphasizing the cause more.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に to indicate where an action occurs, but the location of the action in this sentence uses で.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks the person who performs the action of apologizing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person who receives the apology.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: あやまりました is the polite past form of あやまる.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q5.kobun.why: The topic わたし is marked by は, while the person receiving the apology goes with に. The verb あやまる uses に to indicate the person being apologized to.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use に謝ってもらいました, it means that my friend apologized to me, reversing the person who performs the action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after あやまる, but the person being apologized to must go with に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q6.kobun.vi: While traveling, my bag was stolen.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: のとき indicates the time when the event occurred.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object affected by the action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: ぬすまれました is the polite past passive form. It shows that the speaker was affected by the bag being stolen.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q6.kobun.cn: Passive V: Vない → Vれる・られる; polite-form Vた → Vました
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q6.kobun.why: The phrase indicating time comes at the beginning of the sentence to give the situation. かばんを is the affected object, while the passive verb emphasizes the disadvantage caused to the speaker.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If the active form is used, it means that the speaker stole the bag, which is completely different from having their bag stolen.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is also passive, but it only says that the bag was taken; it does not necessarily emphasize the act of stealing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget that Japanese passive sentences often use を for the affected object and clearly express the disadvantage to the speaker.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the first sound of the word げんいん; because the question contains only one word, it has no separate grammatical role.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: This is the last sound of the word げんいん; the whole word means cause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q7.kobun.why: This is an independent word, so there is no sentence structure or particle to analyze. The word is kept in two parts to meet the segmentation requirement, but grammatically it must still be understood as one vocabulary unit.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t32-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily misread げんいん as げんえん; pronounce the sound い clearly between the two parts.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q1.kobun.vi: This restaurant is delicious, so please be sure to go.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this restaurant the topic of the comment.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: ですから connects the reason to the advice that follows; から means because.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: ぜひ modifies the invitation and shows that the speaker strongly wants the listener to do it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 行ってください is a polite request in the form てください; ね makes the tone softer.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q1.kobun.why: The sentence begins with the topic, then gives a reason and offers advice. から connects the cause with the result, while てください turns going into a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced by ので, the reason sounds more objective and softer, and less direct.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use 行きましょう, the speaker suggests going together instead of telling the listener to go.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use ください as an independent word; remember that the verb must change to the て form before ください.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q1.kobun.cn: Aいですから; Vてください: Vて形 + ください
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q2.kobun.vi: When you take time off work, please contact the company.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks work as the object of the action of taking time off.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: とき indicates a time or condition; は emphasizes the case of taking time off work.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the recipient of the contact.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: してください is a polite request formed with the て form of する and ください.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q2.kobun.why: The clause しごとを休むときは places the condition or time before the request. The company is the recipient of the contact, so it goes with に, while してください is the main predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If とき is replaced by 場合, the sentence emphasizes a hypothetical case rather than a specific time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: へ can also show the direction of contact toward the company, but に is more natural when emphasizing the recipient of the contact.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate ときは simply as “when” and forget that は limits the topic to the case of taking time off work.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q2.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた形・Vない形 + とき; Vて + ください
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q3.kobun.vi: Excuse me, may I sit here?
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: すみません is a polite opening used to get someone's attention before asking a question.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where the action of sitting occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ても creates a permission pattern, meaning that it is okay to do this action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: かまいませんか asks whether the previous action is allowed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q3.kobun.why: The place comes before the verb for sitting and goes with に. The ても form combines with かまいませんか to ask for permission politely.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: The meaning is almost the same, but this expression is more common and direct.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern asks about something being forbidden, so its tone is negative and different from an ordinary request for permission.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse に with で; with すわる, に indicates the place for sitting, while で usually indicates the place where an activity occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q3.kobun.cn: Vて + もかまいませんか
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q4.kobun.vi: A: Shall we go shopping together on Saturday? B: I have something to do on Saturday, so it may be a little difficult…
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: どようび states the time of the invitation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: いっしょに modifies 行く and shows that the speaker wants to go together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the purpose of going.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: 行きませんか uses a negative question form to make a polite invitation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: This part opens B's direct reply.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: は makes Saturday the topic and creates a limiting nuance.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q4.kobun.ch.7.n: が marks ようじ as something that exists or as the reason the speaker cannot go.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q4.kobun.ch.8.vi: because I have something to do
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q4.kobun.ch.8.n: ので connects the reason to the unfinished refusal that follows and creates a softer tone.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q4.kobun.ch.9.n: ちょっと…… is an indirect way to refuse, leaving unsaid the part that is difficult to state clearly.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q4.kobun.cn: N・V普通形 + ので; Vませんか uses the polite negative form to make an invitation
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q4.kobun.why: A's words place the time, manner, and purpose before the invitation. B makes Saturday the topic, uses ようじ as the subject with が, and then uses ので and ちょっと…… to refuse softly.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use から, the reason is still correct, but the refusal sounds more direct and stronger than ので.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If 行きませんか is replaced with 行きましょうか, the sentence can mean suggesting that the speakers decide together whether to go, with a different nuance from a direct invitation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q4.kobun.vs.2.d: If you say 行けません directly, the refusal is clearer and loses the indirect, polite nuance of ちょっと…….
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ちょっと as “a little” only; in conversation, ちょっと…… is often a tactful refusal, and there is no need to finish the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q5.kobun.vi: I did not make it to the appointment on time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The phrase の modifies 時間 and shows which time it is.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the point in time that must be reached.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q5.kobun.ch.2.vi: did not make it in time
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 間に合う means “make it in time”; the form ませんでした shows that someone did not make it in time in the past.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q5.kobun.why: やくそくの modifies 時間, and then に marks the point in time that must be reached. 間に合いませんでした is the main predicate and describes not reaching that time in time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 遅れました, the meaning changes to “arrived late,” focusing on being delayed rather than failing to reach the required time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake に in 時間に for a place, but here it refers to a point in time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q5.tokens.4.m: did not make it in time
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q6.kobun.vi: I invited Yoshida to our party.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the person being invited.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the event or place that the invited person will join.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: さそう is in the polite past form さそいました and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q6.kobun.why: The person being invited comes before を, while the event they are invited to join comes before に. The verb さそいました comes at the end to complete the action of inviting.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 招待しました, the basic meaning is still “invite,” but the nuance is more formal and official than さそいました.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t33-q6.kobun.tip: Do not use を for the party; を marks the invited person, while the party goes with に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q1.kobun.vi: The soccer match starts at 1 p.m.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle から marks the starting point in time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects サッカー with the noun しあい, creating the meaning “soccer match.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject that starts.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: はじまります is the predicate and describes the beginning of the match.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q1.kobun.why: から gives the starting point, サッカーの modifies しあい, and が marks the match as the subject of はじまります. The predicate comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with に, the sentence only states the time when the match starts and does not emphasize the starting point.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q1.kobun.tip: から in this sentence marks a starting point in time, not a cause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q2.kobun.vi: I do not know the rules of this game very well.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects このゲーム with ルール and shows which game the rules belong to.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object that is known.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: よく is an adverb that modifies しりません and shows the degree of knowing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: しりません is the polite negative form of しる and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q2.kobun.why: このゲームの identifies the type of rules, を marks the rules as the object of knowing. よく comes before the verb to modify the degree, while しりません ends the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If よく is replaced with あまり, it also means “not know much.” It usually appears with a negative form and emphasizes the limited degree.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q2.kobun.tip: しる in the negative form is しりません, not しません.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q3.kobun.vi: Let us compete to see who can do it best.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the unknown subject in an indirect question clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: いちばん modifies うまく and creates a superlative meaning.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: うまく is the adverbial form of うまい and modifies できる.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q3.kobun.ch.3.vi: whether someone can do it well
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: できるか creates an indirect question clause, which becomes the content of the competition.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: きょうそうしましょう is a suggestion to compete together and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q3.kobun.why: だれが introduces the information to be determined, while か turns the whole clause だれがいちばんうまくできる into an indirect question. This clause comes before きょうそうしましょう because it is the content of the competition.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If を is added after か, the structure shows more clearly that the question clause is the object of 競争する.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q3.kobun.tip: いちばん modifies the adverb うまく and does not come directly before できる to form a noun phrase.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q4.kobun.vi: If we win the next match, let us celebrate together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the setting or situation in which the action of winning occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: たら connects a hypothetical condition with the main clause that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the people who perform the action together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: ましょう expresses an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q4.kobun.why: The conditional clause comes first and is connected with たら to state what must happen first. みんなで shows that the celebration is done together, while ましょう creates an invitation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with と, the sentence has a stronger nuance of a natural or inevitable result, so it is less suitable for this invitation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: なら usually depends on information or an assumption already given, so its nuance differs from the direct condition かったら.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily think that たら is used only for the past, but in conditional sentences it means “if” or “when.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q5.kobun.vi: This school is very active in sports.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes この学校 the topic being commented on.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject being described as active or well-developed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: さかん is an adjective な used as the predicate, so it goes with です.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q5.kobun.why: は makes the school the topic, while が marks the field being evaluated. さかんです describes a state in which an activity is developing or taking place actively.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence only says that many people play sports; it does not directly comment on sports activities being well-developed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 上手です, the meaning becomes “good at sports,” which usually describes the ability of a person or group.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate さかん as “crowded,” but in this structure it emphasizes the development or lively activity of the field.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q5.kobun.cn: N は ＋ N が ＋ Aなです
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q6.kobun.vi: Before running, you must always warm up.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: 前に sets the action はしる as the time reference for the action that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: かならず modifies the warm-up action and emphasizes that it must definitely be done.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the exercise as completed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q6.kobun.why: The phrase はしる前に places the time before running at the beginning of the sentence. The object じゅんびうんどうを comes directly before します to form the structure for doing warm-up exercises.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 後で, the meaning becomes after running, not the preparation time before running.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with ときに, it means while running and does not emphasize that it happens beforehand.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t34-q6.kobun.tip: After 前に, a verb must use the dictionary form, not the past form はしった.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q1.kobun.vi: Because of the major earthquake, the bookcase fell over and I was injured.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: 大きな directly modifies the noun that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the cause of the bookcase falling over.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the bookcase as the subject of the action of falling over.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the bookcase falling over with the injury that happened next.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks けが as something that must be suffered or experienced.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: てしまいました describes a completed event, often with a feeling of regret or something unwanted.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q1.kobun.why: で gives the cause, and then が identifies the bookcase as the subject of falling over. The two events are connected by て, while てしまいました shows that the injury was fully experienced and regrettable.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used, the sentence connects the cause as a clearer clause and gives a softer explanatory tone.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If しまい is omitted, the sentence only reports that someone was injured and does not clearly express regret or something unwanted.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand で as referring only to a place, but here で indicates the cause of the event.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q1.kobun.cn: N + で; Vて + しまう
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q2.kobun.vi: I planted many flowers in the garden.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the flowers are placed or planted.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: たくさん modifies the number of flowers planted.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the flowers as the objects being planted.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: うえました is the polite past form of the verb meaning to plant.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q2.kobun.why: に sets the place where the flowers are planted, while を marks the flowers as the object of the action. うえました uses the polite past form to say that the planting has been completed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with で, にわで emphasizes the place where the activity occurs, while に is more suitable for the place where flowers are placed or planted.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If が is used, the flowers will be understood as the subject of the action, contrary to the meaning that the flowers are the objects being planted.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で for every place, but the verb meaning to plant usually uses に to indicate where a plant or flower is placed in the ground.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q3.kobun.vi: This pond is deep, so please do not play around it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents this pond as the topic being described.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause with the result that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the action of playing occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: ないでください is used to ask the listener not to do something.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q3.kobun.why: The sentence places the topic first, followed by the cause with ので. It then gives the place with で and ends with a negative request. The form ないでください suits a reminder not to perform the action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the cause has almost the same meaning, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に instead of で when talking about the place where an action occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q4.kobun.vi: Since it is starting to get a little colder, let us turn on the heater.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: 少し modifies the degree to which it is getting cold.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q4.kobun.ch.1.vi: because it has been getting cold
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: てきた describes a change that began and has progressed to the present; ので connects the cause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the thing being turned on.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: ましょう is used to invite or suggest doing an action together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q4.kobun.why: The sentence first states the change in temperature and uses てくる to show that the coldness has gradually reached the present. After ので comes the object affected and the suggestion to turn on the heater.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If ひえていく is used, the gradual cooling is viewed from the present toward the future, instead of progressing toward the present.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand てくる as only meaning movement toward a place, but here it shows a gradual change.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q4.kobun.cn: Vて + くる; V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q5.kobun.vi: It has started to get dark.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject undergoing the change of state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: てきました describes a change that has progressed to the present.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q5.kobun.why: The subject of the change is marked by が. The predicate then uses てくる to show that it is gradually getting dark and this can now be noticed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If くれていきます is used, the sentence emphasizes that the sky will continue to get darker from the present onward.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse てくる and ていく because they focus only on the meaning of going or coming and overlook the direction of the change.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q6.kobun.vi: I disagree with Mr. Tanaka's opinion.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the owner with the noun いけん that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the object toward which the action of opposing is directed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: はんたいします is the main predicate and describes the action of opposing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q6.kobun.why: The possessive phrase with の identifies whose opinion it is. With はんたいする, に marks the object being opposed, and the polite verb ends the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with とちがいます, the sentence means that it is different from that opinion and does not directly state the action of opposing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t35-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with はんたいする out of habit, but this verb usually goes with に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q1.kobun.vi: If there is a word I do not know, I will look it up in the dictionary.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: A plain-form verb comes before a noun to modify that noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the word as something whose existence or absence is assumed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: たら creates a conditional clause leading to the action of looking up the word in a dictionary.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the tool used for looking something up.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: しらべます is the main predicate and describes the action that will be performed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q1.kobun.why: The clause わからないことば modifies the noun ことば, and then たら sets the condition. The tool for looking it up is shown by で, while the main action comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If なら is used, the sentence has a hypothetical tone based on information or a situation that has already been stated.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place わからない after the noun, but Japanese places the modifying clause before the noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q1.kobun.cn: Vた・Aいかった・Aなだった・Nだった + ら
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q2.kobun.vi: I unfortunately forgot to submit the homework to my teacher.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person receiving the submitted work.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being submitted.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: の turns the verb だす into a noun, while を marks the act that was forgotten.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: てしまいました describes a completed action and carries a sense of regret.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q2.kobun.why: 先生に is the person receiving the assignment, while しゅくだいを is the item being submitted. The phrase だすのを is turned into a noun phrase to become the object of わすれる; てしまいました adds the sense of having accidentally done something and regretting it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If のを is replaced with ことを, the basic meaning is still forgetting to do something, but the expression is more formal and general.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If only わすれました is used, it only states that something was forgotten and does not emphasize regret as てしまいました does.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit の when they want to turn a verb into the object of another verb.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q2.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + のを; Vて + しまう
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q3.kobun.vi: The kanji in newspapers are difficult, so I can hardly read them.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 新聞 with かんじ and creates a modifying relationship.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the kanji in the newspaper the topic.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective い changes to the form くて to connect with the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: ほとんど modifies 読めません and shows a level close to being unable to read.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: 読めません is the negative potential form and expresses the inability to read.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q3.kobun.cn: Aい → Aくて; negative potential verb + ません
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q3.kobun.why: 新聞のかんじ forms a noun phrase, and then は makes this phrase the topic. むずかしくて connects a cause or condition with the result 読めません; ほとんど emphasizes the level of being almost unable to read.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If むずかしくて is replaced with むずかしいので, the cause-and-effect relationship becomes clearer and sounds more explanatory.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: あまり読めません means not being able to read much and is weaker than ほとんど読めません, which means being almost unable to read.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use むずかいて; the adjective い must change from い to くて before connecting.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q4.kobun.vi: In the future, I want to do work that is useful to people.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q4.kobun.sk: Time + N の + N に役に立つ + N が + Vたいです
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: しょうらい states the time or period of the wish.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 人 with やくにたつ to show the people who benefit.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: A verb in the dictionary form comes before a noun to modify しごと.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the job as what the speaker wants to do.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: したい expresses the speaker's wish.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q4.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + N; Vます形 omits ます + たいです
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q4.kobun.why: 人のやくにたつ is a clause that modifies しごと, so the whole phrase means a job that is useful to people. The particle が marks what is wanted, while したい states the speaker's wish.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If やくにたつ is replaced with 人のためになる, the meaning is still being useful to others, but the expression focuses more on providing benefits.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: 仕事をしたい only says that the speaker wants to work and does not emphasize that the work is useful to people.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q4.kobun.tip: When a verb comes before a noun to modify it, do not add です and usually keep the dictionary form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 今日 with テスト to identify the test.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes today's test the topic.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: かんたん is an adjective な, so its polite past form is でした.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q5.kobun.why: 今日のテスト is a noun phrase in which 今日 modifies テスト. は makes the test the topic, while かんたんでした is the predicate and shows a past state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with やさしかったです still means easy, but it uses adjective い instead of adjective な かんたん.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q5.kobun.tip: Adjective な does not change to かんたんかった in the past; かんたんでした must be used.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q5.kobun.cn: N + は + Aな + でした
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: ねっしんに modifies the action of studying and shows the manner of doing it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the subject of study as the object of べんきょうしています.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: ている describes an action that is continuing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q6.kobun.why: ねっしんに comes before the verb phrase to describe how the studying is done. 日本語を is the object of studying, while べんきょうしています shows that the action is happening now.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with いっしょうけんめいに still means studying diligently, but emphasizes making one's greatest effort.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If しています is replaced with しました, the sentence changes from studying now to having studied or having finished studying.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q6.kobun.tip: Do not use ねっしんだに; when adjective な modifies a verb, it must change to the form に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: This part combines with きり to form the adverb はっきり.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: This part combines with はっ to complete the adverb はっきり, meaning clearly.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q7.kobun.why: はっきり is an adverb used to modify a verb or adjective and shows a clear, unambiguous state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: ちゃんと focuses on doing something correctly or completely, rather than only expressing clarity like はっきり.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t36-q7.kobun.tip: Do not translate はっきり as only one fixed meaning; depending on the verb it accompanies, it can mean clearly or decisively.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q1.kobun.vi: It takes one hour to get from home to the graduation ceremony venue.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point of the route.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects this noun with the noun for the place that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: まで indicates the endpoint of the route.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The duration phrase comes before かかります to show how long it takes.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: かかります expresses the time required.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q1.kobun.why: The sentence gives the route from the starting point to the endpoint, then states the duration and uses かかります as the predicate. から and まで form a pair showing the range from where to where.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used instead of まで, the sentence focuses only on the destination and loses the sense of a limited route.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit まで because they think it is enough to state the destination, but a route pattern usually uses から～まで.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q2.kobun.vi: Excuse me, please tell the teacher that I will be a little late.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: が softens the opening before a request or favor.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 少し modifies おくれる and shows how late the person will be.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the content being communicated.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the person receiving the information.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: てください combines with a verb to form a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q2.kobun.why: The information to report comes before と, the recipient goes with に, and つたえてください forms the favor at the end of the sentence. This order makes clear what should be reported and to whom.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning is to say the exact words or sentence, while つたえてください is broader and means to pass on information.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with the recipient, but the recipient of information must go with に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q3.kobun.vi: There is a test tomorrow, so I am studying today.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q3.kobun.sk: Time に + N が あります。 + それで） + Time は + N を Vます
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: あした states when the event occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing that exists in the pattern あります.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: あります is the predicate of the first clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: それで connects the preceding cause or situation with the following result.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: は makes today the topic and creates a contrast with tomorrow.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: べんきょうします is the action performed as the result.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q3.kobun.why: The first clause states the situation that there is a test tomorrow, and then それで leads to today's action. は in 今日は creates a contrast between the times あした and 今日.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If だから is used, the cause-and-effect relationship is clearer and more direct; それで focuses more on stating the following result.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use は for テスト, but with あります, an existing object is usually marked with が.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q4.kobun.vi: I wrote and submitted a report on the Asian economy.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の modifies けいざい, forming the phrase “Asian economy.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: について indicates the topic or subject that the report is about.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks レポート as the object of 書いて.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the action of writing with the following action of submitting.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: 出しました is the main action and is in the polite past tense.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q4.kobun.why: The phrase について states the topic of the report, を marks the report as the thing written, and て connects the two actions in order: writing first and submitting second.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If について is replaced with に関する, this phrase becomes a modifier, like “a report related to the economy,” and must directly modify a noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate について as “about” and use it in the wrong position; this pattern comes after the topic and before the verb or noun it connects to.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q5.kobun.vi: I have experience working part-time at a restaurant.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the part-time work takes place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects アルバイト with けいけん, forming the phrase “part-time work experience.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks experience as something that exists or is possessed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: あります completes the pattern for expressing experience.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q5.kobun.why: で states where the part-time experience took place, の makes アルバイト a modifier of けいけん, and けいけんが あります expresses having experience.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes having done something before, while the present-tense sentence emphasizes currently having the experience.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for a place, but an activity taking place at a restaurant must use で.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q6.kobun.vi: This Japanese novel has been translated into English.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: この and の together limit the noun しょうせつ being discussed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the novel as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the target language of the translation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: されました is the polite past passive form, showing that the novel receives the action of translation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q6.kobun.why: The topic is the novel, the target language goes with に, and the passive verb shows that the novel is the thing being translated. Japanese places the target language before the translation verb.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If えいごで is used, the meaning is closer to “in English” or “by means of English,” not “into English.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で because it translates as “in English,” but a change into another language uses に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: Repetition creates a sense of rapid development or an increasingly clear change.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q7.kobun.why: どんどん is a repeated adverb. It can stand alone to emphasize continuous progress.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with だんだん, the meaning suggests a gradual, gentler change.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t37-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate どんどん only as “quickly,” missing the sense of increasingly progressing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q1.kobun.vi: I felt uncomfortable when an unfamiliar person said rude things to me.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q1.kobun.sk: Relative clause + N に + Aな N を + V受身て、 + N が + Aい polite past tense
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The modifying clause comes before 人, creating the meaning “a person whom I do not know.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the person who performs the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な modifies こと, so な stays before the noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the content that was said.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The て form of the passive connects the preceding cause or event with the feeling in the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle が marks the thing that has the state わるい.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: わるい changes to the polite past tense to describe the state at that time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q1.kobun.why: The clause しらない modifies 人, while 人に is the person who caused the passive action. The content that was said comes before を, and then the て form connects the event with the mood.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing に with から can still indicate the person who caused the action, but に is usually more natural in this passive sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use 人が instead of 人に, but in a passive sentence に marks the person who caused the effect.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q2.kobun.vi: This machine is new, and new technology is being used.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は presents the machine as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective い acts as the predicate and describes the topic.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks technology as the object being used in the passive sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The passive form combined with ています describes the state of the technology being used.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q2.kobun.why: The topic is stated before は, followed by its characteristic. The second clause uses が with technology and the passive form to emphasize that the technology is being used.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with つかっています, the subject using the technology will be a person or thing already mentioned.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse the user with the thing being used and use the active voice instead of the passive voice.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q3.kobun.vi: When the schedule is decided, I will let you know by email or phone.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the schedule as the thing that is decided.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The past form きまった combines with ら to create the condition “when the schedule has been decided.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: か comes after a noun to present the first choice.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: または connects choices in a formal way.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle で indicates the means used to give notice.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb in the ます form is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q3.kobun.cn: Vた形 + ら; Aい drop い + かったら; Aな + だったら; N + だったら
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q3.kobun.why: The conditional clause comes first to identify when the main action will happen. か and または connect two means of communication, while で indicates the means of giving notice.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If とき is used, the sentence only indicates a general time and does not emphasize a condition that has just been completed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: なら usually depends on existing information or an assumption, so its nuance differs from the time condition expressed by たら.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に with 電話, but the means of carrying out an action must go with で.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q3.tokens.7.m: to notify, to let someone know
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q5.kobun.vi: Among the people here, I do not know anyone except Mr. Tanaka.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は presents the speaker as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the range being considered for comparison or choice.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: いがいは identifies the part excluded from the range of people known, meaning “not anyone except Tanaka.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: しりません is the negative predicate, showing that the speaker does not know the other people.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q5.kobun.why: この中で limits the scope, while いがいは excludes Tanaka from the negated part. Therefore, しりません applies only to people other than Tanaka.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: When たなかさんだけ知っています is used, the sentence directly states that the speaker knows only Tanaka.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: たなかさんしか知りません emphasizes even more strongly that the speaker knows absolutely no one other than Tanaka.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate 以外は as “only,” but it is important to understand that this is an exclusion structure combined with a negative sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q6.kobun.vi: Mr. Mori went on a business trip instead of Mr. Kimura.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: のかわりに indicates the person or thing being replaced.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject who carried out the action of going on a business trip.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the purpose or destination of going.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きました is the main predicate and uses the polite past form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q6.kobun.why: The phrase for the person being replaced comes before のかわりに, followed by the subject marked with が. に attaches to the noun しゅっちょう to indicate the activity that the subject went to do.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used here, the meaning is going on a business trip for Kimura’s benefit or purpose, not necessarily replacing Kimura.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse のかわりに with のために; the first pattern emphasizes replacement.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q1.kobun.vi: Because I carried heavy luggage every day, my arms became bigger.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q1.kobun.sk: Frequency ＋ Aい ＋ Nを ＋ Vて ＋ Nが ＋ Aいく ＋ なる
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: 毎日 indicates the time or frequency at which an action occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the luggage as the object being carried.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: て-form connects the action はこぶ with the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the arm as the subject undergoing a change.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: ふとく is the connecting form of the adjective い, and comes before なる.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: なりました expresses a change that has already occurred.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q1.kobun.why: 毎日 comes at the beginning of the sentence to state the frequency. It is followed by an adjective modifying the luggage and を marking the object. The て verb sequence connects carrying the luggage with the result of the arms becoming bigger, while Aいく＋なる expresses a change of state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern describes a change into a certain state, while Aいです simply describes a state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If ので is used, the cause is clearly stated in a reason clause, giving a more direct explanatory meaning.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget to change the adjective ending い into the く form before なる.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q2.kobun.vi: My daughter is at least 5 cm taller than me.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q2.kobun.sk: Nより ＋ Nのほうが ＋ Quantity以上 ＋ Nが ＋ Aいです
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: より states the object used as the comparison standard.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects むすめ with ほう, forming a phrase that identifies the side chosen in the comparison.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: ほうが marks the side with the higher degree; ５センチいじょう states the minimum difference.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the specific feature being compared.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: 高いです is the predicate describing height in the present.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q2.kobun.why: より sets the comparison standard, while のほうが marks the side with the higher degree. せが高い is a natural combination for talking about height, in which せが is the subject of the adjective 高い.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: This is a pattern for comparing two objects; if ほうが is omitted, the sentence can still be understood, but the contrast is less clear.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with ほど, the sentence changes to a negative meaning: one object is not as much as the other.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place ５センチ after 高い, but in this sentence it comes before the predicate to indicate the difference in degree.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q3.kobun.vi: I went to visit my friend who is in the hospital.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: This clause modifies 友だち and identifies which friend.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the friend with the act of visiting that person.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the purpose of going.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q3.kobun.why: にゅういんしている comes before 友だち, so it modifies the noun. の identifies the person being visited, while に connects おみまい with 行きました to indicate the purpose of going.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the focus is on going to meet the friend, while おみまい emphasizes the purpose of visiting a sick person.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand にゅういんしている as an independent action, but here it directly modifies 友だち.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q4.kobun.vi: I said to my friend who had a cold, “Get well soon.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: を goes with ひく in the fixed expression かぜをひく, indicating an illness one has caught.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: ひいた is the plain past form and modifies 友だち.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the person listening to the speech.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The phrase in quotation marks is the content of what was said.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: と marks the exact words before 言いました.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: 言いました is the main predicate and receives the quoted content through と.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q4.kobun.why: かぜをひいた comes before 友だち and modifies it to identify the friend. に indicates the listener, while the speech is placed in quotation marks and connected to 言いました by と.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 伝える is used, the sentence emphasizes conveying information and is less natural than 言う when simply saying a wish.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: と言う is used to report or quote speech in general; 言いました identifies an action that has occurred.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を for the listener, but the listener in the structure 言う usually goes with に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q5.kobun.vi: Mr. Kimura has recovered from his illness.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies Mr. Kimura as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object whose state is being described.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb なおる in the polite past form expresses that the illness has gone away.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q5.kobun.why: The sentence places the person being discussed first with は, then states that the illness changed state with が and the verb なおりました. The verb なおる is used when an illness or problem is overcome or repaired.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with よくなる, the sentence leans toward the meaning that the condition has improved, without directly emphasizing that the illness has gone away.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with なおる, but this verb usually goes with が when talking about an illness or problem being overcome or repaired.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q6.kobun.vi: Last week, my older sister left the hospital.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q6.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N が ＋ Nする・しました
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase at the beginning of the sentence identifies when the event happens.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the person who carries out the action of leaving the hospital.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: たいいんする is the verb サ変, changed to たいいんしました to express a completed action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q6.kobun.why: The time phrase is placed first as the background, followed by the subject with が and the main verb at the end. たいいんする describes leaving the hospital after treatment.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: With this pattern, the sentence emphasizes leaving the hospital and then returning, adding a direction of movement compared with simply saying that someone left the hospital.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t39-q6.kobun.tip: Do not translate たいいんする as “go to the hospital”; this word refers to leaving the hospital after treatment.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし with the following noun to show possession.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents father as the topic being introduced.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The noun いしゃ combines with です to form a polite noun predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q1.kobun.why: わたしの identifies the person being discussed as my father. The noun sentence uses the pattern N は N です to state a person's job or status.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the focus is on the person who is a doctor, rather than on presenting father as the topic.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q1.kobun.tip: Do not use の after 父 when you mean “my father”; わたしの must come before 父.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q10.kobun.vi: I want to buy new clothes.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q10.kobun.sk: Aい + N が + Vます remove ます + たいです
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective 新しい modifies the noun （ふく） that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object that the speaker wants to buy in the pattern 買いたい.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: 買います changes into 買いたい to express the speaker's desire.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q10.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます + たいです
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q10.kobun.why: 新しい comes before （ふく） to describe the clothes. （ふく）が is the object of the desire, while 買いたいです expresses the speaker's desire to buy them.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q10.kobun.vs.0.t: Vます remove ます + ほしいです
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern is not used directly with an action performed by the speaker. It expresses a desire to have an object.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with 買いたい, but in a desire pattern, が is usually used for the object.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: それ is the object that the speaker asks to borrow; in casual speech, the particle を is omitted.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: も follows the て form and connects to いい, creating the permission-request pattern てもいい.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: いいですか asks whether the previous action is acceptable.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q11.kobun.why: それ states the thing the speaker wants to borrow, while （かりて）もいいですか asks for permission. The verb must be in the て form before もいい.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: This is a sentence giving or accepting permission, not a question asking for permission.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern changes the meaning to “must not do.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q11.kobun.tip: Do not connect ます directly to もいい; first change the verb to the て form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q11.kobun.cn: Vて + も + いいですか
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q12.kobun.vi: The answer to that problem is not A but B.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects そのもんだい with （こたえ） to show possession or a connection.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes （こたえ） the topic being described.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: じゃなくて denies A and connects to the correct information that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: です concludes the correct information about the topic （こたえ）.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q12.kobun.why: そのもんだいの modifies （こたえ）, and then は presents the answer as the topic. Aじゃなくて denies choice A and moves to conclusion Bです.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: It has a similar meaning but is more formal and rigid than じゃなくて.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: It only denies N and does not directly create a contrast with another answer.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate じゃなくて as a sentence ending, but here it connects to the correct information that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q12.kobun.cn: N・Aな + じゃなくて、+ N・Aなです
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q13.kobun.vi: Every morning, I wake up at 6 and leave home at 7.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q13.kobun.sk: Time + N に + Vて、+ N に + N を + Vます
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: まいあさ indicates how often the whole action happens.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the time of waking up.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects waking up with the following action in sequence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the time of leaving home.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the place someone leaves with the verb 出ます.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q13.kobun.why: The two time points に are linked to the two actions in order. The て form connects the actions in the order they happen, while を with うち shows the place someone leaves.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: Emphasizes that the later action happens only after the earlier action is complete.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: States typical actions, not necessarily in the order shown in this sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q13.kobun.tip: を does not only mark an object affected by an action; with 出ます, it also marks the place someone leaves.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q14.kobun.vi: I borrowed books, studied, and did things like that at the library.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: で marks the place where borrowing books and studying take place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the thing being borrowed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: A verb in the たり form states one typical action in a series of actions.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: たり continues listing typical actions and waits for しました at the end of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: しました ends the pattern ～たり、～たりしました and shows that the actions happened.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q14.kobun.why: で sets the place, while を marks the book being borrowed. The two verbs use the たり form to list typical actions, and しました ends the sentence in the past tense.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: Lists actions in a clearer sequence instead of only giving examples.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: Uses the present tense or describes habits, without stating that the actions have been completed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q14.kobun.tip: The たり form must be used with しました or します at the end; do not use たり as if it were て to connect a sequence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q14.kobun.cn: Vた + り、+ Vた + り + します/しました
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vi: My younger sister is a university student.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の shows the possessive relationship between わたし and the following noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents younger sister as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 大学生 is a noun used as the predicate. It combines with です to create a polite expression.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q2.kobun.why: わたしの comes before いもうと to identify the relative who belongs to the speaker. The topic pronoun は connects with the status noun 大学生 and です.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the emphasis is on the younger sister being a university student.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q2.kobun.tip: いもうと refers only to the speaker's younger sister; when talking about someone else's younger sister, choose the appropriate family term.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vi: My mother is a strict person.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that mother is the topic being described.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective きびしい comes before 人 to modify the person.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 人です forms a noun predicate; the phrase きびしい人 means a strict person.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q3.kobun.why: 母は states the person being described. The adjective きびしい comes before 人 according to the noun-modifying rule, forming the predicate きびしい人 with です.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced in this sentence, the meaning changes to “Mother is a person who is not strict.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q3.kobun.tip: An adjective ending in い comes directly before a noun, without adding の or な.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies the person being discussed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: です comes after the adjective な to end the sentence politely.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q4.kobun.why: The sentence places the person being described first with は, then uses the adjective な as the predicate. です gives the sentence a polite tone.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 親切な is used, it must come before a noun, not directly at the end of a sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 優しいです, the meaning is still “kind,” but the tone is closer to gentle and mild.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget な when the adjective な comes before a noun, but な is not used before です.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vi: My grandmother is very healthy and walks for one hour in the park every morning.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states that grandmother is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies an adjective or stateげんき, showing a high degree.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: で connects the stateげんき with the next clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: まいあさ indicates the time when a repeated action occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: を indicates the place or route passed through while walking here.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: 1時間 indicates the length of time an action continues.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: ています describes an action in progress or a habit that is being maintained.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q5.kobun.why: げんきで connects the state of health with a daily habit. まいあさ comes before the action, while こうえんを indicates the route walked through and １時間 indicates the duration.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If を is replaced with で, the park is understood as the place where the activity happens, without emphasizing the route passed through.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: あるきます only says that someone will walk or usually walks; it does not clearly show an ongoing state like あるいています.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で with every place, but verbs showing movement through a place usually use を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q6.kobun.vi: There is a new supermarket near my house.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects うち with the following noun showing a location.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where the new supermarket appears.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: This part modifies スーパー that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the thing that newly appears or is formed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: できました is the predicate and describes appearance or completion.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q6.kobun.why: The phrase うちのちかくに puts the location first, then スーパーが identifies the thing that newly appears. The adjective comes before the noun to describe the supermarket.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 近くで is used, it means the place where an action happens, not the place where a supermarket appears.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: あります indicates existence, while できました emphasizes that a new supermarket has appeared or has been built.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse に and で; に is used for a place where something exists or appears, while で is used for a place where an action is performed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q7.kobun.vi: My older sister has not been well recently, so I am worried.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies the sister as the person being discussed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: このごろ indicates a period close to the present.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the state described in the phrase げんきがない.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: ので connects the cause before it with the worry that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: です politely ends a predicate describing an emotion.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q7.kobun.why: このごろ limits the time of the unhealthy state. The clause げんきがないので gives the reason, while しんぱいです is the speaker’s result or emotion.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If のに is used, the sentence changes to a contrasting meaning such as “although she is not well, …”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily connect the two parts with から every time, but ので is usually softer and more objective when giving a reason.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q7.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q8.kobun.vi: I am wearing the sweater that my older sister gave me.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person who performs an action for someone or gives something in もらった.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The past clause modifies セーター and tells us from whom the sweater was received.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the sweater as the object of the action of wearing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: ています describes the present state resulting from the action of putting on clothes.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q8.kobun.why: あねにもらった comes before セーター to modify the sweater. セーターを is the object, while ています describes the state of wearing it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: 着ます indicates the action of putting on clothes or the intention to put them on, without emphasizing the state of wearing them.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: はいています is used for trousers, shoes, or things worn on the lower body, not for a sweater.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may always translate ています as “be doing,” but with 着る it often describes the state of wearing something.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q9.kobun.vi: I cooked and then waited for everyone to arrive.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the food as the object being cooked.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects the action of cooking with the action of waiting in sequence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject performing the action 来る in the subordinate clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: の turns the clause 来る into a noun, and を marks it as the thing being waited for.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: まちました is the main predicate in the polite past tense.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q9.kobun.why: つくって connects the two actions in order. The clause みんなが来る is nominalized with の and then becomes the object of 待つ.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: ことを can also nominalize the event of everyone coming, but this expression is more abstract and formal than のを.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: 来てから means “after everyone comes,” so waiting is no longer the main action in the structure.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t4-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit の when they want to turn an entire clause into the object of a verb such as 待つ.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies Mr. Tanaka as the person being described.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks singing as the area being evaluated as good.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: うまい is a stem-ending adjective い used as the predicate, with です added to make it polite.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q1.kobun.why: The pattern NはNがA describes a characteristic or ability of the person stated as the topic. が marks what is being evaluated, and the adjective comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: With this pattern, the sentence emphasizes singing skillfully instead of commenting on singing ability.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q1.kobun.tip: Do not translate が mechanically as “thing”; in this pattern, が marks the content or skill being evaluated.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q1.tokens.1.m: a respectful title for a man or woman
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The form て connects an action or reason to the apology that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: This is an apology placed at the end of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q10.kobun.why: The clause in the form て comes first to state the cause or situation, followed by the apology. This particle and word order create a natural way to apologize for an action that has just happened.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: With this pattern, the sentence emphasizes something that has happened accidentally or caused regret.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate て as “and,” but in this sentence it means “because of having.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q11.kobun.vi: I prepared luggage for the trip.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects noun りょこう with noun にもつ, creating a noun phrase with a modifier.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the luggage as the object being prepared.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is in the polite past form and describes preparation that has been completed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q11.kobun.why: The phrase りょこうのにもつ is formed by placing the modifying noun before the main noun. This noun phrase is the object of を, and the verb よういしました completes the predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used instead of の, the preceding noun may be understood as a place or destination, rather than directly modifying the luggage.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily reverse the order and say “trip luggage,” but Japanese places the modifier before the main noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 今日 with しゅくだい, showing that the homework belongs to today.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes しゅくだい the topic being commented on.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective なかんたん combines with です to form a polite predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q12.kobun.why: 今日のしゅくだい is a noun phrase in which 今日の modifies しゅくだい. は marks the topic, while かんたんです is the comment about that topic.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If a stem-ending い adjective is used, the structure is Aいです; かんたん is a な adjective, so です is needed in this way.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse かんたん with a stem-ending い adjective and add い after it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q14.kobun.vi: The summer vacation is about to end.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q14.kobun.sk: Time + Nが + Vて + しまいます
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: もうすぐ modifies the predicate and shows that the event is about to happen.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the summer vacation as the event that is about to end.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: おわって is the て form of おわる and connects the main verb with しまいます.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: しまいます describes an event that will be completed, often with a feeling of regret or unwillingness.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q14.kobun.why: もうすぐ comes before the predicate to signal that the time is near. Vてしまう emphasizes that the vacation will end completely, together with the speaker’s feeling of regret.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If used in this sentence, the meaning focuses on an ongoing change in the future.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: With this pattern, the sentence only states that the vacation may end; it does not confirm this or express regret.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q14.kobun.tip: Do not confuse しまいます with a particle that marks the future; it also shows a completed result and the speaker’s feelings.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q14.kobun.cn: Vて + しまう/しまいます
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q15.kobun.why: This is an independent vocabulary entry, so it does not have a complete sentence structure to analyze by subject or predicate. The two parts are separated only to show the full sequence of characters in the word.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If 関連する is used, the meaning leans toward “be related,” emphasizing the connection between events.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may remember only the meaning “relationship” and forget that 関係 often goes with に or が in related structures.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to modify library.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the library the topic of the ability to use it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: でも follows an interrogative word and means that any person is acceptable.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: りようする changes to the potential form りようできる, and ます is added to make it polite.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q3.kobun.why: この modifies the noun, は makes the library the topic, and だれでも expands the object to include anyone. できます comes at the end of the sentence to express that use is possible or permitted.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 誰かが is used, the meaning is only that someone can use it, not everyone.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If 利用します is used, the sentence talks about people using it and does not emphasize ability or permission.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q3.kobun.tip: Do not confuse でも in だれでも with “but”; here it means “any … at all.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q3.kobun.cn: 疑問詞 + でも; Nする + できる
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q4.kobun.vi: After waiting for 30 minutes, I was finally able to get on the bus.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q4.kobun.sk: Duration + Vて + Adverb + N に + past potential V
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: A phrase showing the length of time spent waiting.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb 待つ changes to the て form to connect with the action that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb that emphasizes a result achieved after waiting for some time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に indicates the vehicle or object that the speaker was able to board.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: 乗る changes to the potential form 乗れる, and then changes to the polite past form 乗れました.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q4.kobun.why: The duration and the waiting action come first, followed by the result. やっと adds the feeling of finally achieving the expected result.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with やっと still means “finally,” but the tone is slightly more formal.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with すぐに, the meaning changes to “immediately,” which is opposite to the idea of having to wait a long time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake のれました for “get on the vehicle,” but it is the potential form of 乗る, meaning “be able to get on.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q5.kobun.vi: Tea goes very well with cake.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective あまい comes before a noun to modify ケーキ.
