default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle には introduces the object being considered, namely the cake that the tea goes well with.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject that creates the good match with the cake.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 合う describes two things that match or combine well.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q5.kobun.why: The object is introduced with には, while the item that creates the good match is the subject with が. This structure is often used to say that food, clothing, or colors match something.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: A shorter form that still means “go well with N,” but does not emphasize the specific object as には does.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 好きだ, the meaning is “like that item,” not that two things match.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with あう, but the object used with the verb 合う usually takes に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q6.kobun.vi: There is a party tomorrow, but I have a personal matter, so I cannot go.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q6.kobun.sk: Time + N が ありますが、 + N は + N が ありますから + negative potential V
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: A phrase indicating the time of an event.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the existence of something in the pattern あります.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: が connects two contrasting clauses: there is a party, but I cannot go.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle は makes the speaker the topic of the following explanation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle が marks something that exists in the pattern ようじがあります.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q6.kobun.ch.5.vi: because I have something to do
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: から connects the reason with the result: not being able to attend the party.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: 行く changes the verb to the negative potential form, expressing that one cannot go.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q6.kobun.cn: N・V普通形 ＋ が、 / N・V普通形 ＋ から ＋ result clause
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q6.kobun.why: The clause about the party is stated first to set the context. Then が shifts to the speaker’s contrasting situation. から places the reason before the result 行けません.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing から with ので still gives a reason, but the tone is softer and more objective.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing が with けれども still expresses contrast, but the wording is more complete and formal.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place から at the beginning of the sentence because of Vietnamese habits. However, in this sentence, the reason comes before the result and ends with から.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q7.kobun.vi: Before playing the game, we decided the rules.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q7.kobun.sk: N を ＋ V辞書形 ＋ まえに ＋ N を ＋ past-tense V
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object of the verb する.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary form する comes before まえ to modify the time before playing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the time before the action of deciding the rules took place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the object of the action at the end of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The final verb phrase is the main predicate and states the action that was carried out.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q7.kobun.why: The clause ゲームをする identifies the action used as the time reference, while まえに places the action of deciding the rules before that reference point. The two phrases を respectively mark the object of する and the final predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If あとで is used instead, the action of deciding the rules takes place after playing, which is the opposite of this sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes a state that started before the time of playing, not simply a time before playing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit the particle を in ゲームをする, but を is necessary to mark the game as the object of する.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks rice as the object being eaten.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: 食べる changes the past form 食べた and adds ら to connect a condition or a time that occurs after the action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending in い changes to the く form to modify なりました.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: なる expresses a change of state; here, it means becoming sleepy.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q8.kobun.cn: Vた形 ＋ ら; Aい remove い ＋ く ＋ なる
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q8.kobun.why: The action of eating is set as the earlier point. Then たら connects it to the following result. With an adjective ending in い, ねむい changes to ねむく before なる to express a change.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing 食べたら with 食べたあとで only shows the order after eating and has less of a conditional meaning.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: The pattern Vると usually expresses a natural or repeated result, so たら is more suitable for one specific meal.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily say ねむいなりました, but before なる, the adjective ending in い must change to the く form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q9.kobun.vi: The next class starts at 2 o’clock.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q9.kobun.sk: N の ＋ N は ＋ time から ＋ です
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: つぎの comes before a noun and modifies the next class.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は presents the class as the topic being announced.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: から indicates when the class starts.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: です ends the noun sentence and confirms the starting time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q9.kobun.why: The noun つぎの modifies こうぎ. Then は makes the class the topic. The phrase ２時から states the starting point of the time being announced.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with に, it only indicates the time when something occurs and does not emphasize starting at 2 o’clock.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: まで indicates the ending point, so the meaning changes to until or up to 2 o’clock.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand から as expressing a reason, but in this sentence から indicates the starting point of the time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q1.kobun.vi: On days off, I usually get up earlier than usual and go to the park.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q1.kobun.sk: N の ＋ N は ＋ N より ＋ Aい remove い＋く ＋ Vて、＋ N に ＋ Vます
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 休み with 日, forming the noun phrase 休みの日.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the day off the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: より sets the comparison point for how early one gets up.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: はやく is an adverbial form that modifies おきて.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The て form connects getting up with going to the park.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: に marks the destination of 行きます.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q1.kobun.cn: N より ＋ Aい remove い＋く; Vて ＋ Vます
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q1.kobun.why: 休みの日は sets the context, while いつもより creates the comparison point for how early. はやく modifies getting up, and the て form connects getting up with going to the park.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Use an adjective to say that a time or thing is earlier, not to directly modify a verb.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: The meaning changes to doing one action before another action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q1.kobun.tip: When modifying a verb, the adjective い must change to the く form, such as はやい changing to はやく.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the writing is done.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the address as the content being written; の connects the possessive part to the following noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: 書いてください uses the て form with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q10.kobun.why: The place comes before the object and the action, following the natural word order of Japanese. The pattern Vてください turns the action of writing into a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 書きましょう is used instead, the sentence becomes an invitation or suggestion to write together, rather than a request for the listener to write.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If 書いてもいいです is used instead, the sentence asks or confirms whether writing is allowed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q10.kobun.tip: Do not connect the dictionary form of a verb directly to ください; change it to the て form first.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the speaker as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the place of residence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: すんで is the て form of すむ. It connects with います to express an ongoing state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: います completes the pattern for expressing a continuing state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q11.kobun.why: A place of residence is used with に. Then the verb すむ changes to the て form and combines with います. This structure shows that the state of living there is still continuing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 行きます is used instead, it means going to Tokyo and describes movement, not the place where one lives.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If 働いています is used instead, it means working in Tokyo and does not confirm the place of residence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q11.kobun.tip: Do not use で with すむ; a place of residence is usually used with に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q12.kobun.vi: If you go straight through that slope, there will be a supermarket on the right.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the route or place passed through during movement.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: まっすぐ modifies how the action すすむ is performed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects a condition with the result that usually follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the location where the supermarket exists.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks an object that appears or exists in that location.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: あります is the predicate indicating that an object exists.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q12.kobun.why: The first part gives the route and way of moving, while と connects it to the natural result discovered on the right. In an existence sentence, the location goes with に, the existing object goes with が, and あります is the predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: The pattern と describes a natural or usual result that occurs when the preceding action is performed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with たら, the sentence becomes the hypothetical condition “if you continue,” with less emphasis on an inevitable result.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q12.kobun.vs.2.d: If it is replaced with てください, the sentence becomes a request to go straight, rather than directions leading to a result.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q12.kobun.tip: In the existence pattern, do not change に for the location to で; で usually indicates where an action takes place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q13.kobun.sk: Adv ＋ Nをします polite volitional
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: そろそろ modifies the suggestion and shows that the appropriate time is near.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: しましょう is the polite volitional form of します, used to invite or suggest doing an action together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q13.kobun.why: そろそろ is placed before the suggestion to show that it is almost time to leave. しましょう expresses an invitation to do something together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with しませんか, the invitation becomes a softer question, equivalent to “Shall we leave?”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with してください, the speaker asks the listener to leave, so it is no longer a suggestion to act together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand しましょう as a command; in fact, this pattern is usually an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes この道 the topic being described.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: です follows an adjective ending in い to form a polite sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q14.kobun.why: The sentence places この道は at the beginning to state the subject, then uses the adjective くらい as the predicate. です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used, the sentence means that this road is not dark.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget です when using an adjective politely.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q2.kobun.vi: If you turn at the corner, you will see a bookstore.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the place where the turning action occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects an earlier action with the natural result that occurs afterward.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object that exists after the pattern indicating appearance.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is the predicate indicating that an object or place exists.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q2.kobun.why: The location phrase comes before を as the place where the turning action occurs. The pattern V＋と connects that action with the natural result that there is a bookstore ahead.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with まがったら, the sentence has the meaning “after/if you turn” and does not emphasize a natural result as much as と.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: なら needs a condition or topic that has already been stated, so it is less suitable than と in these directions.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use たら for every meaning of “when,” but と is suitable when the result happens automatically after the action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q3.kobun.vi: I still have not decided what I want to buy.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.0.vi: the thing I want to buy
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: 買いたい modifies もの, while が marks the thing that has not been decided.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The polite negative form ません shows that the decision is still unfinished.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q3.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます ＋ たい; Vたい ＋ N; まだ ＋ Vません
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q3.kobun.why: The clause 買いたい modifies もの to create the meaning “the thing I want to buy.” This phrase is the subject with が, while まだ combines with ません to express that the decision is still unfinished up to now.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 買いたがる is used, the sentence talks about another person’s desire, not the speaker’s desire.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: 買うもの means “the thing that will be bought/the thing that is bought,” and does not clearly express the desire to buy as 買いたいもの does.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistake 買いたいもの for “want to buy something,” but in this sentence the whole phrase means “the thing that I want to buy.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q4.kobun.vi: I asked a store employee where the sweets were.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q4.kobun.sk: N は ＋ question word ＋ か ＋ N に ＋ Vました
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the sweets the topic of the information being asked about.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: か changes a direct question into the content of an indirect question before 聞きました.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the person being asked.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 聞きました is the polite past form of 聞く and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q4.kobun.cn: Question word ＋ か; N に ＋ 聞く
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q4.kobun.why: おかしはどこか is the information being asked about, with か placed at the end of the indirect-question clause. The person being asked goes with に, while 聞きました comes at the end as the main action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: どこですか is a direct question, while どこか is inside a larger sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: どこにあるか emphasizes the location where the sweets exist and is more complete when asking where an object is.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may put か at the end of the whole sentence, but an indirect question needs か immediately after the information being asked about.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q5.kobun.vi: Because work was busy, I could not eat lunch.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q5.kobun.sk: N が ＋ Aいくて ＋ N が ＋ past negative potential V
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks work as the cause described as busy.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: An adjective ending in い changes to くて to connect the cause with the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks lunch as the object that could not be eaten in the potential sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 食べられませんでした is the past negative potential form, expressing that the speaker could not eat.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q5.kobun.cn: Aい remove い ＋ くて; Group 2 verbs remove る ＋ られる; Vられる ＋ ませんでした
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q5.kobun.why: いそがしくて connects the cause with the result in the following clause. In the potential pattern, the food goes with が because it is treated as the object that can or cannot be acted on.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: 忙しいので also means “because it was busy,” but its explanatory tone is clearer and softer.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: 忙しくなくて instead means “because it was not busy” or connects a negative state, so the meaning changes.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を before 食べられませんでした, but potential verbs usually use が to mark the object that can be acted on.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q6.kobun.vi: This piece of meat is very tender, isn’t it?
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: この must come before a noun to modify it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes this piece of meat the topic being commented on.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies the adjective やわらかい and shows a high degree.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending in い acts as the predicate and describes the meat.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: ですね makes the comment softer and invites the listener to agree.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q6.kobun.why: この comes before にく to identify “this piece of meat”. After stating the topic with は, とても modifies the adjective and ですね turns the comment into a gentle shared observation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: ですね suggests agreement, while ですよ emphasizes the information the speaker wants to convey.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: やわらかそうです only describes an appearance that seems tender; it does not make as certain a statement as やわらかい.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use この単独 as a pronoun, but この always needs a noun after it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q6.kobun.cn: この ＋ N; とても ＋ Aい; Aい ＋ ですね
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: いっしょに modifies the action of eating and shows that it is done together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks rice as the object being eaten.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: ませんか uses a polite negative form to make a gentle invitation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q7.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます ＋ ませんか
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q7.kobun.why: いっしょに comes before the verb to add the meaning of doing something together. ごはん is the object used with を, while ませんか comes at the end of the sentence to make a polite invitation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: 食べましょうか focuses more on suggesting that people do something together, while 食べませんか invites the listener to join.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: 食べましょう has a stronger sense of deciding or inviting someone, and is less like a question.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand ませんか as a real negative question, but in this pattern it is usually a polite invitation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: 毎日 shows the time or frequency of the action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the food being eaten.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 食べます is the predicate in the polite present form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q8.kobun.why: The sentence states the topic first, then the frequency, and finally the object of the action. The particle を connects the food with the verb 食べます.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q8.kobun.tip: Do not use に after 毎日 when simply talking about regular frequency.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q9.kobun.vi: My house is far from the station.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the speaker’s house as the topic for comparison or description.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the point used as the basis for judging the distance.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: とおいです is the adjective predicate い in the polite form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q9.kobun.why: The topic is my house, while 駅から serves as the reference point for determining the distance. The adjective とおい directly acts as the predicate and takes です to create a polite tone.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with まで, it means “as far as the station”, emphasizing the endpoint of the distance.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: 駅に usually indicates a direction or destination, so it is not suitable for expressing a reference point for measuring distance in this sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t5-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に instead of から when saying “far from a certain place”.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vi: Let’s take a picture together here.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the people who perform the action together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the action takes place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being photographed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: ましょう is attached to the ます form of a verb to invite or suggest doing something together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q1.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます ＋ ましょう
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q1.kobun.why: みんなで states who joins, ここで states where the action happens, and を marks the object of とる. ましょう comes at the end to create an invitation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence becomes a gentler invitation: shall we take a picture together?
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q1.kobun.tip: Do not use に to indicate the place where the action takes place; in this case, you must use で.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vi: Today was a very enjoyable day.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes today the topic being evaluated.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies the following adjective and shows a high degree.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: たのしい comes before a noun to modify 一日.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: でした acts as a polite past noun predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q10.kobun.why: とても increases the degree of the adjective, while the adjective comes before 一日 to form a noun phrase. でした concludes the statement and looks back on a day that has passed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If です is used, the sentence describes the present or gives a general opinion instead of looking back on a finished day.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If the adjective is changed to the past form, the nuance emphasizes that the day itself was enjoyable.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q10.kobun.tip: An adjective ending in い can come directly before a noun; do not add な between たのしい and １日.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vi: I ended up losing to my older brother in the game.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person the speaker lost to in the game.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the context or activity in which the loss happened.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the verb まける with しまう to create a pattern expressing something that happened accidentally or was completed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: しまいました expresses that something has been completed, often with a feeling of regret or against one’s wishes.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q11.kobun.why: The person who was beaten is used with に, the context of the game is used with で, and the verb is connected in the て form with しまう. This structure makes it clear that the loss was fully completed and that the speaker feels some regret.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes completion or regret, so it fits the unwanted feeling in the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with てみる, the meaning becomes trying to do something, without the meaning of accidentally losing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with the person who was lost to, but the object in まける usually goes with に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q11.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ しまう／しまいます／しまった／しまいました
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q12.kobun.vi: When winter comes, I want to travel.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the time when something happens.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: なったら is the た form of なる connected to ら, creating the condition “when”.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the purpose or destination of 行きたい.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きたい expresses the speaker’s desire.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q12.kobun.why: The time frame comes first, followed by the condition なったら. The verb 行く changes to 行きたい to express the desire to travel.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with とき, the sentence only says “in winter” and does not emphasize a condition as なったら does.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake に in ふゆに for “to arrive,” but here it marks a point in time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject that has the characteristic of being cold.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective つめたい acts as the predicate and describes how the wind feels.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q13.kobun.why: The noun serving as the subject comes before が, while the adjective comes at the end of the sentence to state the subject’s characteristic.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use 寒いです, the sentence usually talks about the weather or a person’s feeling of cold, rather than directly describing cold wind.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q13.kobun.tip: Do not use おおきい to say that the wind is cold; the suitable adjective here is つめたい.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vi: Even if I am opposed, I will still study abroad.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q14.kobun.sk: passive Vて + も + Nを + Vします
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: されても combines the passive form with ても to create the concessive meaning “even if...”.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb します is the main predicate and states the action that will still be carried out.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q14.kobun.why: The clause containing ても comes first to state the obstacle, while the following clause describes the action that is still carried out despite it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: ても emphasizes the contrast between being opposed and still studying abroad.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: のに often expresses surprise or regret, so its meaning is not simply a concessive condition.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily leave out も after て, but only ても creates the meaning “even if... still...”.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q14.kobun.cn: Vて・Aくて・Aなで・Nで + も
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vi: I looked at the map and then went to that store.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the map as the object of 見る.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects the action of looking with the following action of going.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction of movement to the store.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: ました shows that the action happened in polite speech.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q2.kobun.why: を is attached to the object being looked at, て connects two actions in sequence, and へ shows the direction of movement. The main action comes last and is changed to the polite past form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, it would mean looking at the map while going, emphasizing that the two actions happen at the same time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q2.kobun.tip: て in this sentence connects two actions that happen one after another; it does not necessarily express a command.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q2.kobun.cn: Vて + V; Vて + ください; Vて + います
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vi: The train is not running because of an accident.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the cause that makes the train stop operating.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the train as the subject in the state of not running.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ていません indicates a state that is not continuing or is not happening now.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q3.kobun.why: じこで states the cause, 電車が is the affected subject, and うごいていません describes the current state of not operating.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence would only say that the train does not run as an event or decision, without emphasizing its current state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q3.kobun.tip: For a direct cause that makes an event happen or not happen, use で after a noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vi: I will rest for a while because I have a headache.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the body part that is in a painful state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason clause with the act of resting in the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: ちょっと modifies the degree or duration of the rest.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 休みます is the main action and is in the polite form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q4.kobun.why: The clause あたまがいたいので comes first to state the reason, while the main action 休みます comes last. が is often used when talking about symptoms in a body part.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with から, the reason is almost unchanged, but the expression is more direct and subjective.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q4.kobun.tip: When talking about pain in a body part, Vietnamese learners may easily use は; in this basic pattern, が is more natural.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vi: I was warned not to run because it was dangerous.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: ので connects the reason in the warning with the request not to run.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: ないで connects the negative form of the verb with ください to create a request not to do something.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the entire quoted statement.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: されました is the polite past passive form and shows that the speaker received the warning from someone else.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q5.kobun.why: The spoken content is placed inside quotation marks and ends with と. The passive verb then describes the speaker being warned. ないでください is a request not to perform an action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence would have a stronger rule or prohibition-like tone and would no longer be a direct warning.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, it would mean that the speaker warned someone else instead of being warned.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse the direction of the passive form; されました here shows that the speaker is the person who received the warning.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので; Vないで + ください; 「～」と + V被動
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vi: When school ends, let’s meet at the station.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of ending.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: たら connects the conditional clause with the action in the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the meeting takes place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: ましょう expresses an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q6.kobun.why: The conditional clause comes first, followed by the place and the suggested action. が makes it clear that the school is the subject of ending, while で indicates the meeting place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with と, the sentence would suggest that the result naturally occurs whenever the condition happens, which is less suitable for an invitation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with なら, the sentence would have a hypothetical tone based on information already stated or known.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse で with に, but で only indicates the place where an action takes place, while に usually indicates a place where something exists or a destination.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q6.kobun.cn: Vた形・Aい・Aな+だった・N+だった + ら
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vi: Sorry, but Wednesday is not convenient for me.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: が gently connects the apology with the information the speaker wants to give.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents Wednesday as the topic or time being discussed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject being described as convenient or inconvenient.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: わるいです is the adjective predicate and describes an inconvenient situation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q7.kobun.why: The sentence first sets Wednesday as the scope, then describes the condition of つごう. The pattern NはNがAい describes a characteristic or condition of the noun mentioned first.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning changes to being unable to arrange or fit the schedule.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If わるい is changed to いい, the meaning becomes “Wednesday is convenient.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q7.kobun.tip: Do not translate つごうがわるい mechanically as “bad”; in the context of making an appointment, this phrase means “inconvenient.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vi: I will go home early today.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets today as the time reference for the action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: はやく modifies the action of going home and shows that the person will go home early.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: かえります is the main predicate in the polite present or future form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q8.kobun.why: The time reference comes at the beginning of the sentence, and the adverb はやく comes before the verb to modify the action. は limits the content to today.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence becomes “must go home early,” adding a meaning of obligation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the sentence expresses a wish to go home early instead of simply giving information.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q8.kobun.tip: When an い-ending adjective functions as an adverb, い changes to く, as in はやい → はやく.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the tennis activity the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: から shows the time when the activity begins.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: はじまります is the predicate showing that a match or playing session begins.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q9.kobun.why: The activity is introduced as the topic, followed by the starting point and then the verb. から identifies the starting point in time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used, the sentence only indicates that the event takes place at nine o’clock, without emphasizing the starting point.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If まで is used, the sentence shows a limit up to nine o’clock, not a start from nine o’clock.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t6-q9.kobun.tip: For a starting point in time, use から; do not use で as a replacement in this structure.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vi: Please tell me the meaning of this word.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects このことば to the noun that follows and identifies the meaning as belonging to this word.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object being explained.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: おしえて is the て form and connects the verb to the request ください.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes at the end to make a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q1.kobun.why: The phrase このことばの modifies いみ, and then いみを is the object of おしえる. The て form combines with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern asks whether the listener can help, so it is softer than a direct request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q1.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before ください; change the verb to the て form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q10.kobun.vi: I have gained weight recently, so I want to lose weight.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause to the result in the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: たいです is attached to the verb stem to express the speaker’s wish.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q10.kobun.why: さいきん comes at the beginning to state the time. The clause with ので comes first to give the reason, and then たいです expresses the speaker’s wish.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If only Vてしまう is used without たいです, the sentence emphasizes completion or regret rather than a wish.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse たいです with a way to express another person’s wish, while this pattern is mainly used for the speaker’s own wish.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q10.kobun.cn: Vて + しまう; V普通形・Aい・Aな + な・N + な + ので; Vます-stem + たいです
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q11.kobun.vi: I can hear a healthy child’s voice.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 子ども to the following noun to show possession or belonging.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: An な-ending adjective needs な when it comes before a noun to modify that noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the sound that is heard, which is the subject of 聞こえます.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: 聞こえます describes a sound that naturally reaches the listener’s ears.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q11.kobun.why: 子どもの and げんきな both modify こえ, forming the phrase “a healthy child’s voice.” こえが is the sound that is heard, while 聞こえます is the main predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is changed to 元気な子どものこえ, the meaning becomes “the voice of a healthy child,” with 元気な directly modifying 子ども.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If 聞こえます is replaced with 聞きます, the sentence has the active meaning “listen,” and the listener usually needs to be the subject.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget な after an な-ending adjective when the adjective comes before a noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: 少し modifies いたい to soften the degree of pain.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the body part that is in a painful state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: いたい is an adjective describing pain in a body part.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q12.kobun.why: 少し comes before an adjective to show degree. When describing symptoms, the body part goes with が, and the adjective comes at the end to state the condition.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If 頭を痛めています is used, the meaning usually involves struggling with or worrying about a problem, not simply having a headache.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を because of Vietnamese habits, but in the pattern “a body part hurts,” Japanese usually uses が.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q13.kobun.vi: Please go straight along this road.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the route or space through which the movement takes place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: まっすぐ modifies the action すすんで and shows how the movement is carried out.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: Vてください is used to give a polite request or instruction.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q13.kobun.why: この道を states the route to follow, while まっすぐ shows how to go. The verb in the て form combines with ください to make a polite instruction.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used, the sentence sounds unnatural when saying to go along a route; を is more suitable for showing the way.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If 進みます is used, the sentence only states “I will go straight” and is no longer a request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate を as “the affected object,” but with movement verbs, を can also indicate the road or place passed through.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q14.kobun.vi: The teacher’s explanation is very easy to understand.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 先生 with せつめい to show that the explanation belongs to or was given by the teacher.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes せつめい the topic that is described at the end of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: わかりやすい is a compound adjective describing how easy it is to carry out the action of understanding.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q14.kobun.why: 先生の modifies せつめい to identify whose explanation it is. This noun phrase becomes the topic with は, and then わかりやすい states the characteristic of the explanation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If わかりやすい is replaced with わかりにくい, the meaning changes to “difficult to understand.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If よくわかります is used, the sentence emphasizes that the listener understands clearly, instead of describing the explanation itself as easy to understand.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may connect やすい directly to the dictionary-form verb, but they must use the verb stem without ます.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the person who asks the question.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the person who is asked.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: しました is the polite past form of します.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q2.kobun.why: The person asking the question goes with が, the person being asked goes with に, and the question action comes at the end of the sentence. The form しました shows that the action happened in the past.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If 聞きました is used, the meaning is broader: it can mean asked or heard, depending on the context.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q2.kobun.tip: With 質問する, the person being asked usually goes with に, not を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vi: I will explain what we will do from now on.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: これから refers to a point in time or a period beginning in the present.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause すること turns an action into a noun, while を marks the object being explained.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: します is the main predicate and describes the act of explaining.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q3.kobun.why: これから sets the time context, while することを forms a noun phrase meaning what will be done. This phrase is the object of せつめいします.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 説明します is used directly without することを, the sentence only says “explain” and does not clearly state that the content is something that will be done.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q3.kobun.tip: When turning a verb into “what to do,” use V辞書形＋こと, not the past form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vi: I am interested in Vietnamese culture.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ベトナム to the noun that follows and modifies the object of interest.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the object that the speaker is interested in.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: あります describes the existence of 興味, creating the meaning “be interested.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q4.kobun.why: ベトナムの comes before a noun to specify the type of culture. The object phrase goes with に, and then きょうみがあります serves as the main predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Using this instead makes the sentence more formal, close to “have an interest in.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after the object, but the pattern きょうみがあります uses に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vi: My older sister can speak both Japanese and English.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q5.kobun.sk: Nは ＋ Nも ＋ Nも ＋ potential V
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies あね as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: も replaces を and marks Japanese as a language that she can speak.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: も adds English to the same group as 日本語, creating the structure “both A and B.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 話せます is the potential form of 話します and expresses the ability to speak.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q5.kobun.why: Both languages are marked with も to show that they are included together. 話せます is the predicate and shows the subject’s ability.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with や, the sentence gives Japanese and English as examples and does not say that there are only two languages.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use をも in this pattern; も directly replaces を after a noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q6.kobun.vi: We will carry out construction work in March.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the time when the action takes place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 工事 as the action being carried out.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: します is the predicate and combines with 工事 to express carrying out construction work.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q6.kobun.why: The time expression comes before the action and goes with に. 工事をします is a verb phrase in which 工事 is the noun serving as the object of します.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 3月で is not suitable for indicating a time; で usually indicates a place or means.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q6.kobun.tip: Do not confuse 工事をします with 工事があります: this sentence emphasizes carrying out the construction work.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q7.kobun.vi: I will announce that the customer has arrived.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks おきゃくさん as the subject of the action 来た.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: こと nominalizes clause 来た, while を marks the whole event as the content being announced.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: しらせます is the predicate and takes the announcement content through を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q7.kobun.why: Clause おきゃくさんが来た is turned into an event by こと. This event is the object of しらせます, so it goes with を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If こと is replaced with と, the sentence sounds more like directly conveying information or a report.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q7.kobun.tip: こと in this pattern does not mean “thing” on its own; it nominalizes the whole clause before it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q7.kobun.cn: V普通形 ＋ ことを ＋ Vます
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q8.kobun.vi: I escorted the customer to the station.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the person being escorted or taken somewhere.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: まで indicates the endpoint of the journey.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: おくりました is the polite past form of おくります.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q8.kobun.why: The person being escorted is the object with を, while the station is the endpoint and therefore goes with まで. おくりました ends the sentence and shows that the action happened in the past.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used, the sentence only emphasizes the destination; まで emphasizes the route or the limit “as far as the station.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q8.kobun.tip: まで here does not mean “even”; it only limits the place where the customer was escorted.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q9.kobun.vi: Because I was very sleepy, I fell asleep as soon as I closed my eyes.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: とても modifies adjective ねむかった to show a high degree.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause to the result that follows; adjective い changes to its past form ねむかった before ので.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the eyes as the body part affected by the action of closing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: ら attaches to the past form to create a condition or time when the result occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: すぐに modifies the action of sleeping and shows that it happened immediately afterward.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: て connects ねる with しまいました to create a sequence of actions and a sense of completion.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: てしまいました expresses a completed action with an unintended or regretful feeling.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q9.kobun.why: ので gives the cause first, then たら connects closing the eyes with the result that happens immediately afterward. てしまいました emphasizes that falling asleep was fully completed, almost unintentionally.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 目をとじると is used, the sentence focuses on a natural result or general rule and does not emphasize the situation that has just occurred.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If used after closing the eyes, the sentence only states the time sequence and loses the “as soon as” feeling of たら.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use から instead of ので without realizing that ので sounds softer and more objective when giving a reason.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t7-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な・の ＋ ので; Vた ＋ ら; Vて ＋ しまう
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q1.kobun.vi: I am interested in Japanese films.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes わたし the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 日本 with えいが to modify it and show that the film belongs to Japan.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the object toward which the interest is directed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks きょうみ as something that exists in the speaker.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: あります functions as the predicate and expresses the existence of the interest.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q1.kobun.why: わたしは states who has the interested state. 日本のえいがに is the object of interest, while きょうみがあります uses an existence structure to say “be interested.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 日本のえいがが好きです, meaning “like Japanese films,” the sentence is simpler and does not emphasize concern or interest.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If 関心があります is used, the tone is more formal and focuses more on interest in a field or issue.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after the object, but 興味があります usually uses に to indicate what they are interested in.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q1.kobun.cn: N に ＋ 興味がある
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q10.kobun.vi: Thanks to you, I am gradually getting used to my new job.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q10.kobun.sk: Cause phrase ＋ Aい ＋ N に ＋ Vて＋くる
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: This fixed phrase states a positive cause that leads to the result in the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective い comes before a noun to modify it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the object that the speaker is gradually getting used to.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: なれて is the て form of なれる; くる shows that the state of becoming accustomed has continued up to the present.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q10.kobun.why: The job is the object of なれる, so に is used. The form なれてきました combines the て form with くる to express a developing change from the past to the present.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If なれました is used, the sentence only says that the speaker has become used to it and does not emphasize the gradual process.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: なれていきます directs the change toward the future, while なれてきました directs the result toward the present.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit に after a noun, but なれる usually goes with an object marked by に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q10.tokens.0.m: thanks to your kindness; thanks to that
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q11.kobun.vi: The family next door is arguing very loudly.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects となり with かぞく to modify “family.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject performing the action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: 大きな comes before a noun and directly modifies it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the manner or means of performing the action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: けんかしています is a noun combined with する in the ている form, expressing an action in progress.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q11.kobun.why: かぞくが is the subject, while こえで shows how they are arguing. ています places the action in progress at the time of speaking.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with けんかしました, the sentence only says that they argued and does not show that they are still arguing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: 大きい声で also means “in a loud voice,” but 大きな comes directly before the noun in a different fixed pattern.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q11.kobun.tip: Do not translate で as “at”; in this sentence, で indicates the manner of producing the sound.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q11.tokens.8.n: verb する in the て form
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q12.kobun.vi: I have a habit of waking up at 6 o’clock every morning.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q12.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Frequency ＋ Time に ＋ V辞書形 ＋ N が ＋ あります
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic discussed in the whole sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: A frequency phrase comes directly before the action and does not need に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the specific time when the action occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: A dictionary-form verb comes before a noun to modify しゅうかん.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the habit as existing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: あります expresses the existence of the habit.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q12.kobun.why: おきる modifies しゅうかん, so it comes directly before the noun and stays in the dictionary form. An exact time uses に, while the frequency phrase まいあさ does not need a particle.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, it means that waking up at 6 o’clock sometimes happens, not that it is a regular habit.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: This expression only states the action or schedule of waking up at 6 o’clock; it does not state the noun “habit.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place に after まいあさ, but words such as まいあさ usually do not go with に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q13.kobun.vi: Everyone discussed it and then gave flowers to the teacher.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the group of people who perform the action together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: そうだんして is the て form of a noun combined with する, used to connect the earlier action with the later action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the receiver of the gift.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the thing being given.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: プレゼントしました is the polite past form of プレゼントする.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q13.kobun.why: The そうだんして clause describes the earlier action and is connected with the て form. In the giving action, the receiver takes に, while the gift takes を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the before-and-after order is emphasized more clearly, and the sentence has the meaning “after discussing it.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: へ can also indicate the direction of giving, but it emphasizes the direction toward the receiver rather than the receiver’s direct role.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily reverse に and を; remember that the receiver uses に, while the thing being given uses を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q14.kobun.vi: What will you give to celebrate your friends’ wedding?
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects this noun with the following noun and creates a possessive or relational meaning.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects けっこん with おいわい and states the content of the congratulations.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the occasion or purpose of giving the gift.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the thing being given.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: あげますか creates a polite question about the act of giving.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q14.kobun.why: The two phrases の modify the gift-giving occasion in turn. に indicates the purpose or occasion, while を marks the gift before the verb あげます.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with おいわいとして, the tone emphasizes giving the item as a congratulatory gift.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit に after おいわい, but に is necessary here to indicate the occasion or purpose of giving.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q15.kobun.vi: Who will you invite to the wedding?
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place or event that the invited person will attend.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the person affected by the action of inviting.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: しょうたいしますか is a polite interrogative predicate about inviting.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q15.kobun.why: The event is stated first with に, the invited person comes before を, and then the verb しょうたいします appears. This order makes it clear who is invited to which event.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If へ is used instead of に, the sentence emphasizes direction toward the wedding rather than the event being attended.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for the invited person, but the invited person must go with を in the structure だれをしょうたいする.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q16.kobun.vi: The child was very happy after receiving their favorite sweets.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the child is the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the food that was received; すきな modifies おかし.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the action of receiving with the happy state in the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: ～ていました describes a state or action continuing in the past.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q16.kobun.why: The topic 子どもは is placed at the beginning of the sentence. The receiving action uses the form て to connect with the happy state that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If もらったあとで is used, the sentence emphasizes the time order after receiving rather than a natural continuation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate て simply as “and,” but here it connects a cause or earlier action with the happy state that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q17.kobun.vi: I want to score 80 points or more on the next test.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: つぎの directly modifies テスト.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the setting or range in which the score is achieved.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: The score phrase is the object of とる, while いじょう states the minimum level.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: ～たいです expresses the speaker’s desire.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q17.kobun.why: つぎの modifies テスト, で gives the setting, and the score comes before とる. The form ～たいです turns the action of achieving a score into a desire.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If とれます is used, the sentence talks about the ability to achieve 80 points or more, not a desire.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand とりたい as “want to take,” but in the context of scores, とる means to achieve a score.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q18.kobun.vi: Because the school is far away, I try to leave home as early as possible every morning.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the clause stating the reason.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason with the result stated in the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: The time phrase is placed before the main action to show when it is repeated.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: なるべく modifies はやく and shows the degree of effort.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: The adverbial form はやく modifies 出ます.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q18.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the place one leaves, not the object of 出ます.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q18.kobun.ch.6.n: 出ます is the main predicate and indicates the action of leaving home.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q18.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first and is connected with ので. The adverbs of time, degree, and manner successively modify the action of leaving home at the end of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used, the reason has a more direct and subjective tone than ので.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily treat うちを as an object, but with 出る, を usually indicates a place or starting point.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the initial number to which another amount is added.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the number added in the calculation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: たすと connects the calculation with the necessary result in the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the result or state reached after the change.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: なります is the predicate showing the result of the calculation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q19.kobun.why: に identifies the base number, and に after 100 shows the result. The dictionary form + と expresses the natural, necessary result of doing the calculation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If たせば is used, the sentence has a clearer hypothetical condition instead of a direct result rule.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use と after 59 to indicate addition, but this structure uses に for the initial number and を for the number added.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし with the noun しゅみ to show possession.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes しゅみ the topic explained at the end of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks しょうせつ as the object of the action 読む.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb 読む combines with こと to turn the action into a noun, making it the content of the hobby.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: です ends a noun sentence and creates a polite expression.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q2.kobun.why: The sentence places the topic しゅみ before は, then states the specific content with a verb phrase nominalized using こと. The verb 読む comes before こと in the dictionary form because the action is discussed as a concept.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the sentence emphasizes the feeling of liking to read novels rather than defining the hobby as reading.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used, the meaning remains similar, but the focus shifts to reading as an activity趣味.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget こと after a verb when they want to turn the whole action into a noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q2.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + ことだ/です
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q20.kobun.vi: I listened to a lecture by a famous teacher.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects the possessor with the noun it modifies.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the content that was heard.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 聞く takes the polite past form 聞きました.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q20.kobun.why: The phrase ゆうめいな modifies 先生, while 先生の modifies こうぎ. こうぎを is the direct object of 聞きました.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the meaning becomes that the teacher listened to the lecture.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse の with が; の here indicates a “of” relationship and does not mark the subject.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q21.kobun.vi: Because I overslept, I arrived late for class.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: The form て connects a cause or an earlier action to the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the point or event toward which the late arrival is directed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q21.kobun.why: あさねぼうして states the cause first, and then ちこくしました states the result. に is connected to the event of arriving late, namely class.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: ので also states a cause, but it gives a clearer explanation than て.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate て as “and” in every situation, but here it means “because.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q3.kobun.vi: I am working part-time at a nearby shop.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks わたし as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects ちかく with 店, creating a modifying phrase for the shop.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the part-time work takes place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks アルバイト as the content of the work performed with しています.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: しています is the ている form of する, showing that the work is continuing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q3.kobun.why: The place 店で comes before the work and the main verb. The pattern ています describes ongoing part-time work or a current state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is replaced with に, に usually marks a place of existence or a destination, so it is not suitable for marking where the work takes place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with あります, the sentence only says that part-time work exists; it does not say that the speaker is doing it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に instead of で when talking about the place where an action takes place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q4.kobun.vi: My country is trading with Japan.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の expresses possession between わたし and 国.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes 国 the topic described in the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: と indicates the partner participating in the trading activity.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the content of the activity that goes with the verb しています.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: しています describes trading that is in progress or being maintained.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q4.kobun.why: In this structure, 日本と states the participating party, while ぼうえきを states the activity being carried out. The particle と is suitable for nouns that indicate a partner in a relationship or shared activity.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is replaced with に, 日本 is easily understood as the target or place affected, so the meaning of a trading partner is no longer clear.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If と is replaced with から, the meaning changes to originating from Japan or receiving goods from Japan.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit と or use に, although と here means “as a partner.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q4.kobun.cn: N と ＋ N を ＋ する
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q5.kobun.vi: Mr. Kim is listening carefully to the teacher's words.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks キムさん as the topic of the listening action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 先生 with 話 to indicate words belonging to or spoken by the teacher.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks 話 as the object being heard.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective な changes into the adverb form まじめに to modify 聞いています.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: 聞いています uses the ている form to express that the listening action is continuing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q5.kobun.why: 話を is the direct object of 聞く, while まじめに shows how the action is performed. The ている form is placed at the end to show that the listening is taking place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If まじめな is used, it must come before a noun to modify a person or thing; it cannot directly modify 聞く.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with よく, the nuance changes from listening seriously to listening carefully or often.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use まじめな before a verb; before a verb, the adjective な must change to まじめに.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q5.kobun.cn: Aな ＋ に; Vて ＋ いる／います
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q6.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I went to a beauty salon to get my hair cut.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q6.kobun.sk: 時点 ＋ N を ＋ Vます-removeます ＋ に ＋ N へ ＋ Vました
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: きのう states the time of the entire action and comes at the beginning of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks かみ as the object being cut.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: きりに is the form with ます removed from きります, combined with に to show purpose.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: へ indicates the direction toward the place where the purpose is carried out.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: 行きました is the polite past form of 行く and serves as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q6.kobun.cn: Vます形 remove ます ＋ に ＋ 行く／来る／帰る
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q6.kobun.why: The phrase きりに expresses the purpose of going, while びよういんへ is the destination. The purpose verb comes before に with ます removed, followed by the verb 行きました as the main predicate.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with きるために, the purpose remains the same, but the expression is more formal and emphasizes the purpose more strongly.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If びよういんで is used, the sentence emphasizes the place where the haircut takes place, not the direction of travel.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily conjugate きりますに; before に indicates purpose, ます must be changed to きりに.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks なかがわさん as the topic being described.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: おとなしい is the adjective い placed before 人 to modify that person.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: 人です creates a noun predicate and ends the sentence in a polite way.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q7.kobun.why: The adjective おとなしい comes directly before 人 to describe the type of person being discussed. The phrase 人です serves as the predicate, and です connects the characteristic to the topic politely.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with おとなしくて, the sentence is incomplete because the て form is usually used to connect to another clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If one says おとなしいです, the sentence directly describes Mr. Nakagawa as quiet, without using the noun 人 for classification.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place 人 before the adjective; in Japanese, the adjective comes before the noun it modifies.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q8.kobun.vi: There is an interesting TV program being broadcast tonight.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q8.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Aい ＋ N の ＋ N が ＋ ありますよ
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: A time expression; the particle に is not needed in this expression.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects this phrase to ほうそう and shows that the program is being broadcast.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the thing being stated as existing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: あります expresses the existence of an event; よ is used to inform the listener.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q8.kobun.why: The sentence moves from the time, to the program's feature, and then to the event being announced. The particle の connects the modifying noun to the main noun, while が marks the content that exists.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence emphasizes that the program will be broadcast, rather than announcing that there is a broadcast.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate every time expression as に, but こんや usually comes directly before the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q9.kobun.vi: Because I cannot meet my friend, I am very sad.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person whom the speaker wants to meet.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: 会えない is the negative potential form of 会う; て connects the cause to the emotion in the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective い combines with です to create a polite expression.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q9.kobun.why: The object of meeting goes with に. The clause 会えなくて gives the reason, and then the adjective さびしい expresses the feeling caused by that reason.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 会わなくて, it means not meeting because one does not do it, without emphasizing that meeting is impossible.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: ので also gives a reason, but its tone explains the reason more softly and clearly than て.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t8-q9.kobun.tip: Do not mistake 会えない for “not meet,” because it is the negative potential form: “cannot meet.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q1.kobun.vi: On rainy days, I was very sorry because I could not play soccer.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes rainy days the topic and setting of the whole sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the activity that is said to be impossible.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: できなくて is the て form of できない, connecting the reason to the feeling in the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: でした politely expresses regret about a past situation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q1.kobun.why: 雨の日は sets the scene, and サッカーが is the object of the impossible activity. できなくて connects the reason with the feeling ざんねんでした.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: ので also gives a reason, but its tone explains it more directly and clearly.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with できる, but ability usually goes with が: サッカーができる.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q1.kobun.cn: Vない → Vなくて; Aな ＋ でした
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes this type of milk the topic.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: へんな is an な adjective modifying あじ; the comma remains as in the given sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks taste as a sensation that appears in the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: あじがする is a pattern that expresses having or sensing a certain taste.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q10.kobun.why: The topic is introduced with は, and then へんな modifies あじ. The pattern あじがする uses する to express the sensation of taste instead of using a verb for eating or drinking.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence directly states that it is a strange taste, with less emphasis on the sensation being noticed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with あじ, but the pattern for expressing having a taste is あじがする.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q11.kobun.vi: Dinner is ready, so let's eat.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q11.kobun.sk: N の ＋ N が ＋ Vます・ past ＋ から、＋ Vましょう
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects this noun to したく to modify the preparation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of the state できました.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: から connects the reason to the main clause; できました is the polite past form of できる.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: ましょう attaches to the masu stem to express an invitation or suggestion.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q11.kobun.why: ばんごはんの modifies したく, and then したくが becomes the subject of できました. The clause with から comes first to give the reason, and then ましょう gives an invitation to do it together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing から with ので still means “because...,” but the tone is softer and more objective.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use から as a preposition before a noun, but in this sentence it comes after a whole clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ＋から
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q12.kobun.vi: Let's reserve the restaurant we will go to tomorrow.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: あした indicates the time of the action 行く.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: A verb in the dictionary form comes before a noun to modify レストラン.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects レストラン with the noun よやく, creating the phrase “restaurant reservation.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object of the verb しましょう.
