default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: しましょう is the inviting form of する, used to suggest making a reservation together.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q12.kobun.why: あした adds the time to 行く. The phrase あした行く comes before レストラン to identify the restaurant we will go to tomorrow; then よやくをしましょう expresses the suggested action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: This phrase means the restaurant that the speaker will go to tomorrow, not a restaurant that was visited tomorrow.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If あしたの is used, it only says “tomorrow's restaurant” and does not clearly state the action of going.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put 行く after the noun, but a modifying clause in Japanese must come before the noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q13.kobun.vi: Because I will drink coffee, please boil some water for me.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the drink as the object of 飲みます.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason to the request that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks おゆ as the object that needs to be boiled.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: ください creates a polite request; the verb before ください is in the て form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q13.kobun.why: コーヒーを飲みますから gives a practical purpose as the basis for the request. おゆを is the object of boiling, while てください places the polite request at the end of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: Using ので instead of から makes the reason softer and less direct.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: Using ましょう would make it a suggestion to boil it together, not a request for the listener to do it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q13.kobun.tip: Do not use the masu form immediately before ください; change the verb to the て form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q13.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ ください; V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ＋から
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q14.kobun.vi: A: A hamburger and coffee, please. B: Certainly, I understand.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: コーヒー is the second item in the order.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: お願いします is placed at the end to turn the list of items into a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: かしこまりました is the respectful reply a staff member gives when accepting a request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q14.kobun.why: と connects two nouns in the list of ordered items. おねがいします comes after the list to express a request; the server replies respectfully.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: ください can also be used to request an item, but おねがいします is more polite and more suitable for ordering food.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: わかりました only means “understood” in an ordinary way and is less formal than かしこまりました.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate と as “with,” but here と is used to list items.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q15.kobun.vi: I am looking for an apartment with rent of 50,000 yen or less.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q15.kobun.sk: N が ＋ Quantity 以下の ＋ N を ＋ Vて ＋ います
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the factor used as the price-limit condition.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: いかの modifies アパート and limits the rent to no more than the amount stated earlier.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the apartment as the object being searched for.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: さがして connects the main verb with います to create the progressive form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: います after the て form shows that the action is in progress.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q15.kobun.cn: Quantity ＋ 以下の ＋ N; Vて ＋ いる
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q15.kobun.why: やちんが gives the rent criterion, while ５万円以下のアパート is the noun phrase serving as the object of さがす. さがして います shows that the search is still continuing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: 未満の means under 50,000 yen, excluding exactly 50,000 yen; 以下の may include 50,000 yen.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: 以内の emphasizes the whole range not exceeding 50,000 yen. It has a similar meaning but is often used for limits on range or time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand 以下 as absolutely “lower than,” but it usually includes the exact limit.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q16.kobun.vi: Because the window had broken, I asked someone to repair it for me.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the window as the subject in the state of being broken.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause; てしまった emphasizes that the event was completed and often carries a sense of regret.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: なおして in the て form connects with もらいました to show that someone receives help.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: Vて＋もらう expresses that the speaker receives help from another person.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q16.kobun.why: まどが is the subject of the breaking, while ので connects that event with the result of dealing with it. The phrase なおしてもらいました shows that the speaker received help with the repair.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: から also states a cause, but it is more direct and conversational than ので.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: なおしました means repairing it oneself. It does not show that someone else repaired it for the speaker, as なおしてもらいました does.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q16.kobun.vs.2.d: なおしてくれました emphasizes that another person willingly did something helpful for the speaker.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistake てしまう for simply “finished doing,” but in this sentence it also suggests that the event was unwanted.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q16.tokens.5.m: ask someone to do; have something done
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q16.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ しまう; V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な＋ので; Vて ＋ もらう
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q17.kobun.vi: Because today is my birthday, I will decorate the table with flowers.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks today as the time topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: なので connects the cause with the result and means “because it is a birthday.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に shows where an object is placed or decorated.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the object being decorated.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q17.kobun.why: The sentence gives the time and reason first, and then states the action. に shows where the flowers are placed, while を marks the object being decorated.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If なので is replaced with だから, the tone becomes more casual and direct.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use に for the decorated object and forget that the object must be used with を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q18.kobun.vi: I hung a calendar on the classroom wall.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects noun きょうしつ with noun かべ to show the wall belonging to the classroom.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に shows where the calendar is hung.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object being hung.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: The polite past form ました shows that the action was completed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q18.kobun.why: The phrase の modifies かべ, forming “classroom wall.” A location uses に, while the affected object uses を.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used instead of に, the sentence focuses on the place where the action happens, not the fixed place where something is hung.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse に and で; for a place where an object is placed or hung, use に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q19.kobun.vi: Because it is dark here at night, it is scary.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the place being described.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: よる modifies くらい and limits the time of the dark state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: くらい is an adjective predicate, while ですから connects the cause with the result that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q19.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ＋から; the corresponding polite form can use ですから
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q19.kobun.why: The sentence places the cause before the result in the order “because …, so …”. よる modifies くらい, while から turns the preceding clause into a reason.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used, the reason sounds softer and more objective than から.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate から as “so”; in this sentence, から comes after the reason, and the result comes after it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q2.kobun.vi: If I did something bad, my father scolded me harshly.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the action performed in the conditional clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects a condition with the result that usually follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: In a passive sentence, に identifies the person who performs the action affecting the subject.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: きびしく is an adverbial form that modifies the scolding action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: しかられました is the polite past passive form of しかる.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q2.kobun.why: すると states the condition, while the following clause states the result. Because the passive voice is used, the person doing the scolding takes に, while the person being scolded is understood as the affected subject.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: たら expresses a more specific condition and does not necessarily mean that the result always occurs.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use 父を, but in a passive sentence, the person performing the action must use に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q2.kobun.cn: Vる ＋ と; Vる → Vられる
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q20.kobun.vi: The train arrived at the station a little while ago.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject performing the action of arriving at the station.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: さっき modifies the action and shows that it happened recently.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に shows where the train arrives.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: つきました is the polite past form of the verb meaning to arrive.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q20.kobun.why: The subject 電車 uses が, and the destination 駅 uses に. さっき comes before the verb phrase to add the time.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If 駅で is used, the station becomes the place where the action occurs rather than the destination.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use で with “arrive at the station,” but verbs of arrival usually use に.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q21.kobun.vi: This seat is empty. Would you like to sit down?
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: ここの modifies せき and identifies the seat or place belonging to this location.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the seat as being in an empty state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: あいています describes a state of being open or empty, and から connects the reason with the suggestion.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: Vませんか is used to make an invitation or suggestion politely.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q21.kobun.why: The sentence first gives the empty seat as the basis, then uses ませんか to invite the listener to sit. が marks the object that is in an empty state.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If すわりましょうか is used, the speaker makes a clearer proposal to sit together or take the action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand ませんか as a simple negative question, but here it is a polite invitation.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q21.kobun.cn: Vて形＋いる＋から; Vます-stem＋ませんか
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q3.kobun.vi: I received change from the employee, but it was 20 yen short.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: に identifies the person who gives the change to the speaker.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the change as what is received.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: が connects two clauses with contrasting meanings.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: This phrase is the subject described as being short in 足りませんでした.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: 足りませんでした describes an amount of money that was insufficient in the past.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q3.kobun.cn: Nが + V; Vました + が + following clause
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q3.kobun.why: もらいました describes receiving money, and then が changes to an unexpected result. ２０円 is the amount of money that was missing, so it is used as the subject with 足りませんでした.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: しかし also connects contrasting ideas, but it usually starts a new sentence and is more formal than が.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand 足りません as “not have,” but 足りる means “be enough,” so 足りません means “be insufficient.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q4.kobun.vi: Please choose your favorite color from these.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: で limits the range used for comparison or selection.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: いちばん modifies すきな and shows the highest degree.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: すきな modifies いろ, while を marks the chosen color.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects the verb えらぶ with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: ください at the end of the sentence completes the request pattern Vてください.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q4.kobun.why: この中で identifies the range of choices, and いちばんすきな shows the highest degree. えらんでください is a polite request pattern in which the verb must be in the て form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern asks whether the listener can choose it for the speaker. It sounds softer and has the feeling of asking a favor.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use いちばんすきのいろ with な, but the adjective must connect directly to the noun with すきないろ.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q4.kobun.cn: Aな + N; Vて + ください
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q5.kobun.vi: That shirt looks nice. It suits you very well.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The noun is made the topic by a pause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に marks the person or object that the item suits; ています describes a state that continues.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q5.kobun.why: The first sentence comments on the shirt, and the next sentence describes the state of the shirt suiting the person wearing it. にあう uses に to indicate the person or object that the item suits.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced in this sentence, the meaning becomes “it seems that it will suit,” without confirming that it suits the person now.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with にあう, but the correct pattern is Nに似合う.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q6.kobun.vi: I put on a hat and tried looking at myself in the mirror.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the item being worn on the head.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects the action of putting on the hat with the next action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で indicates the means or place where the action of looking is performed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: 見てみる means trying the action of looking; ました describes an action that happened.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q6.kobun.why: The two actions are connected in order by the て form. かがみで shows that the mirror is the means of observing, while Vてみる adds the meaning of trying.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 見てみました is used instead, it only means “looked,” without emphasizing trying.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate で as “at,” but in this sentence で indicates the means of observing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q7.kobun.vi: The bread sold at this store is very soft.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the bread is sold.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb clause comes before the noun パン to modify that noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は makes パン the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q7.kobun.why: The clause うっている comes before パン to identify which bread is meant. After stating the topic with は, the sentence ends with the adjective やわらかい to describe the bread.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 売った is used, it refers only to bread that was sold in the past and does not emphasize that the store is selling it now.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place the modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese places the clause before the noun.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q8.kobun.vi: No matter how much I scold him, my son does not eat vegetables.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: いくら adds the degree of the scolding action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The ても form connects a concessive clause with a result that does not change.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は presents my son as the subject discussed in the main clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the food that my son does not eat.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The polite negative form 食べません describes an action that does not happen.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q8.kobun.why: The clause しかっても is placed first to state a concessive condition. は limits the subject to むすこ, while を marks vegetables as the object of 食べる.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with しかったら, the meaning becomes “if I scold him,” and it no longer has the meaning “even if I scold him, the result stays the same.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand ても as “if,” but in this sentence it means “even if...still.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q8.tokens.0.m: usually filled with いくら: no matter how much...
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q8.kobun.cn: Vて・Aいくて・Aなで・Nで + も
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q9.kobun.vi: Because I am full, I cannot finish eating.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of the state of being full.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: なので connects the cause with the result; なので follows the adjective な in the な form.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: の turns 食べる into a noun meaning the act of eating, while は makes that act the topic.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q9.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first and is connected with なので. The phrase 食べるのは turns the action of eating into a noun and makes it the topic, which is then described as むり.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If のは is replaced with ことは, the basic meaning is similar, but the tone is more general and formal.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit な before ので after the adjective な, but they must say いっぱいなので.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t9-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q9.kobun.vi: I will practice as hard as I can.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase acts as an adverb and modifies the action of practicing.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The present polite verb form describes an action that will be carried out.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q9.kobun.why: The phrase showing degree comes before the verb and modifies how the action is performed. The verb れんしゅうします is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t12-q9.kobun.tip: いっしょうけんめい should not be translated as a proper noun; in this sentence, it functions as an adverb showing degree.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q4.kobun.vi: Check once more to make sure there are no mistakes, then submit it.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The form て connects with いない to create a state of having no mistakes.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: いないか creates an indirect question clause about whether there are mistakes.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてから expresses checking first and then carrying out the next action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: 出して is the form て used to connect a verb with ください and make a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: ください is placed after the form て to ask the listener to carry out an action.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q4.kobun.why: The clause まちがっていないか states what needs to be checked. てから clearly shows the order: check first, then submit; てください changes the final action into a polite request.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with たあとで, the meaning is still “after doing it,” but it emphasizes that the earlier action has been completed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence becomes a request not to do something, which is opposite to the intended request to submit the work.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate てから as “because,” but in this sentence it only shows the order of events.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q4.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ から; Vて ＋ ください; Vている ＋ か
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the first sound of the word 見学 and has no independent grammatical role.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: This is the final sound; the two parts combine to form one complete vocabulary word.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q7.kobun.why: けんがく is a Japanese compound word of Chinese origin, commonly used for a visit intended for learning or practical observation. Since the question asks about vocabulary, there is no sentence structure or particle to analyze.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t38-q7.kobun.tip: 見学 should not be separated into two independent grammatical words; けん and がく are only the two sound components of one word.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q2.kobun.vi: After being scolded by my teacher in front of everyone, I felt very embarrassed.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the scolding took place.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person who performed the action in the passive sentence.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: しかられて is the form て of the passive verb, connecting the scolding event with the emotion that follows.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: とても modifies an adjective and shows a strong degree of emotion.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: This is the past form of the い-ending adjective and serves as the main predicate expressing the speaker's emotion.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: です is placed at the end of the sentence to create a polite tone; with a past adjective, use はずかしかったです.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q2.kobun.why: The phrase showing the place and the person who performed the action comes before the passive verb. The form て connects a cause or an earlier event with the emotional result stated in the following clause.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with しかられたら, the meaning changes to “if I am scolded,” expressing a condition instead of an event that has already happened.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with しかられたので, the cause-and-effect relationship is stated more clearly, meaning “because I was scolded.”
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に as an ordinary subject; in this passive sentence, に indicates the person who caused the action, while the person affected is omitted.
default.q.pointmoji_n4-t40-q2.kobun.cn: V受身て、＋ とても ＋ Aいかったです
